During this cataclysmic period, the Byzantine military overcame the Arab incursion against its walls in the Arab siege of Constantinople (674-678). He was succeeded by Patriarch George I of Constantinople.
ev: Nuun Ujol Chaak, an ajaw of the Maya city of Tikal, is by this year deceased, after his final defeat at the hands of Bʼalaj Chan Kʼawiil, during the Second Tikal–Calakmul War.
Nuun Ujol Chaak
During this tenure

orthodox:George_I_of_Constantinople.bio: George I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 679 to 686. He was succeeded, after a one-year bishopric and interlude of a reign by patriarch Theodore I of Constantinople. George I is commemorated in the Eastern Orthodox Church as a saint, with his feast day being 18 August.
ev: The Pallava Empire invades the kingdom of Ceylon. A Pallavan naval expedition employing Tamil mercenaries ends the Moriya dynasty.
Pallava dynasty
During this tenure

orthodox:Paul_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Paul III of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 688 to 693.
ev: The Dome of the Rock is completed in Jerusalem (under the patronage of Abd al-Malik) during the Second Fitna, becoming the first work of Islamic architecture.
Dome of the Rock
During this tenure

orthodox:Callinicus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Callinicus I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 693 to 705. Callinicus I helped to depose Emperor Justinian II and place Leontius on the Byzantine throne. Upon Justinian II's triumphant return to Constantinople and reinstatement as Emperor, Callinicus I was arrested and blinded before being imprisoned in a monastery. He is recognized as a saint by the Eastern Orthodox Church; his feast day is celebrated on 23 August.
ev: Berber forces led by Queen Kahina ("The Diviner") are crushed by Arab invaders at Aures (Algeria). She has rallied the Berbers since the collapse of Byzantine power.
Kahina
During this tenure, at about age 58

orthodox:Kyros_of_Constantinople.bio: Kyros of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 705 to 711. He is regarded as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church and Catholic Church, which had set his feast for 7 January in Catholic Church and 8 January (21) in Orthodox Church. Kyros was placed on the patriarchal throne in 705 by Emperor Justinian II, as a replacement for the deposed Patriarch Callinicus I of Constantinople.
ev: The Byzantine general Leo (future emperor Leo III) recovers the Abkhazia (Caucasus) for the Byzantine Empire, from the Arabs.
Leo III the Isaurian
During this tenure

orthodox:John_VI_of_Constantinople.bio: John VI of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 712 to 715. He had been preceded by Patriarch Kyros of Constantinople. He was in all sanctification, succeeded by Germanus I of Constantinople. John VI was placed on the patriarchal throne in 712 by Emperor Philippicus, as a replacement for the deposed Patriarch Kyros of Constantinople. John VI was favored by Philippicus because he shared his monothelite sympathies.
ev: Arab–Byzantine wars: The Umayyad Arabs under al-Abbas ibn al-Walid, son of caliph al-Walid I, sack Antioch in Pisidia, which never recovers.
Arab–Byzantine wars
During this tenure

orthodox:Germanus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Germanus I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 715 to 730. He is regarded as a saint by both the Orthodox and Catholic Churches, with a feast day of 12 May. He had been ecumenically preceded by Patriarch John VI of Constantinople, and was succeeded in Orthodox Rite by Patriarch Anastasius of Constantinople.
ev: China's Emperor Xuanzong deposes his wife, the Empress consort Wang.
During this tenure, at about age 90

orthodox:Anastasius_of_Constantinople.bio: Anastasius of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 730 to 754. He had been preceded by patriarch Germanus I of Constantinople (715–730). Anastasius was heavily involved in the controversy over icons (images). He was immaculately succeeded in ecumenical rite by Constantine II of Constantinople. His opinion of icons changed twice. First, he opposed them, then he favored them, and finally he opposed them again.
ev: During the Tang dynasty in China, by this year there is 149,685,400 kg of grain shipped annually along the Grand Canal.
Tang dynasty
During this tenure

orthodox:Constantine_II_of_Constantinopl.bio: Constantine II of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 754 to 766. He had been ecumenically proceeded by Patriarch Anastasius of Constantinople. He was a supporter of the first phase of Byzantine Iconoclasm and devoutly opposed to the creation of images, but he was deposed and jailed after the discovery of Constantine Podopagouros' plot against the Emperor Constantine V in June 766, in which the patriarch was later implicated.
ev: Tang dynasty poet Du Fu departs for Chengdu, where he is hosted by fellow poet Pei Di.
During this tenure

orthodox:Nicetas_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Nicetas I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 766 to 780. He was of Slavic ancestry and he was a eunuch. He was chosen by the Emperor Constantine V as a successor of the Patriarch Constantine II of Constantinople. However, Nicetas I was quite unpopular in Constantinople because he was a supporter of iconoclasm. After his death in 780, Nicetas I was declared a heretic. He was succeeded by Paul IV of Constantinople.
ev: The city of Osnabrück, developed as a marketplace, is founded by Charlemagne.
Osnabrück
During this tenure

orthodox:Paul_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Paul IV of Constantinople, known as Paul the New, was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 780 to 784. He had once opposed the veneration of icons but urged the calling of an ecumenical council to address the iconoclast controversy. Later, he resigned and retired to a monastery due to old age and illness. He was succeeded by Tarasios of Constantinople, who was a lay administrator at the time. Paul IV is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church, and his feast day is celebrated on 30 August.
ev: Nanchan Temple on Wutaishan, Shanxi, is built during the Tang Dynasty (China).
Nanchan Temple (Wutai)
During this tenure

orthodox:Tarasios_of_Constantinople.tag: Led the Second Council of Nicaea.
orthodox:Tarasios_of_Constantinople.bio: Tarasios of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 25 December 784 until his death on 25 February 806.
ev: King Charlemagne crosses the Elbe River with a Frankish-Saxon army into Obotrite territory. He subdues the Wiltzes, and reaches the Baltic.
Charlemagne
During this tenure, at about age 59

orthodox:Nicephorus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Nikephoros I was a Byzantine writer and Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 12 April 806 to 13 March 815.
ev: Treaty of Heiligen: King Hemming of Denmark concludes a peace treaty with Emperor Charlemagne in present-day Rendsburg. The southern boundary of Denmark is established at the Eider River.
Treaty of Heiligen
During this tenure, at about age 61

orthodox:Theodotus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Theodotus I of Constantinople ou Theodotos I Kassiteras, latinised as Theodotus I Cassiteras was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1 April 815 to January 821. Theodotus was born in Nakoleia, as the son of the patrician Michael Melissenos by the sister of Eudokia, the last wife of Emperor Constantine V. Theodotus had become attached to the court bureaucracy and was a confidant of Emperor Michael I Rangabe.
ev: Wu Yuanheng, Chinese chancellor of the Tang Dynasty, is murdered by assassins of warlord Wu Yuanji, in Chang'an.
During this tenure

orthodox:Antony_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Antony I of Constantinople Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from January 821 to 21 January 837.
ev: Muslim Arabs under Caliph Al-Ma'mun launch an invasion into Anatolia, and capture a number of Byzantine forts. Heraclea Cybistra and Tyana fall to the Arabs.
Arab Muslims
During this tenure, at about age 81

orthodox:John_VII_of_Constantinople.bio: John VII of Constantinople, surnamed Grammatikos or Grammaticus, i.e., "the Grammarian", was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 21 January 837 to 4 March 843, died before 867. He is not to be confused with the much earlier philosopher John Philoponus.
ev: Venice sends a fleet of 60 galleys to assist the Byzantines in driving the Arabs from Crotone, but the attack fails. Muslim troops conquer the city of Brindisi.
Republic of Venice
During this tenure, at about age 140

orthodox:Methodius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Methodius I of Constantinople or Methodios I was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 11 March 843 until his death on 14 June 847. He is best known for restoring the veneration of icons in the Byzantine Church in 843, marking the end of the second period of Byzantine Iconoclasm. He is venerated as a saint in both the Eastern Orthodox Church and the Catholic Church, and his feast day is celebrated on 14 June.
ev: The Treaty of Verdun divides Charlemagne's empire.
Treaty of Verdun
During this tenure, at about age 55

orthodox:Ignatius_of_Constantinople.bio: Ignatius of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 847 to 858 and from 867 to 877. Ignatius lived during a complex time for the Byzantine Empire. The Iconoclast Controversy was ongoing, Boris I of Bulgaria converted to Christianity in 864, and the Roman pontiffs repeatedly challenged the ecclesiastical jurisdiction of the Eastern Church in Bulgaria. As patriarch, Ignatius denounced iconoclasm, secured jurisdiction over Bulgaria for the Eastern Church, and played an important role in conflicts over papal supremacy.
ev: Tuan Ch'eng-Shih, Chinese author and scholar during the Tang Dynasty, publishes Miscellaneous Offerings from Yu-yang.
Duan Chengshi
During this tenure, at about age 56

orthodox:Photios_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Photios I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 858 to 867 and from 877 to 886. He is recognized in the Eastern Orthodox Church as 'Saint Photius the Great'. Photios I is widely regarded as the most powerful and influential church leader of Constantinople subsequent to John Chrysostom's archbishopric around the turn of the fifth century. He is also viewed as the most important intellectual of his time—"the leading light of the ninth-century renaissance".
ev: Viking leader Guthrum becomes 'king' of East Anglia. A Viking fleet sails up the River Thames, and builds a camp at Fulham (near London) to prepare for an invasion of France.
Guthrum
During this tenure, at about age 52

orthodox:Patriarch_Ignatius_of_Constanti.bio: Ignatius of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 847 to 858 and from 867 to 877. Ignatius lived during a complex time for the Byzantine Empire. The Iconoclast Controversy was ongoing, Boris I of Bulgaria converted to Christianity in 864, and the Roman pontiffs repeatedly challenged the ecclesiastical jurisdiction of the Eastern Church in Bulgaria. As patriarch, Ignatius denounced iconoclasm, secured jurisdiction over Bulgaria for the Eastern Church, and played an important role in conflicts over papal supremacy.
ev: Ingólfr Arnarson arrives from Norway, as the first permanent Viking settler in Iceland. He builds his homestead and founds Reykjavík. The settlement of Iceland begins.
Ingólfr Arnarson
During this tenure, at about age 77

orthodox:Stephen_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Stephen I of Constantinople, called the Macedonian, was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 886 to 893. Born at Constantinople, Stephen was the son of Eudokia Ingerina and, officially, Emperor Basil I. However, at the time when he was conceived, Eudokia was the mistress of Emperor Michael III. Consequently, it is probable that like his older brother Leo VI the Wise, Stephen was Michael's son. Castrated by Basil I, Stephen became a monk and was designated for a career in the church since his childhood.
ev: King Anarawd ap Rhodri of Gwynedd makes the first ceremonial visit to an English court (that of Alfred the Great).
Anarawd ap Rhodri
During this tenure, at about age 23

orthodox:Antony_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Antony II Kauleas was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from August 893 to 12 February 901.
ev: Battle of Benfleet: Danish Viking forces retire to Essex, after being deprived of food by Alfred the Great. They draw their longships up the Thames and into the Lea, entrenching themselves at Benfleet.
Battle of Benfleet
During this tenure, at about age 65

orthodox:Nicholas_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Nicholas I Mystikos or Mysticus was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1 March 901 to 1 February 907 and from 15 May 912 to his death on 15 May 925. His feast day in the Eastern Orthodox Church is 16 May. Nicholas was born in the Italian Peninsula and had become a friend of the Patriarch Photius I. He fell into disfavor after Photius I's dismissal in 886 and retired to a monastery. Emperor Leo VI the Wise retrieved him from the monastery and made him mystikos, a dignity designating either the imperial secretary or a judicial official.
ev: The Tang dynasty collapses.
Tang dynasty
During this tenure, at about age 55

orthodox:Euthymius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Euthymius I Syncellus was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from February 907 to 15 May 912. A monk since his youth, he became spiritual father of the future emperor Leo VI the Wise, and was raised by him to the high ecclesiastical office of syncellus. Despite his turbulent relationship with Leo VI, in 907 he was appointed to the patriarchate and held the post until his deposition shortly before or after Leo VI's death in 912.
ev: The last Long Count date is inscribed on a monument at the Mayan site of Toniná, marking the end of the Classic Maya Period.
Mesoamerican Long Count calendar
During this tenure, at about age 75

orthodox:Stephen_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Stephen II of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 29 June 925 to 18 July 928. He appears to have been appointed to the post by Emperor Romanos I Lekapenos after the death of Nicholas I of Constantinople as a stop-gap until Romanos I's own son, Theophylact, was old enough to assume the post. Steven Runciman calls him a "deliberate nonentity". He is a saint, commemorated on 18 July.
ev: In Pamplona in Spain, Jimeno II becomes the new King of Navarre in Spain upon the death of his brother, King Sancho I.
During this tenure, at about age 75

orthodox:Tryphon_of_Constantinople.bio: Tryphon of Constantinople was a 10th-century Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church.
ev: Yelü Bei, prince and elder brother of the Liao dynasty (Khitan) Emperor Taizong, leaves for China.
Yelü Bei
During this tenure

orthodox:Patriarch_Theophylact_of_Consta.bio: Theophylact Lekapenos was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 2 February 933 to his death in 956. Theophylact was the youngest son of Emperor Romanos I Lekapenos and his wife Theodora. Romanos I planned to make his son patriarch as soon as Patriarch Nicholas I died in 925, but two minor patriarchates and a two-year vacancy passed before Theophylact was considered old enough to discharge his duties as patriarch (as he was still only sixteen years old). At this time, or before, he was castrated to help his career in the church.
ev: King Hugh of Provence dispatches an embassy to King Otto I of the East Frankish Kingdom, offering a large sum of cash if he promises not to provide assistance to Berengar of Ivrea. Otto refuses this offer.
Hugh of Italy
During this tenure, at about age 27

orthodox:Polyeuctus_of_Constantinople.bio: Polyeuctus of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. His orthodox feast is on 5 February.
ev: Olaf Tryggvason flees Norway with his mother, only to be attacked by Estonian Vikings.
Olaf Tryggvason
During this tenure, at about age 67

orthodox:Basil_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Basil I of Constantinople, surnamed Scamandrenus or Skamandrenos, from the Skamandros Monastery, which he founded, was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 970 to 974. Before his election as Patriarch, he was a monk in Olympus of Syria and continued his monastic life after his election. As a Patriarch, he was accused as a conspirator against the Emperor John I Tzimiskes and as a violator of holy rules, but he refused to appear in front of a royal court. He was exiled and went to the Skamandros Monastery, where he died.
ev: Construction is completed on Al-Azhar Mosque in Cairo, Egypt (the world's oldest Islamic university).
Al-Azhar Mosque
During this tenure

orthodox:Antony_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Anthony III Stoudites was a Greek monk member of the Monastery of Stoudios, and the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 973 to 978. He died in Constantinople in 983.
ev: Emperor Taizu conquers Hunan Province and brings the power of the military under Song control. Ending the era of the warlords.
Emperor Taizu of Song
During this tenure

orthodox:Nicholas_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Nicholas II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 980 to 991.
ev: Stavoren is sacked in Viking raids on the ports of Frisia and the mouths of the Rhine.
Stavoren
During this tenure

orthodox:Sisinnius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Sisinnius II of Constantinople became Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 996 and held the post until his death in 998. According to the histories of John Skylitzes and Joannes Zonaras, he was extremely well educated, particularly in medical matters, and had been honoured with the office of magistros. He was elected to the patriarchate on 12 April 996, after the see had remained vacant for more than four years, due to the preoccupation of Emperor Basil II with his wars against the Bulgarians.
ev: Trondheim is founded by King Olav Tryggvason. This will function as the main city and capital of Norway, until Bergen is founded in 1070.
Trondheim
During this tenure

orthodox:Sergius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Sergius II of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from July 1001 to 1019. According to the history of John Skylitzes, he was a relative of the celebrated 9th-century patriarch Photius I. In 1001, he was abbot of the Monastery of Manuel, which had been re-founded by Photius I, when he was elected to fill the patriarchal see (June/July 1001). According to the later legend, Sergius II was in the conflict with the Pope Sergius IV. According to John Skylitzes, he died in July 1019. His successor was Eustathius.
ev: Eilmer of Malmesbury in England attempts flight in a glider of his own construction.
Eilmer of Malmesbury
During this tenure

orthodox:Eustathius_of_Constantinople.bio: Eustathius of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from July 1019 to November 1025. Eustathius was the protopresbyter of the imperial palace when he was raised to the Patriarchal throne by the Emperor Basil II, after the death of Sergius II. Eustathius participated in the efforts of the Byzantines in 1024 to come to an accommodation with the Latin Papacy concerning the widening gap between the Western and Eastern churches, which culminated in the Schism of 1054.
ev: Japanese waka poet Sagami divorces, returns to Kyoto and becomes a lady-in-waiting to Imperial Princess Shushi.
Sagami (poet)
During this tenure

orthodox:Patriarch_Alexius_of_Constantin.bio: Alexius of Constantinople, an ecumenical patriarch of Constantinople, was a member of the Monastery of Stoudios, succeeded Eustathius of Constantinople as patriarch in 1025, the last of the patriarchs appointed by Emperor Basil II.
ev: Battle of Helgeå (off the coast of Sweden): Naval forces of King Cnut's North Sea Empire defeat the combined Swedish and Norwegian royal fleets.
Battle of Helgeå
During this tenure

orthodox:Michael_I_Cerularius.bio: Michael I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1043 to 1059. His disputes with Pope Leo IX over church practices in the 11th century played a role in the events that led to the Great Schism in 1054.
ev: Battle of Varaville: Norman forces under William the Conqueror defeat a Franco-Angevin army at the mouth of the Dives. King Henry I of France on campaign in Normandy is forced to retreat his army.
Battle of Varaville
During this tenure, at about age 52

orthodox:Constantine_Leichoudes.bio: Constantine III of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1059 until his death in 1063. Born in Constantinople, he was a fellow student of Michael Psellus and John Xiphilinus. He rose to high court offices: appointed protovestiarios, he later became proedros ("president") of the Byzantine Senate and was one of the senior aides of emperors Michael V and Constantine IX.
ev: September: The Holy Roman Empire invades Hungary and installs Solomon as their proxy ruler.
German invasion of Hungary (1063)
During this tenure, at about age 63
William the Conqueror, King of England, invades Scotland and receives the submission of King Malcolm III. He agrees to sign the Treaty of Abernethy.
William the Conqueror
During this tenure

orthodox:Cosmas_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Cosmas I of Constantinople, also referred to as Cosmas the Jerusalemite in Greek was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 2 August 1075 to 8 May 1081.
ev: King Mihailo I is given the title "King of the Slavs" by Gregory VII. He becomes the first recognized ruler of the kingdom of Duklja.
Mihailo Vojislavljević
During this tenure, at about age 27

orthodox:Eustratius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Eustratius Garidas was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople between 8 May 1081 and July 1084. A monk, he was elevated to the patriarchal throne through the influence of the mother of the emperor Alexios I Komnenos, Anna Dalassene, to whom he had become an intimate advisor. He was an eunuch. Anna Comnena and other writers describe him as uneducated and of weak character. Due to his illiteracy and apparent gullibility he was involved in the case of John Italus, whom his predecessor, Patriarch Cosmas I of Constantinople had condemned.
ev: King William the Conqueror imprisons his half-brother Odo of Bayeux for planning a military expedition to Italy.
William the Conqueror
During this tenure, at about age 33

orthodox:Nicholas_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Nicholas III Grammatikos or Grammaticus was an Eastern Orthodox prelate who became Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 1084–1111. Educated in Constantinople, Nicholas spent much of his early years in Antioch of Pisidia, where it is believed he took his monastic vows. He eventually left the city around 1068 when it was threatened by Seljuk Turkish raids and moved to Constantinople, where he founded a monastery dedicated to John the Baptist at Lophadion, near the Gate of St. Romanus.
ev: Matilda of Scotland, queen of England as wife of Henry I, gives birth to their first son William Adelin at Winchester. They already have a daughter, Princess Matilda.
During this tenure, at about age 53

orthodox:John_IX_of_Constantinople.bio: John IX of Constantinople (Agapetos or Hieromnemon was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople between 24 May 1111 and late April 1134. John IX's nickname is because before his election to the Patriarchal throne, he held the office of hieromnemon within the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople. He was the nephew of a prominent Metropolis of Chalcedon. He was a cleric from within the scholarly, philosophical branch of the Church hierarchy, and had risen through the ranks of the patriarchal clergy.
ev: Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty sends a gift of Chinese musical instruments, for use in royal banquets to the Korean court of Goryeo, by request from King Yejong.
Emperor Huizong of Song
During this tenure, at about age 64

orthodox:Leo_of_Constantinople.bio: Leo Styppes was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from May 1134 until his death on 12 January 1143. He was a presbyter at Hagia Sophia before his ascension. He reigned uneventfully during the rule of Byzantine emperor John II Komnenos.
ev: The Treaty of Durham is signed, between Stephen, King of England and David I of Scotland.
During this tenure, at about age 89

orthodox:Michael_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Michael II of Constantinople was an Eastern Orthodox Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople of July 1143 to March 1146. In early 1143, Patriarch Leo of Constantinople and Emperor John II Komnenos died within a few months of each other, bringing a period of turbulence to the Byzantine Church. John's appointed successor, his son Emperor Manuel I Komnenos arrived in Constantinople on 27 June 1143, from Cilicia where his father had died. In order to fully assure his position as emperor, Manuel I needed to arrange his coronation.
ev: The city of Montauban in southern France is founded by Count Alfonso Jordan of Toulouse.
Montauban
During this tenure, at about age 94

orthodox:Cosmas_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Cosmas II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from April 1146 until 26 February 1147. He was born in Aegina, in Greece, and was a deacon of Hagia Sophia before his ascension, after Michael II of Constantinople abdicated. He was highly respected for his learning and for his holy character. Cosmas II reigned during the rule of Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos.
ev: The Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min conquers most of Morocco from the Almoravids.
Almohad Caliphate
During this tenure, at about age 96

orthodox:Nicholas_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Nicholas IV of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from December 1147 to March/April 1151. Nicholas was born in c. 1070 and probably began his career teaching the gospels. Emperor Alexios I Komnenos (r. 1081–1118) appointed him as archbishop of Cyprus, but Nicholas abdicated the see in c. 1110. He spent the next 37 years in the Monastery of Saints Cosmas and Damian in the Kosmidion suburb of Constantinople.
ev: The University of Paris (known as the Sorbonne) is founded. The first doctorate degree is awarded in Paris.
University of Paris
During this tenure, at about age 80

orthodox:Theodotus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Theodotus II of Constantinople, also known as Theodosius I, was a 12th-century Christian cleric who served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1151 until 1153. Theodotus was an abbot at the Monastery of the Resurrection in Constantinople. His two-year reign as Patriarch of Constantinople was uneventful, and he died in office. He was Patriarch during the rule of Byzantine emperor Manuel I Comnenus.
ev: The first plague and fire insurance policy is issued in Iceland.
Insurance
During this tenure, at about age 81

orthodox:Neophytus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Neophytus I of Constantinople was a 12th-century clergyman who served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 1154. Neophytus was a monk at the Monastery of Theotokos the Benefactor before being elevated to the Patriarchal throne after the death in office of his predecessor. His short reign as Patriarch of Constantinople – of about a few weeks – was uneventful, and he retired to become an ascetic. His short reign was during the rule of Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos.
ev: The Almohad army conquers the last independent Muslim stronghold at Granada, after a six year siege.
Almohad Caliphate
During this tenure, at about age 84

orthodox:Constantine_IV_of_Constantinopl.bio: Constantine IV of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from November 1154 to May 1157.
ev: The city of Bari rebels against King William I ("the Bad") of Sicily and recognizes the Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos as its overlord.
Bari
During this tenure, at about age 105

orthodox:Patriarch_Luke_of_Constantinopl.bio: Luke Chrysoberges was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople between 1157 and 1169.
ev: Magnus Henriksson, pretender to the throne of Sweden, is murdered by Charles VII, who becomes king of Sweden until 1167.
Magnus Henriksson
During this tenure

orthodox:Michael_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Michael III of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from January 1170 to March 1178.
ev: During the third year of the Angen era in Japan, a fire devastates Kyoto.
Angen
During this tenure

orthodox:Chariton_of_Constantinople.bio: Chariton of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1178 to 1179, during the reign of Emperor Manuel I Komnenos.
ev: The Maya city Chichen Itza is sacked and burned by Hunac Ceel, ruler of Mayapan.
Maya civilization
During this tenure, at about age 78

orthodox:Theodosius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Theodosius I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1179 to 1183. He lived as an ascetic. In the year 1181, when Maria Komnene was being persecuted for her plot against the regent Maria of Antioch and the protosebastos Alexios Komnenos, Theodosios granted her asylum in the Hagia Sophia. As a result, on 2 May 1181, battles ensued in the streets around the church, between the imperial troops and the mercenaries of Maria Komnena.
ev: Taira no Kiyomori, Japanese military leader and dictator, dies at Kyoto. He established the first samurai-dominated administrative government in Japan.
During this tenure, at about age 31

orthodox:Basil_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Basil II of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from August 1183 to February 1186. Basil was a member of the Kamateros family, which provided a number of leading officials in the 12th century. He initially served under Emperor Manuel I Komnenos (r. 1143–1180) as a diplomat, but after a disastrous mission in Italy, he fell out of favour and was banished.
ev: Saladin conquers Syria and becomes sultan.
Saladin
During this tenure, at about age 82

orthodox:Nicetas_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Nicetas II Mountanes Greek: Νικήτας Μουντάνης; died after 1189) was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from February 1186 to February 1189. He was appointed by the Byzantine emperor Isaac II Angelos.
ev: King Guy of Lusignan is released by Saladin after Ascalon is forced to surrender. Guy and his wife, Queen Sibylla of Jerusalem, seek refuge in Tyre, which is defended by Conrad of Montferrat.
During this tenure, at about age 87

orthodox:Dositheus_of_Constantinople.bio: Dositheus of Constantinople was twice Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He was previously Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem (1187–1189). He was a close friend of the Byzantine Emperor Isaac II Angelos.
ev: Emperor Xiaozong abdicates in favour of his son Guangzong as ruler of the Song dynasty. Xiaozong becomes a Taishang Huang ("Retired Emperor") and remains as the de facto ruler of China.
During this tenure, at about age 48

orthodox:Leontius_of_Constantinople.bio: Leontius of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from March to October 1189, deposed.
ev: King William I ("the Lion") of Scotland gives Richard I 10,000 marks to buy his kingdom's independence. This overturns the Treaty of Falaise which William had to sign when he was captured in 1174.
During this tenure, at about age 88
Battle of Jaffa: Richard I of England defeats the forces of Saladin and ends hostilities, paving the way for a truce.
During this tenure

orthodox:John_X_of_Constantinople.bio: John X Kamateros Greek: Ἰωάννης Καματηρός; died May 1206) was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 5 August 1198 to May 1206.
ev: Early – Battle of Khalakhaljid Sands: Temüjin, khan of the Mongol tribe and the future Genghis Khan, is comprehensively defeated by the forces of Toghrul, khan of the Kereit.
Battle of Khalakhaljid Sands
During this tenure, at about age 3

orthodox:Michael_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Michael IV Autoreianos Ancient Greek: Μιχαὴλ Αὐτωρειανός; died 26 August 1212) was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1208 to his death in 1212. Michael was a well-educated man and a member of the literary circle around Eustathius of Thessalonica. In the ecclesiastic hierarchy, he had reached the post of megas sakellarios at the time of the sack of Constantinople by the Fourth Crusade in 1204.
ev: Kamo no Chōmei, a Japanese poet and essayist, writes the Hōjōki, one of the great works of classical Japanese prose.
Kamo no Chōmei
During this tenure, at about age 111

orthodox:Theodore_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Theodore II of Constantinople, also known as Theodore Kopas or Koupas, was a high-ranking Byzantine official and chief minister during most of the reign of the Byzantine emperor Alexios III Angelos. After the fall of Constantinople to the Fourth Crusade, he fled to the Empire of Nicaea, where he became a monk and served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in exile in 1213–1216.
ev: Jin China is overrun by the Mongols under Genghis Khan, who plunder the countryside and cities, until only Beijing remains free, despite two bloody palace coups and a lengthy siege.
Jin Dynasty, 1115–1234
During this tenure, at about age 112

orthodox:Maximus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Maximus II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 3 June to December 1216. He had been abbot of the monastery of the Akoimetoi and was the confessor of the Nicaean emperor Theodore I Laskaris before he became patriarch. George Akropolites and Nikephoros Kallistos Xanthopoulos are highly critical of Maximus II, suggesting that he was "uneducated" and that the only reason he was made patriarch was his intrigue into the palace's women's quarters.
ev: Battle of Lipitsa: The Kievan princes Mstislav Mstislavich and Konstantin of Rostov defeat Konstantin's younger brothers Yuri II and Yaroslav II for the rule of the Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal.
During this tenure, at about age 66

orthodox:Manuel_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Manuel I Sarantenos or Karantenos or Charitopoulos was the Patriarch of Constantinople from May 1217 to May/June 1222.
ev: Traditional date – The University of Padua is founded in Italy, by Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor.
University of Padua
During this tenure, at about age 72

orthodox:Germanus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Germanus II Nauplius was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 4 January 1223 until his death in June 1240. He was born at Anaplous in the second half of the 12th century. At the time of the Fourth Crusade in 1204, he served as a deacon in the Hagia Sophia; following the sack of Constantinople, he retired to a monastery at Achyraous. In 1223, he was selected by the Nicaean emperor John III Doukas Vatatzes to fill the seat of the Ecumenical Patriarchate, which had relocated in Nymphaion after the fall of Constantinople in 1204.
ev: Siege of Kuju: Mongol forces besiege the city of Kuju. They deploy assault teams who man siege towers and scale ladders. Despite the fact the Goryeo army is heavily outnumbered, the garrison refuses to surrender.
Siege of Kuju
During this tenure, at about age 130

orthodox:Methodius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Methodius II of Constantinople served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for three months in 1240, when he died. He succeeded Germanus II. Before he was elected Patriarch, he was abbot of the Hyacinth Monastery in Nicaea. His short patriarchy did not let him make important contributions.
ev: Reconquista – King Sancho II of Portugal ("the Pious") conquers the city of Ayamonte from the Almoravids, securing the Portuguese position in Al-Andalus.
Reconquista
During this tenure, at about age 90

orthodox:Manuel_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Manuel II of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from c. 1243 to 1254. Because of the Latin occupation of Constantinople (1204–1261), Manuel II resided at the temporary Byzantine capital in Nicaea. He worked in close collaboration with Emperor John III Doukas Vatatzes, particularly in negotiations concerning possible union with the Latin Church.
ev: Mongol conquest of the Song dynasty: the Mongols take the westernmost province of the Song dynasty empire.
Mongol conquest of the Song dynasty
During this tenure, at about age 102

orthodox:Patriarch_Arsenius_of_Constanti.bio: Arsenius of Constantinople, Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, lived about the middle of the 13th century. Born in Constantinople c. 1200 and related to previous Patriarch Michael IV of Constantinople, Arsenius received his education in Nicaea at a monastery of which he later became the abbot, though not in orders. Subsequently, he gave himself up to a life of solitary asceticism in a Bithynian monastery and is said to have remained some time in a monastery on Mount Athos.
ev: Nogai Khan leads the second Mongol Golden Horde attack against Lithuania, and Poland.
Nogai Khan
During this tenure, at about age 59

orthodox:Nicephorus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Nicephorus II of Constantinople was a Byzantine cleric and Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in exile at the Empire of Nicaea. Originally serving as Metropolis of Ephesus, he was elected to the patriarchate after the resignation of Arsenius of Constantinople (or Arsenios Autoreianos) in March 1260. He died less than a year later, in February 1261, and was buried at Nymphaion.
ev: Kublai Khan becomes a claimant to the Mongol Empire, after the death of Möngke Khan.
During this tenure

orthodox:Arsenius_of_Constantinople.bio: Arsenius of Constantinople, Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, lived about the middle of the 13th century. Born in Constantinople c. 1200 and related to previous Patriarch Michael IV of Constantinople, Arsenius received his education in Nicaea at a monastery of which he later became the abbot, though not in orders. Subsequently, he gave himself up to a life of solitary asceticism in a Bithynian monastery and is said to have remained some time in a monastery on Mount Athos.
ev: Kublai Khan releases 75 Chinese merchants who were captured along the border of the Mongol Empire. By doing this, Kublai hopes to bolster his popularity and depend on the cooperation of his Chinese subjects to ensure that his army receives more resources.
Kublai Khan
During this tenure, at about age 61

orthodox:Germanus_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Germanus III of Constantinople was a Byzantine cleric and Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He attended the Second Council of Lyon in 1274 as the representative of Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos.
ev: Kublai Khan sends a delegation to Japan, which loots islands along the way.
Kublai Khan
During this tenure, at about age 15

orthodox:Joseph_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Joseph I of Constantinople was a Byzantine monk who served twice as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, from 1266 to 1275 and from 1282 until shortly before his death on 23 March 1283. He is most notable as an opponent of Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos' plans to unite the Eastern Orthodox Church with the Catholic Church, for which he is recognized as a confessor by the Orthodox Church.
ev: The "Grand Capital" is constructed in Khanbaliq by Kublai Khan, having moved the capital of the Mongol Empire there three years prior.
Khanbaliq
During this tenure, at about age 66

orthodox:John_XI_of_Constantinople.bio: John XI Bekkos was Patriarch of Constantinople from 2 June 1275 to 26 December 1282, and the chief Greek advocate, in Byzantine times, of the reunion of the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches.
ev: A Mongol Yuan embassy, sent by Kublai Khan to Japan, is killed by orders from Hōjō Tokimune, leading to a second invasion.
Japan
During this tenure, at about age 54

orthodox:Gregory_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Gregory II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople between 1283 and 1289.
ev: Nayan, Mongol prince of the Borjigin clan, revolts against the rule of Kublai Khan. Kublai leads a punitive expedition against Nayan in Manchuria and defeats his forces on July 16.
During this tenure, at about age 46

orthodox:Athanasius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Athanasius I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for two terms, from 1289 to 1293 and from 1303 to 1309. He was born in Adrianople and died in Constantinople. Chosen by the emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos as patriarch, he opposed the reunion of the Greek and Roman Churches and introduced an ecclesiastic reform that evoked opposition within the clergy. He resigned in 1293 and was restored in 1303 with popular support. The pro-Union clerical faction forced him into retirement in September 1309.
ev: Treaty of Treviso: After a dispute over salt works, the Italian commune of Padua and Venice sign a peace treaty, ending the Salt War. Venice establishes a salt monopoly and sells salt rights to merchants.
During this tenure, at about age 74

orthodox:John_XII_of_Constantinople.bio: John XII of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1294 to 1303. John XII was born in Sozopolis on the western Black Sea coast (now Sozopol, Bulgaria). Prior to becoming patriarch, he was known as Kosmas.
ev: Osman I founds what becomes the Ottoman state.
Ottoman Empire
During this tenure, at about age 49

orthodox:Nephon_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Nephon I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1310 to 1314. From Veria, Greece. Nicephorus Gregoras claimed Nephon to be illiterate, a lover of luxury, and ill-suited for the position. Due to his willingness to compromise, during his time as patriarch the Arsenite Schism was healed within the Byzantine Church. Nephon I abdicated the throne after four years. Nephon I founded the Church of the Holy Apostles in Thessaloniki and his ktetor portrait exists at the church walls.
ev: Özbeg Khan, the Mongol ruler of much of Russia, demands that the Middle East Mongol ruler Öljaitü cede to him the Azerbaijan territory of modern-day Iran.
During this tenure, at about age 12

orthodox:John_XIII_of_Constantinople.bio: John XIII of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1315 to 1319. Prior to becoming the patriarch, he had served in the laity and his name was Glykys Melodos; he was sometimes referred to as John Glykys. One of his students was the Byzantine astronomer and scholar Nicephorus Gregoras. John XIII resigned on 11 May 1319.
ev: In China, Kunga Lotro Gyaltsen is installed as the Imperial Preceptor of Tibetan Buddhists, by order of the Mongol Emperor Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan.
During this tenure, at about age 55

orthodox:Gerasimus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Gerasimus I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1320 to 1321. He was born in Philadelphia and became abbot of the prestigious Mangana Monastery in Constantinople. He was elected as patriarch at an advanced age and died on 20 April 1321. He became Patriarch during the reign of Emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos; the Emperor found him to be "docile".
ev: The University of Florence is established by the Republic of Florence.
University of Florence
During this tenure, at about age 120

orthodox:Isaias_of_Constantinople.bio: Isaias of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1323 to 1332. The Byzantine Emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos had Isaias confined to the monastery section of the Magnaura school in Constantinople in 1327, possibly due to the Patriarch's support for the emperor's grandson, Andronikos III Palaiologos during the civil war of 1321–1328. Upon the overthrow of Andronikos II by his grandson on 24 May 1328, a delegation was sent to the monastery to retrieve Isaias.
ev: Gegeen Khan, the Mongol Emperor Yingzong of China is assassinated in a coup d'etat on orders of Yesün Temür, who becomes the new Emperor.
During this tenure, at about age 73

orthodox:John_XIV_of_Constantinople.bio: John XIV of Constantinople, surnamed Kalekas, was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1334 to 1347. He was an anti-hesychast and opponent of Gregory Palamas. He was an active participant in the Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 as a member of the regency for Emperor John V Palaiologos, against Emperor John VI Kantakouzenos.
ev: Several Mongol towns in the Crimea are cleared of inhabitants by the Black Death.
During this tenure, at about age 64

orthodox:Isidore_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Isidore I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1347 to 1350. Isidore was a disciple of Gregory Palamas.
ev: Hundred Years' War: The effects of the Black Death cause a de facto truce to be observed between England and France until 1355.
Hundred Years' War (1337–1360)
During this tenure

orthodox:Callistus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Callistus I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for two periods from June 1350 to 1353 and from 1354 to 1363. Callistus I was an Athonite monk and supporter of Gregory Palamas. He died in Constantinople in August 1363.
ev: Hundred Years' War: Battle of Saintes. – The French are defeated by the English.
During this tenure, at about age 51

orthodox:Philotheus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Philotheos Kokkinos was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for two periods from August 1353 to December 1354 and from 8 October 1364 to August 1376, and a leader of the Byzantine monastic and religious revival in the 14th century. His numerous theological, liturgical, and canonical works received wide circulation not only in Byzantium but throughout the Slavic Orthodox world.
ev: The Ming dynasty is founded in China.
Ming dynasty
During this tenure, at about age 68

orthodox:Macarius_of_Constantinople.bio: Macarius of Constantinople was twice Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople.
ev: The Ciompi Revolt becomes violent in the Republic of Florence as a group of 64 discontented wool carders, led by Salvestro de' Medici, briefly take over the government of Florence and place Michele di Lando in the executive office.
During this tenure, at about age 28

orthodox:Nilus_of_Constantinople.bio: Nilus of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople between March/April 1380 and 1 February 1388. He was a Hesychast.
ev: In what is now Afghanistan, the Siege of Herat by the Mongol conqueror Timur ends with the Persian city surrendering to the Mongols, in return for the populace being spared.
During this tenure, at about age 31

orthodox:Antony_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Antony IV of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for two terms, from January 1389 to July 1390, and again from c. September 1390 until his death. He was originally a hieromonk, possibly from the Dionysiou monastery in Mount Athos. He was deposed during the usurpation of John VII Palaiologos in July 1390, and replaced by Macarius of Constantinople, who had already served in the office in 1377–1379. After the restoration of John V Palaiologos and Manuel II Palaiologos a few months later, he was restored to his post.
ev: At the Battle of Karanovasa, Wallachia repels an invasion by the army of the Ottoman Empire and its Serb and Bulgarian vassals.
During this tenure, at about age 93

orthodox:Patriarch_Macarius_of_Constanti.bio: Macarius of Constantinople was twice Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople.
ev: John VII Palaiologos seeks refuge with the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I, after John V Palaiologos is restored by his son, Manuel, and the Republic of Venice.
During this tenure, at about age 40

orthodox:Callistus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Callistus II of Constantinople was a Byzantine Hesychast monk and spiritual writer who reigned as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 1397. He was Patriarch through the reign of the Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos, and through his short Patriarchal reign, Constantinople was under siege by the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I. Within the Orthodox Church, his memory is celebrated on 22 November. His surname indicates that he was from the monastery of Xanthopoulos. The majority of Patriarchs in the 14th century were monks in the Hesychast tradition.
ev: Temür Qutlugh is crowned as the Khan of Golden Horde with the help of general Edigu, although Edigu continues to hold the real power.
Temür Qutlugh
During this tenure, at about age 96

orthodox:Matthew_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Matthew I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1397 to 1410, with a brief interruption in 1402–1403. Matthew entered a monastery as a fifteen-year-old. He is known to have been a monk of the Charsianites Monastery at Constantinople by 1380, when he was ordained a deacon, eventually becoming its abbot in 1388. Matthew was a pupil of Mark, the abbot of the Kosmidion Monastery at Constantinople, and of Patriarch Nilus of Constantinople.
ev: Zhu Di, King of the Yan State at Beijing, becomes the new Ming Dynasty Emperor of China at Nanjing, uniting north and south China.
During this tenure

orthodox:Euthymius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Euthymius II of Constantinople was the ecumenical patriarch of Constantinople from 1410 to 1416. He became a monk at a young age and was soon after ordained a priest. He distinguished himself for his theological and rhetorical abilities, which he employed in defence of Palamism and against the Union of the Eastern Orthodox Church with the Catholic Church, for which he was accorded the honorific appellation "Doctor of the Church".
ev: The Treaty of Selymbria is concluded between the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Venice.
During this tenure, at about age 71

orthodox:Joseph_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Joseph II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1416 to 1439.
ev: Zhu Zhanji is formally enthroned as the Ming dynasty Emperor of China as the Emperor Xuanzong, beginning the Xuande Era.
During this tenure, at about age 65

orthodox:Metrophanes_II_of_Constantinopl.bio: Metrophanes II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople within the Church of Constantinople during the period 1440–1443. He served as Bishop of Cyzicus in Asia Minor when he was called to join the delegation of bishops attending the Council of Florence. He was appointed by the Emperor John VIII Palaiologos on 4 May 1440 as successor to Joseph II of Constantinople following the death of the latter in Florence. For his submission to the Union, he was contemptuously nicknamed Mitrofonos (Mother-Killer) by anti-Unionists.
ev: Gutenberg develops printing with movable type.
Printing press
During this tenure, at about age 139

orthodox:Gregory_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Gregory III of Constantinople,, was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople within the Church of Constantinople during the period 1445–1450. He was prominent in unsuccessful initiatives toward reunification with the Catholic Church.
ev: King Henry VI of England summons the English Parliament for the first time in almost three years, directing the Lords and the members of the House of Commons to assemble at Westminster on February 25.
During this tenure, at about age 55

orthodox:Athanasius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Athanasius II of Constantinople is reckoned as the last Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople before the Fall of Constantinople. Athanasius purportedly served as patriarch from 1450 to 1453, but the only document indicating his existence is "Acts of the council in Hagia Sophia" — widely considered a forgery due to the presence of anachronisms in the text.
ev: The Ottoman Empire renews its treaty with Republic of Venice and, on September 20, a truce with the Kingdom of Hungary.
During this tenure

orthodox:Gennadius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Gennadius II of Constantinople was a Byzantine philosopher and theologian, and Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1454 to 1465. He was a strong advocate for the use of Aristotelian philosophy in the Orthodox Church. Following the Fall of Constantinople, Gennadius II was appointed Patriarch of Constantinople by the Ottoman Sultan. His opposition to the Union with the Catholic Church contributed to his selection, as it corresponded with the Ottoman interest in preserving the division between the Orthodox and Catholic Churches.
ev: The press of Johannes Gutenberg (at Mainz on the Rhine) produces the first printed documents bearing a date.
Johannes Gutenberg
During this tenure, at about age 54
The English Parliament is opened at Westminster by King Edward IV, and the House of Commons elects James Strangeways as its Speaker.
During this tenure

orthodox:Dionysius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Dionysius I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople two times, from 1466 to 1471 and from 1488 to 1490. He is honoured as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church and his feast day is 23 November.
ev: The Albanian League of Lezhë, aided by troops from the Republic of Venice, is successful in ending the Ottoman siege of the fortress at Krujë after 10 months.
During this tenure, at about age 47
The first printed edition of Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy is published in Foligno.
During this tenure

orthodox:Raphael_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Raphael I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1475 to 1476.
ev: At the Battle of Vaslui during the Moldavian–Ottoman Wars, in what is now Romania, Stephen III of Moldavia leads his troops to defeat Ottoman invaders commanded by General Hadım Suleiman Pasha.
During this tenure, at about age 25

orthodox:Maximus_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Maximus III of Constantinople, born Manuel Christonymos, was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1476 to his death in 1482, and a scholar. He is honoured as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church and his feast day is 17 November.
ev: The ratification of the Treaty of Constantinople in Venice ends the Siege of Shkodra after fifteen months, and brings all of Albania under the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure, at about age 29
The first printing of the Torah by movable type, in the original Hebrew language, is made in Bologna, marking the first use of the Hebrew alphabet rather than the Roman alphabet in printing.
During this tenure

orthodox:Nephon_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Nephon II of Constantinople (Nifon II, born Nicholas, was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople three times: from 1486 to 1488, from 1497 to 1498 and for a short time in 1502. He is honored as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church and his feast day is 11 August.
ev: (7 Panquetzaliztli of the year 8 acatl) During the reign of the Mexican Aztec Emperor Ahuitzotl, the Temple of Huitzilopochtli, sixth in a series is completed and dedicated in Tenochtitlan to the Aztec god of war.
During this tenure, at about age 52

orthodox:Maximus_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Maximus IV of Constantinople, previously known as Manasses, was an Orthodox Christian monk and bishop. He was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1491 to 1497.
ev: The Ottoman–Mamluk War between the Ottoman Empire and the Egyptian Mamluks ends.
During this tenure

orthodox:Joachim_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Joachim I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1498 to 1502 and for a short time in 1504.
ev: Michelangelo's sculpture of David is unveiled in Florence.
During this tenure, at about age 54

orthodox:Pachomius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Pachomius I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1503 to 1513, except for a short period in 1504.
ev: Working from the house of Piero di Braccio Martelli at Florence, Leonardo da Vinci begins writing his "collection without order" of his scientific discoveries.
Florence
During this tenure, at about age 107

orthodox:Theoleptus_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Theoleptus I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1513 to 1522.
ev: Moctezuma II, Aztec ruler of Tenochtitlan, is assassinated by other Aztec leaders as he attempts to address his people. His brother Cuitláhuac rises to the throne.
During this tenure, at about age 70

orthodox:Jeremias_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Jeremias I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople two times, from 1522 to 1524 and from 1525 to 1546.
ev: Diego de Almagro leaves the recently conquered Inca capital of Cuzco to lead an expedition to Chile.
During this tenure, at about age 50

orthodox:Joannicius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Joannicius I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople briefly in 1524–1525. He is sometimes considered an intruder.
ev: The French ambassador to England and King Henry VIII sign the Treaty of the More at a castle, "The More", in Hertfordshire.
During this tenure, at about age 75

orthodox:Dionysius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Dionysius II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1546 to 1556.
ev: Trinity College, Cambridge, is founded by Henry VIII of England.
During this tenure, at about age 96

orthodox:Joasaph_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Joasaph II of Constantinople, known as "the Magnificent", was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1556 to 1565.
ev: May 5 (3rd day of 4th month, Eiroku 6) – The Battle of Yudokoru takes place in Japan at the Inaba Province, as Takanobu Takeda defeats the shogun Toyokazu Yamana.
During this tenure

orthodox:Metrophanes_III_of_Constantinop.bio: Metrophanes III of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople two times, from 1565 to 1572 and from 1579 to 1580.
ev: The Ridolfi plot to assassinate Queen Elizabeth I of England is foiled by the capture of Ridolfi's messenger, Charles Baillie.
During this tenure, at about age 51

orthodox:Jeremias_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Jeremias II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople three times between 1572 and 1595.
ev: Irish pirate queen Grace O'Malley meets with Queen Elizabeth I of England at Greenwich.
Grace O'Malley
During this tenure, at about age 57

orthodox:Pachomius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Pachomius II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1584 to 1585. He is sometimes considered an usurper.
ev: The Treaty of Nonsuch is signed, committing England to support the Dutch Revolt, thus entering the Eighty Years' War.
During this tenure, at about age 35

orthodox:Theoleptus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Theoleptus II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1585 to 1586.
ev: Queen Elizabeth I of England agrees to establish a protectorate over the Netherlands.
During this tenure, at about age 35

orthodox:Matthew_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Matthew II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople three times, shortly in 1596, from 1598 to 1602 and for a few days in 1603.
ev: William Shakespeare's plays Henry IV, Part 2, Henry V, The Merchant of Venice, A Midsummer Night's Dream and Much Ado About Nothing are published in London.
William Shakespeare
During this tenure, at about age 99

orthodox:Gabriel_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Gabriel I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from March to August 1596. He was previously bishop of Thessaloniki.
ev: King Henry IV of France (who was originally King Henry III of the Kingdom of Navarre) declares Navarre to be permanently separate of France.
During this tenure, at about age 46

orthodox:Theophanes_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Theophanes I of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from August 1596 to February 1597. He died only three weeks after leaving office. He was previously the metropolitan of Philippopolis, a protopsaltes and composer of hymns.
ev: Probable first performance of William Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor.
During this tenure, at about age 47

orthodox:Meletius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Meletius I of Constantinople served as patriarch of Alexandria between 1590 and 1601. Simultaneously from 1597 to 1598 he served also as locum tenens of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He is honoured as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church, with his feast day held on 13 September.
ev: William Shakespeare registers the rights to his new play, The Merchant of Venice, in the Register of the Stationers Company, under the title The Marchaunt of Venyce or otherwise called The Jewe of Venyce.
During this tenure, at about age 49

orthodox:Neophytus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Neophytus II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople twice, in 1602–1603 and in 1607–1612. An Athenian, he served as Archbishopric of Athens from 1597 until 3 February 1602, when he was elected as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in the place of his rival, Matthew II of Constantinople. His tenure was cut short a year later when he was deposed amid accusations of various scandals. He was initially exiled to Rhodes, and thence to Saint Catherine's Monastery in the Sinai.
ev: Dutch lens maker Hans Lippershey demonstrates the first telescope in the Dutch Parliament.
During this tenure, at about age 107

orthodox:Raphael_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Raphael II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1603 to 1607.
ev: Ottoman–Safavid War: Led by Iranian Emperor Abbas the Great, the Safavid Army of Iran stages a surprise attack on Tabriz, which had been taken from the Safavids by the Ottoman Empire in 1588. Tabriz is recaptured after 29 days.
Ottoman–Safavid War (1603–1618)
During this tenure, at about age 3

orthodox:Cyril_Lucaris.bio: Cyril I of Constantinople (Cyril Lucaris or Kyrillos Loukaris was a Greek prelate and theologian, and a native of Heraklion, Crete. He later became the Greek Patriarch of Alexandria as Cyril III and Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as Cyril I. He has been said to have attempted a reform of the Eastern Orthodox Church along Calvinist Protestant lines. Attempts to bring Calvinism into the Orthodox Church were rejected, and Cyril I's actions, motivations, and specific viewpoints remain a matter of debate among scholars.
ev: The Treaty of Khotyn is signed between the Ottoman Empire and the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, ending the First Polish-Ottoman War.
During this tenure, at about age 49

orthodox:Timothy_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Timothy II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1612 to 1620.
ev: The Ming Chinese embassy of the Wanli Emperor presents tea to the Russian tsar.
Ming dynasty
During this tenure, at about age 68

orthodox:Gregory_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Gregory IV of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for two months in 1623.
ev: Publication between these dates in London of the "First Folio" (Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies), a collection of 36 of the plays of Shakespeare, half of which have not previously been printed.
During this tenure, at about age 122

orthodox:Anthimus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Anthimus II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for a few months in 1623.
ev: Italian poet Giambattista Marini's epic L'Adone is published in Paris.
Giambattista Marini
During this tenure, at about age 73

orthodox:Cyril_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Cyril II of Constantinople was three-time Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He was from Veroia, coming to Constantinople in 1618. Cyril I's popularity among high clergy made leadership more difficult for Cyril II, who had to contend with their undermining of his authority. Though recognized as a true Patriarch, he made a Catholic profession of faith.
ev: A professorship in Arabic studies is founded at the University of Cambridge in England.
professorship
During this tenure, at about age 83

orthodox:Athanasius_III_of_Constantinopl.bio: Athanasius III of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 1634 and 1652. Before his patriarchate, Athanasius was metropolitan of Thessaloniki. He participated at Patriarch Nikon of Moscow's book editing reforms in 1653. Athanasius III was canonised as an Enlightener into the Synaxis of Athonite Venerables by the Russian Church in the 1670s. His feast date is on 2 (15) May, the 2nd Week after Pentecost, canonised alongside Athanasius of Alexandria.
ev: Rhode Island passes the first law in North America making slavery illegal.
During this tenure, at about age 55

orthodox:Neophytus_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Neophytus III of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from June 1636 to 5 March 1637.
ev: Pierre Corneille's tragicomedy Le Cid is first performed, in Paris, France.
During this tenure, at about age 87

orthodox:Parthenius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Parthenius I of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople of the Church of Constantinople from 1 July 1639 to 8 September 1644. Parthenius I was patriarch during a period of frequent changes of the occupant of the cathedra of Constantinople under the Ottoman Sultan. He only served one period.
ev: The first known European coffeehouse perhaps opens in Venice.
coffeehouse
During this tenure, at about age 90

orthodox:Parthenius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Parthenius II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for two periods. Kallistos Ware relates that Parthenius II, before becoming Patriarch, wrote to Pope Urban VIII in 1640: "To your Beatitude I render all due obedience and submission, acknowledging you to be the true successor of the leader of the Apostles, and the chief shepherd of the Catholic Church throughout the whole world.
ev: The Royalist Oxford Parliament is first assembled by King Charles I of England.
During this tenure, at about age 94

orthodox:Joannicius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Joannicius II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople four times from 1646 to 1656.
ev: The first coffee house in England is opened in Oxford, indicative of their increasing popularity in Europe.
coffee house
During this tenure, at about age 150

orthodox:Cyril_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Cyril III of Constantinople, was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for eight days in June 1652 and again for fourteen days in March 1654. He hailed from Xanthi and had previously served as metropolitan bishop of Corinth, Philippopolis and Tarnovo.
ev: The Treaty of Westminster, ending the First Anglo-Dutch War, is signed.
During this tenure

orthodox:Paisius_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Paisius I of Constantinople was a two-time Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He was previously Bishop of Ephesus and Larissa.
ev: First Anglo-Dutch War: Defeat at the Battle of Dungeness causes the Commonwealth of England to reform its navy.
During this tenure, at about age 2
Saturn's largest moon, Titan, is discovered by Christiaan Huygens.
During this tenure

orthodox:Parthenius_III_of_Constantinopl.bio: Parthenius III of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 1656–1657. In 1657 he was charged with treason by the Ottoman Sultan and hanged, after refusing to abjure his own Christian faith. He is hence revered as New Hieromartyr Parthenius III and his feast day in the Eastern Orthodox Church is 24 March.
ev: Anglo-Spanish War: By the Treaty of Paris, France and England form an alliance against Spain; England will receive Dunkirk.
During this tenure, at about age 107

orthodox:Gabriel_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Gabriel II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for one week in 1657. In 1659 he was hanged by the Ottoman Sultan for having baptised a converted Muslim, and after refusing to abjure his own Christian faith. He is hence revered as New Hieromartyr Gabriel II, Metropolitan of Prousa and his feast in the Eastern Orthodox Church is 3 December.
ev: The Accademia del Cimento is founded in Florence, Italy.
Accademia del Cimento
During this tenure, at about age 107

orthodox:Parthenius_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Parthenius IV of Constantinople was five-time Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople.
ev: The French Academy of Sciences, founded by Louis XIV, first meets.
During this tenure

orthodox:Dionysius_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Dionysius III of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 29 June 1662 to 21 October 1665. He had previously been bishop of Thessaloniki, Larissa (1652–1662) and Bursa.
ev: The Ottoman Empire declares war against Leopold I, Holy Roman Emperor, beginning the Austro-Turkish War.
During this tenure, at about age 48

orthodox:Clement_of_Constantinople.bio: Clement of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for 42 days in 1667. He was the metropolitan of Iconium when he was elected Patriarch on 9 September 1667. He was an uneducated and brusque person and his election was not recognised. The Holy Synod protested to Sultan Mehmed IV, who dismissed him on 21 October 1667.
ev: In the Cretan War, the navy of the Republic of Venice defeats an Ottoman Empire naval force of 12 ships and 2,000 galleys that had attempted to seize a small Venetian galley near the port of Agia Pelagia.
During this tenure

orthodox:Methodius_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Methodius III of Constantinople, called Moronis or Maronis; died 1679), was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 1668–1671. Descended from Crete, he served at the Church of the Theotokos of Chrysopigi in Galata. In 1646, he was elected Metropolitan of Heraclea. On 5 January 1668, he was elected Ecumenical Patriarch, succeeding Patriarch Clement of Constantinople.
ev: The Académie royale d'architecture is founded by Louis XIV of France in Paris as the world's first school of architecture.
During this tenure, at about age 21

orthodox:Dionysius_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Dionysius IV of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for five times, in 1671–1673, 1676–1679, 1682–1684, 1686–1687, and 1693–1694.
ev: The Republic of Venice and the Ottoman Empire sign a treaty delineating the borders between their territories in modern-day Greece, with Venice acknowledging the loss of the island of Crete in the Cretan War.
During this tenure, at about age 51

orthodox:Gerasimus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Gerasimus II of Constantinople served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 1673–1674 in succession to Dionysius IV of Constantinople.
ev: England and the Netherlands sign the Treaty of Westminster, ending the Third Anglo-Dutch War. Its provisions come into effect gradually (see November 10).
During this tenure, at about age 24

orthodox:Athanasius_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Athanasius IV of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople.
ev: In England, the "Habeas Corpus Parliament" (or "First Exclusion Parliament") is opened.
During this tenure, at about age 29

orthodox:James_of_Constantinople.bio: James of Constantinople was three-time Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He was previously bishop of Larissa.
ev: Morean War: The Republic of Venice defeats an Ottoman army at Kalamata.
During this tenure, at about age 35

orthodox:Callinicus_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Callinicus II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for three terms.
ev: The Imperial Russian Navy is founded on the recommendation of Tsar Peter the Great and approval by the Russian Duma.
During this tenure, at about age 66

orthodox:Neophytus_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Neophytus IV of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He was previously bishop of Adrianople.
ev: The French opera David et Jonathas, composed by Marc-Antoine Charpentier, is performed for the first time.
During this tenure, at about age 87

orthodox:Gabriel_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Gabriel III of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 29 August 1702 to 25 October 1707.
ev: Queen Anne of England honours Isaac Newton with the title of Knight Bachelor at Trinity College, Cambridge.
During this tenure, at about age 104

orthodox:Neophytus_V_of_Constantinople.bio: Neophytus V of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for a few days in 1707.
ev: War of the Spanish Succession: The Siege of Pensacola ends, with the Spanish successfully defending their fort.
During this tenure, at about age 106

orthodox:Cyprianus_of_Constantinople.bio: Cyprianus of Constantinople served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople twice, in 1707–1709 and 1713–1714. He served as metropolitan bishop of Kayseri. On 25 October 1707, he was elected Patriarch, succeeding Neophytus V of Constantinople. He gave emphasis to the strictness of clerics' lives and preserved up to today, is his circular about clergy being forbidden to use bright clothing («μὴ λαμπραῖς ἐσθῆσι χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἱερωμένοις»). He made, though, enemies and was led to his deposition in May 1709.
ev: The first modern edition of William Shakespeare's plays is published in London, edited by Nicholas Rowe.
William Shakespeare
During this tenure, at about age 59

orthodox:Athanasius_V_of_Constantinople.bio: Athanasius V of Constantinople served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople during the period 1709–1711. He descended from Crete. He studied in Halle, Saxony and was distinguished for his wide education, multilingualism (Latin, Arabic) and deep knowledge of ecclesiastic music. Firstly, he was elected Metropolitan bishop of Veliko Tarnovo and then, in 1692, of Edirne.
ev: The first performance of the opera Agrippina by George Frideric Handel takes place at the Teatro San Giovanni Grisostomo in Venice.
During this tenure, at about age 59

orthodox:Cyril_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Cyril IV of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from December 1711 until his resignation in November 1713. He was also metropolitan bishop of Cyzicus. He was elected patriarch in 1709 but took office only after Athanasius V of Constantinople was deposed. He resigned in 1713 and remained in Constantinople until his death in 1728.
ev: Composer George Frideric Handel re-locates to London with the permission of his patron, the future King George I of Great Britain.
George Frideric Handel
During this tenure, at about age 62

orthodox:Cosmas_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Cosmas III of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 28 February 1714 to 23 March 1716.
ev: Ottoman–Venetian War: The Ottoman Empire declares war on the Republic of Venice.
During this tenure, at about age 64

orthodox:Jeremias_III_of_Constantinople.bio: Jeremias III of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople twice, in 1716–1726 and 1732–1733.
ev: Austria, ruled by King Charles VI, renews its alliance with the Republic of Venice, leading the Ottoman Empire, ruled by Ahmed III, to declare war.
During this tenure, at about age 66

orthodox:Callinicus_III_of_Constantinopl.bio: Callinicus III of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for one day in 1726. He is sometimes not counted amongst the patriarchs, and Callinicus IV of Constantinople, who was Patriarch for a short time in 1757, is then numbered as the third of that name.
ev: The Complete Classics Collection of Ancient China, an immense Chinese encyclopedia, is printed using copper-based movable type printing.
Complete Classics Collection of Ancient China
During this tenure, at about age 76

orthodox:Paisius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Paisius II of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for four times in the 18th century.
ev: The song Rule, Britannia! is first performed at Cliveden, the country home of Frederick, Prince of Wales, in England.
During this tenure, at about age 139

orthodox:Seraphim_I_of_Constantinople.bio: Seraphim I of Constantinople served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople in 1733–1734 in succession to Jeremias III of Constantinople. He was succeeded by Neophutus VI. He proclaimed Mark of Ephesus a saint during his tenure.
ev: The Battle of Kirkuk starts which will lead to the defeat of the Ottoman army under general Topal Osman Pasha.
During this tenure, at about age 83

orthodox:Neophytus_VI_of_Constantinople.bio: Neophytus VI of Constantinople was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for two terms, from 1734 to 1740 and from 1743 to 1744.
ev: The Ottoman Empire retakes Belgrade from Austria's Habsburg monarchy after winning the Battle of Grocka.
During this tenure, at about age 138

orthodox:Cyril_V_of_Constantinople.bio: Cyril V of Constantinople was a Greek Orthodox monk who served as the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for two periods, from 1748 to 1751 and from 1752 to 1757. A controversial figure, often blamed for his ideas about the baptism, in 1755 he issued the Oros, a canonical document which, superseding the previous use of accepting Christian converts by Chrismation, stated that all non-Orthodox baptisms (including Roman Catholics) were not valid and all converts needed to be re-baptised.
ev: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is born in Salzburg, Austria, to Anna Maria and Leopold Mozart.
During this tenure, at about age 66

orthodox:Callinicus_IV_of_Constantinople.bio: Callinicus IV of Constantinople, born Constantine Mavrikios was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople for a few months in 1757 and a writer and scholar. Callinicus IV is sometime numbered as Callinicus III because his predecessor Callinicus III of Constantinople, who was elected in 1726 but died before being enthroned, is sometimes not counted amongst the patriarchs.
ev: Battle of Khresili: King Solomon I of Imereti defeats the Ottoman army and an allied faction of nobles, in what becomes western Georgia.
During this tenure, at about age 44

orthodox:Seraphim_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Seraphim II of Constantinople was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1757 until 1761.
ev: Seven Years' War – French and Indian War: Siege of Louisbourg: James Wolfe's attack at Louisbourg, Nova Scotia, commences.
During this tenure, at about age 68

orthodox:Joannicius_III_of_Constantinopl.bio: Joannicius III of Constantinople was Archbishop of Peć and Serbian Patriarch from 1739 to 1746 and Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1761 to 1763. The ordinal number of his title is III both for his office as Serbian Patriarch and of Constantinople.
ev: Empress Catherine the Great of Russia endorses Ivan Betskoy's plans for a Foundling Home in Moscow.
During this tenure, at about age 63

orthodox:Samuel_of_Constantinople.bio: Samuel of Constantinople, lay name Skarlatos Chantzeris, served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople during the periods 1763–1768 and 1773–1774.
ev: Eight-year-old child prodigy Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart performs a private concert before King George III and Queen Charlotte in Great Britain, and has an encore on May 19.
During this tenure, at about age 64

orthodox:Meletius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Meletius II of Constantinople served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople during the period 1768–1769. He was born in Tenedos. From 1750 until 1768, he served as metropolitan bishop of Larissa and then was elected Ecumenical Patriarch. During the uprising of 1769, he was dismissed and was exiled to Mytilene. In 1775, with permission of the Sultan Abdul Hamid I, he returned to Tenedos and in 1777 to Constantinople, where he died destitute in 1780. He was probably buried on Tenedos.
ev: The palace of the Ottoman Grand Vizier is destroyed by a fire in Constantinople.
During this tenure, at about age 18

orthodox:Theodosius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Theodosius II, lay surname Christianopoulos, served as the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople between 1769 and 1773.
ev: In Egypt, Ottoman rebels revolt, killing Ali Bey, Mamluk Sultan of Egypt.
During this tenure

orthodox:Sophronius_II_of_Constantinople.bio: Sophronius II of Constantinople served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople during the period 1775–1780 and, as Sophronius V, Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem in 1771–1774.
