When the abbot of the monastery departed, he was chosen to replace him and did well in managing the monastery. For his good virtues, he was ordained a Pope to succeed the great Pope Cyril IV, the 110th Patriarch.
ev: Hector Berlioz's opera Les Troyens is performed for the first time, at the Théâtre Lyrique in Paris.
During this tenure, at about age 63

coptic:Pope_Cyril_V_of_Alexandria.bio: Pope Cyril V of Alexandria was the 112th Pope of Alexandria & Patriarch of the See of St. Mark, reigning for 52 years, 9 months and 6 days. He was the longest-serving Pope in the history of the Coptic Orthodox Church. He was born as Youhanna (John) in 1824 or 1830/1831 according to different accounts and he died on 7 August 1927.
ev: Wilbur Wright flies in France for the first time, demonstrating controlled powered flight in Europe.
Wilbur Wright
During this tenure, at about age 84

coptic:Pope_John_XIX_of_Alexandria.bio: Pope John XIX of Alexandria was the Coptic Patriarch of Alexandria, Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St. Mark from 1928 until his death in 1942.
ev: The BBC launches the world's first regular television service in high-definition (according to contemporary standards).
BBC
During this tenure, at about age 81

coptic:Pope_Macarius_III_of_Alexandria.bio: Pope Macarius III of Alexandria was the 114th Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St. Mark. Before becoming a pope, he was the Metropolitan of Asyut in Egypt. He is the second metropolitan of an Eparchy to become a pope in the history of the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria. The first metropolitan to become a pope was John XIX. On several occasions, Habib Elmasry, secretary of the General Congregation Council (Elmagles Elmelly Ela'am) of the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria, vocally disagreed with Macarius's papal appointment.
ev: The Dumbarton Oaks Conference (Washington Conversations on International Peace and Security Organization) opens in Washington, D.C.: U.S., British, Chinese, French and Soviet representatives meet to plan the foundation of the United Nations.
Dumbarton Oaks Conference
During this tenure, at about age 72

coptic:Pope_Joseph_II_of_Alexandria.bio: Pope Joseph II of Alexandria was the 115th Pope of Alexandria & Patriarch of the See of St. Mark.
ev: EDSAC, the first practicable stored-program computer, runs its first program at Cambridge University.
During this tenure, at about age 74

coptic:Pope_Cyril_VI_of_Alexandria.bio: Pope Cyril VI was the 116th pope of Alexandria and patriarch of the See of St. Mark from 10 May 1959 until his death in 1971.
ev: President John F. Kennedy, in his "We choose to go to the Moon" speech at Rice University, reaffirms that the U.S. will put a man on the Moon by the end of the decade.
John F. Kennedy
During this tenure, at about age 60

coptic:Pope_Shenouda_III_of_Alexandria.bio: Pope Shenouda III was the 117th Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St. Mark. His papacy lasted 40 years, 4 months, and 4 days, from 14 November 1971 until his death in 2012. His official title was Pope of Alexandria and the Patriarch of All Africa on the Holy Apostolic Throne of Saint Mark the Evangelist, Father of fathers, Shepherd of shepherds, Successor of Saint Mark, thirteenth among the Apostles, Ecumenical Judge, Beloved of Christ. He was also the head of the Holy Synod of the Coptic Orthodox Church.
ev: Michael Jackson performs the Moonwalk for the first time while performing "Billie Jean" on the Motown 25 television special.
During this tenure, at about age 60

coptic:Pope_Tawadros_II_of_Alexandria.bio: Pope Tawadros II is the 118th and current pope of Alexandria and patriarch of the See of St. Mark, succeeding the late Pope Shenouda III as leader of the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria. He took office on 18 November 2012 (Coptic calendar: 9 Hathor 1729), two weeks after being selected.
ev: Chinese probe Chang'e 4 becomes the first artificial object to land on the far side of the Moon.
During this tenure, at about age 67

syriac:Severus_of_Antioch.bio: Severus of Antioch also known as Severus of Gaza and nicknamed the Crown of Syrians, was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 512 until his death in 538. He is venerated as a saint in the Oriental Orthodox Church, and his feast day is celebrated on 29 September by the Syriac Orthodox Church and 8 February by the Coptic Orthodox Church Born in Sozopolis, Severus studied grammar, rhetoric and philosophy in the city of Alexandria, Egypt.
ev: Battle of Satala: A Byzantine cavalry force under command of Sittas defeats a major Persian invasion into Roman Armenia.
Battle of Satala (530)
During this tenure, at about age 74

syriac:Sergius_of_Tella.bio: Sergius of Tella was the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from c. 544 to c. 547 or c. 557 to 560.
ev: Battle of the Fields of Cato: The Byzantine army, under John Troglita, crushes the Moorish revolt in Byzacena (Tunisia).
Battle of the Fields of Cato
During this tenure

syriac:Paul_the_Black.bio: Paul II the Black, also known as Paul of Bēth Ukkāme, was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from c. 551 or 564 to his deposition in 578. He succeeded Sergius of Tella as the spiritual leader of the Syrian non-Chalcedonians, in opposition to the Chalcedonian Imperial Church, and led the nascent Syriac Orthodox Church as it endured division and persecution.
ev: Lazic War: A Byzantine expeditionary force under Justin retakes Archaeopolis, and routs the Persian army.
Lazic War
During this tenure

syriac:Peter_III_of_Callinicum.bio: Peter III of Callinicum was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 581 until his death in 591. He is commemorated as a saint by the Syriac Orthodox Church in the Martyrology of Rabban Sliba, and his feast day is 22 April.
ev: The Franks and Burgundians under King Guntram invade Italy. They capture the cities Milan and Verona, but are forced to leave by a plague outbreak in the Po Valley.
Franks
During this tenure, at about age 89
King Khosrau II sends a Persian expedition to South Arabia and conquers Yemen. He establishes a military base to control the sea trade with the East.
Khosrau II
During this tenure

syriac:Athanasius_I_Gammolo.bio: Athanasius I Gammolo was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 594/595 or 603 until his death in 631. He is commemorated as a saint by the Syriac Orthodox Church in the Martyrology of Rabban Sliba, and his feast day is 3 January.
ev: The first of the Japanese embassies to Imperial China is sent.
Japanese missions to Imperial China
During this tenure, at about age 99

syriac:John_III_of_the_Sedre.bio: John III of the Sedre was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 631 until his death in 648. He is commemorated as a saint by the Syriac Orthodox Church, and his feast day is 14 December.
ev: Empress Kōgyoku ascends to the throne of Japan, after her husband (and uncle) Emperor Jomei's death in 641.
Empress Kōgyoku
During this tenure, at about age 42

syriac:Theodore_(Syriac_Orthodox_patriar.bio: Theodore was the Syriac Orthodox patriarch of Antioch whose term began between 649 and 651 and ended with his death between 664 and 667. According to Bar Hebraeus, Theodore was a monk in the desert of Skete in Egypt who later moved to the monastery of Qenneshre in Syria. He was consecrated as patriarch of Antioch by the bishop Abraham of Emesa. Sources disagree on the date of Theodore's consecration as patriarch, as it is placed in December 649 by Bar Hebraeus in his Ecclesiastical History, whilst the Zuqnin Chronicle dates the consecration to 650/1.
ev: King Penda of Mercia invades Bernicia, and besieges King Oswiu at Bamburgh, in North East England.
Penda of Mercia
During this tenure

syriac:Severus_II_bar_Masqeh.bio: Severus II bar Masqeh was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 667/668 until his death in 684. He is commemorated as a saint by the Syriac Orthodox Church.
ev: King Hlothhere of Kent re-establishes Kentish supremacy in London.
During this tenure, at about age 74

syriac:Athanasius_II_Baldoyo.bio: Athanasius II Baldoyo, also known as Athanasius of Balad, and Athanasius of Nisibis, was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 684 until his death in 687.
ev: Kʼinich Kan Bahlam II accedes to the rulership of the Maya polity of Palenque.
During this tenure, at about age 50

Arab conquest of Armenia: The Muslim Arabs under Abdallah ibn Abd al-Malik (a son of caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan) invade Armenia and subdue the anti-Arab revolt along with his uncle Muhammad ibn Marwan.
Arab conquest of Armenia
During this tenure

syriac:Elias_I_of_Antioch.bio: Elias I of Antioch was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 709 until his death in 723. He is commemorated as a saint by the Syriac Orthodox Church in the Martyrology of Rabban Sliba, and his feast day is 3 November.
ev: King Dae Jo-yeong of Balhae (Korea) resumes tributary payments to the Tang dynasty. The Tai peoples are forced to accept Chinese sovereignty.
Go of Balhae
During this tenure, at about age 71

syriac:Athanasius_III_(Syriac_Orthodox_p.bio: Athanasius III was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 724 until his death in 739/740.
syriac:Athanasius_III_(Syriac_Orthodox_p.w: Athanasius III (Syriac Orthodox patriarch of Antioch)
ev: The first annual Sumo tournament in Japan is held by Emperor Shōmu.
Sumo
During this tenure

syriac:Iwannis_I.bio: Iwannis I was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 739/740 until his death in 754/755.
ev: An earthquake strikes the Middle East from northern Egypt to northwestern Mesopotamia, destroying many remnants of Byzantine culture.
earthquake
During this tenure

syriac:George_of_Beltan.bio: George of Beltan was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 758 until his death in 789 or 790.
ev: The Maya city of Dos Pilas is abandoned, after the Tamarindito and Petexbatún centres revolt against their Dos Pilas overlord.
Maya civilization
During this tenure, at about age 59

syriac:Joseph_of_Antioch.bio: Joseph was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 790 until he died in 792.
ev: The Westphalians rise up against the Saxons, in response to a forcible recruitment for wars against the Avars. However, Pepin, sub-king of Northern Italy and son of King Charlemagne, continues the war, and wins considerable booty from the Avars.
Westphalia
During this tenure, at about age 91

syriac:Quriaqos_of_Tagrit.bio: Quriaqos of Tagrit was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church, from 793 until his death in 817. He is commemorated as a saint by the Syriac Orthodox Church in the Martyrology of Rabban Sliba, and his feast day is 13 or 16 August.
ev: Caliph al Ma’mun founds a school in Baghdad called the House of Wisdom. In this school scholars translated Greek philosophy classics into Arabic.
Al-Ma'mun
During this tenure, at about age 63

syriac:Dionysius_I_Telmaharoyo.bio: Dionysius I Telmaharoyo, also known as Dionysius of Tel Mahre, was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 818 until his death in 845.
ev: Battle of Roncevaux Pass: The Basques and Banu Qasi defeat a Frankish expedition, led by Counts Aznar and Ebles, in the Pyrenees.
Battle of Roncevaux Pass (824)
During this tenure, at about age 51

syriac:John_IV_of_Antioch.bio: John IV was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 846 until his death in 873.
ev: King Louis the German suppresses the revolt of his son Carloman (for the second time), who wants a partition (mainly of Bavaria) of the East Frankish Kingdom.
Louis the German
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_II.bio: Ignatius II was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 878 until his death in 883.
ev: Battle of Saucourt-en-Vimeu: The West Frankish kings Louis III, and his brother Carloman II, rout Viking raiders (near Abbeville).
During this tenure
Kings Eochaid and Giric of Alba and Strathclyde are deposed by Viking invaders. They are succeeded by Donald II, the son of the late Constantine I, who becomes king of Scotland.
Eochaid, son of Rhun
During this tenure

syriac:Dionysius_II_of_Antioch.bio: Dionysius II was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 896/897 until his death in 908/909.
ev: China loses control over Annam (Northern Vietnam). The village notable Khuc Thua Du leads a rebellion against the Tang Dynasty. The Chinese garrison at Tong Binh is destroyed. Khuc Thua Du declares Annam autonomous.
China
During this tenure, at about age 104

Ragnall ua Ímair, a Viking chief from Ireland, takes control of the Norse Kingdom of York (also referred to as Jórvik) and the English-ruled Earldom of Northumbria. He establishes himself as king at York.
Ragnall ua Ímair
During this tenure
In Spain, Fruela II, King of León and King of Galicia, dies and is temporarily succeeded by his son, Alfonso Fróilaz.
During this tenure
Battle of Alhandic: Abd-al-Rahman III defeats the garrison of those loyal to Ramiro II at Zamora, in the context of the Spanish Reconquista.
During this tenure
The Tenryaku era under the reign of Emperor Murakami ends. The Tentoku era begins.
Tenryaku
During this tenure
The Song dynasty is founded in China.
Song dynasty
During this tenure
The Nanping State, one of the Ten Kingdoms in south-central China, is forced to surrender, when invaded by armies of the Song Dynasty.
Jingnan
During this tenure

syriac:John_VII_Sarigta.bio: John VII Sarigta was the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 965 until his death in 985.
ev: Fall – Otto II departs with an expeditionary force from Rome, and invades Apulia (Southern Italy) to punish the Saracens. He demands a fleet from Pisa, and imposes a trade embargo against Venice.
Apulia
During this tenure

syriac:Athanasius_IV_Salhoyo.bio: Athanasius IV Salhoyo was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 986/987 until his death in 1002/1003.
ev: A Danish Viking fleet, under Olaf Tryggvason, sails up the Thames Estuary, and besieges London. King Æthelred II (the Unready) pays Olaf 16,000 lbs of silver (Danegeld).
Denmark
During this tenure, at about age 93

syriac:John_VIII_bar_Abdoun.bio: John VIII bar Abdoun was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1004 until his death in 1033.
ev: Emperor Rajendra Chola I extends his influence of the Chola Empire to the banks of the Ganges River (North India) and invades Bengal.
Rajendra Chola I
During this tenure, at about age 77
Battle of Ostrovo: The Byzantines, with the help of the Varangian Guard, led by Harald Hardrada (future king of Norway), defeat the Bulgarian troops, near Lake Ostrovo in Greece.
Battle of Ostrovo
During this tenure
The Iron Pagoda in Kaifeng is constructed, during the Chinese Song dynasty.
Iron Pagoda
During this tenure
The Seljuk Turks under Alp Arslan invade Anatolia, and capture Ani after a siege of 25-days. He sacks the city and slaughters its citizens.
Anatolia
During this tenure

syriac:John_X_bar_Shushan.bio: John X bar Shushan was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church, from 1063/1064 until his death in 1072/1073.
ev: Edgar Ætheling is proclaimed king of England (but is never crowned). He is soon forced to submit to the rule of William the Conqueror.
During this tenure, at about age 65
Battle of Kemej: King Solomon, King of Hungary routs the army of his cousin Duke Géza with the assistance of German troops.
During this tenure
Robert Curthose instigates his first insurrection against his father, King William the Conqueror in the Normandy.
Robert Curthose
During this tenure
Siege of Syracuse – Norman forces under Count Roger I ("Bosso") conquer Syracuse, the last Muslim stronghold in Sicily.
Siege of Syracuse (1086)
During this tenure
Qin Guan, Chinese poet of the Song dynasty, writes the Can Shu (Book of Sericulture), which describes a silk-reeling machine that has the world's oldest known mechanical belt drive.
Qin Guan
During this tenure

syriac:Athanasius_VI_bar_Khamoro.bio: Athanasius VI bar Khamoro was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1091 until his death in 1129.
ev: Henry IV, Holy Roman Emperor, is deposed by his son Henry V (who is king of Germany). Henry is forced to resign his crown and is imprisoned in the castle of Böckelheim.
During this tenure, at about age 104

syriac:John_XI_bar_Mawdyono.bio: John XI bar Mawdyono, also known as Yuhanna Modyana, was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1130 until his death in 1137.
ev: Jin–Song War: Emperor Gao Zong of the Song dynasty moves the capital from Yangzhou to Hangzhou, after the Jurchen Jin dynasty captures Kaifeng in the Jingkang Incident.
Jin–Song Wars
During this tenure, at about age 128

syriac:Athanasius_VII_bar_Qatra.bio: Athanasius VII bar Qatra was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1139 until his death in 1166.
ev: Portuguese forces, led by King Afonso I of Portugal ("the Great"), conquer Pamela, Alcácer do Sal and Sesimbra from the diminished Almoravids.
Afonso I of Portugal
During this tenure

syriac:Michael_the_Syrian.bio: Michael the Syrian, also known as Michael the Great, was the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 1166 until his death in 1199. He is widely regarded as one of the most important figures in the history of the Syriac Orthodox Church, remembered both as a saint and as a historian. Hailing from the distinguished Qindisi family of Melitene, he quickly rose through the ranks to become Patriarch of Antioch.
ev: Vordingborg Castle is completed by King Valdemar I of Denmark as a defensive fortress.
Vordingborg Castle
During this tenure, at about age 49

Jochi, eldest son of Genghis Khan, subjugates people of the Siberian forest (taiga); the Uriankhai, the Oirats, the Barga, the Khakas, the Buryats, and the Tuvans, extending the northern border of the Mongol Empire.
Jochi
During this tenure

syriac:John_XII_of_Antioch.bio: John XII Yeshu was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1208 until his death in 1220.
ev: Mina'i ware pottery production in Persia ceases as a result of the Mongol conquests.
Mina'i ware
During this tenure, at about age 118

syriac:Ignatius_III_David.bio: Ignatius III David was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1222 until 1252.
ev: Battle of Cheoin: Korean forces defeat a Mongol attack at Cheoin. The Mongol Empire concludes a peace treaty with Goryeo and withdraws its forces.
During this tenure

syriac:John_XIII_bar_Ma'dani.bio: John XIII Aaron bar Ma'dani was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1252 until his death in 1263.
ev: The Chinese era Jingding begins and ends in 1264 in the Southern Song dynasty of China (last era of Emperor Lizong).
Chinese era name
During this tenure, at about age 59
Kublai Khan renames his empire "Great Yuan" (大元; dà yuán), officially marking the start of the Yuan dynasty in China.
During this tenure
Beatrice Portinari, muse of the Italian poet Dante Alighieri, dies in Florence. In his Divine Comedy (La Divina Commedia), he transforms his memory of Beatrice into an allegory of divine love.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Behnam_Hadloyo.bio: Ignatius Behnam Hadloyo was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1445 until his death in 1454.
ev: The English Parliament is opened by King Henry VI at Westminster for a five month session.
During this tenure
In what is now the nation of Kosovo, the city of Prizren is captured from the Serbian Despotate by the Ottoman Turkish invaders.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_John_XIV.bio: Ignatius John XIV bar Shay Allah was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1483 until his death in 1493.
ev: Christopher Columbus anchors in Lisbon and completes his February 15 letter on the first voyage, conveying the news of his discoveries.
During this tenure, at about age 51

syriac:Ignatius_Noah_of_Lebanon.bio: Ignatius Noah of Lebanon, also known as Nūḥ Pūnīqoyo or Nūḥ al-Bqūfānī, was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1493/1494 until his death in 1509.
ev: Harmonice Musices Odhecaton, the first printed collection of polyphonic music, is published by Ottaviano Petrucci in Venice.
During this tenure, at about age 50
French ambassador Janus Lascaris leaves Venice, after being recalled by king Louis XII in the eve of the War of the League of Cambrai.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Jacob_I.bio: Ignatius Jacob I, also known as Jacob al-Khuri or Jacob of al-Nabk, was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1510/1512 until his death in 1517/1519.
ev: Thérouanne in the north of France is given to Henry VIII of England after a treaty is concluded in the aftermath of the Battle of the Spurs.
During this tenure
King Henry VIII of England and King Francis I of France meet at the famous Field of the Cloth of Gold.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Abdullah_I.bio: Ignatius Abdullah I was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1521 until his death in 1557.
ev: King Henry VIII of England is first informed of that the Queen consort, Catherine Howard, has been having an affair with Thomas Culpeper.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Ni'matallah.bio: Ignatius Niʿmatallah was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1557 until his resignation in 1576.
ev: The Ottoman conquest of Cyprus begins as more than 350 Ottoman ships and over 60,000 troops land near Larnaca and then march toward the Cypriot capital, Nicosia.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_David_II_Shah.bio: Ignatius David II Shah was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1576 until his death in 1591.
ev: The first biography of Nicolaus Copernicus is completed by Bernardino Baldi.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Pilate.bio: Ignatius Pilate was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1591 until his death in 1597.
ev: What is probably the first performance of William Shakespeare's play, Richard II, takes place in London.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Hidayat_Allah.bio: Ignatius Hidayat Allah was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1597/1598 until 1639/1640.
ev: The siege of Székesfehérvár, an Ottoman occupied Hungarian fortress, is completed by troops of the Holy Roman Empire after 16 days. The Ottomans will recapture Székesfehérvár a year later.
During this tenure, at about age 100

syriac:Ignatius_Simon.bio: Ignatius Simon was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1640 until 1653.
ev: King Frederick III of Denmark signs a manifesto, de facto declaring war on Sweden.
Frederick III of Denmark
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Yeshu_II.bio: Ignatius Yeshu II was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1653 until his death in 1661.
ev: Anglo-Spanish War – Battle of Santa Cruz de Tenerife: English Admiral Robert Blake attempts to seize a Spanish treasure fleet.
Anglo-Spanish War (1654–1660)
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Abdulmasih_I.bio: Ignatius Abdulmasih I was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1662 until 1686.
ev: Thomas Otway's classic play Venice Preserv'd or A Plot Discover'd is given its first performance, premiering at the Duke's Theatre.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_George_II.bio: Ignatius George II was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1687 until his death in 1708.
ev: The Nine Years' War begins in Europe and America after Louis XIV attacks Philippsburg in the Holy Roman Empire.
During this tenure, at about age 40

syriac:Ignatius_Isaac_II.bio: Ignatius Isaac II was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1709 until his abdication in 1723.
ev: Seventh Ottoman–Venetian War: The Ottoman Empire unsuccessfully lays siege to Corfu, the last bastion of the Republic of Venice in the Greek islands.
During this tenure, at about age 69

syriac:Ignatius_Shukrallah_II.bio: Ignatius Shukrallah II was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1722 until his death in 1745.
ev: The Treaty of Constantinople is signed, partitioning Persia between the Ottoman Empire and Russia.
During this tenure, at about age 50

syriac:Ignatius_George_III.bio: Ignatius George III was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1745 until his death in 1768.
ev: The Seven Years' War formally begins, when Great Britain declares war on France.
During this tenure, at about age 68

syriac:Ignatius_George_IV.bio: Ignatius George IV was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1768 until his death in 1781.
ev: American Revolutionary War: Battle of Harlem Heights – The Continental Army under Washington is victorious against the British on Manhattan.
During this tenure, at about age 67

syriac:Ignatius_Matthew.bio: Ignatius Matthew was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1782 until his death in 1817.
ev: Napoleon is defeated at Waterloo.
Battle of Waterloo
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Yunan.bio: Ignatius Yunan was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1817 until 1818 when he resigned from the Holy See and went to live in the Monastery of Mor Elias until his death in 1823. His time as a patriarch was the shortest among all Syriac Orthodox patriarchs.
ev: Carl III of Sweden–Norway is crowned king of Norway, in Trondheim.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_George_V.bio: Ignatius George V was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1818 until his death in 1836.
ev: French explorer René Caillié becomes the first non-Muslim to enter Timbuktu and later return alive.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Elias_II.bio: Ignatius Elias II was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1838 until his death in 1847.
ev: The Polytechnic Institution, predecessor of the University of Westminster and Britain's first polytechnic, opens in Regent Street, London.
During this tenure, at about age 60

syriac:Ignatius_Jacob_II.bio: Ignatius Jacob II was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1847 until his death in 1871.
ev: American Civil War: Julia Ward Howe's "Battle Hymn of the Republic" is published for the first time in the Atlantic Monthly.
During this tenure

syriac:Ignatius_Peter_IV.bio: Mor Ignatius Peter IV, also known as Ignatius Peter III, was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1872 until his death in 1894. He is regarded by many as the architect of the modern church.
ev: Richard D'Oyly Carte's Savoy Theatre opens in London, the world's first public building to be fully lit by electricity, using Joseph Swan's incandescent light bulbs.
During this tenure, at about age 83

syriac:Ignatius_Abded_Mshiho_II.bio: Ignatius Abdulmasih II was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1895 until his deposition in 1903.
ev: The British Empire celebrates Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee, marking the 60th year of her reign. No other British monarch will celebrate such a jubilee until Victoria's great-great-granddaughter Elizabeth II in 2012.
During this tenure, at about age 43

syriac:Ignatius_Abded_Aloho_II.bio: Ignatius Abdullah II also Ignatius Abdullah II Stephan was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1906 until his death in 1915.
ev: Armenian genocide: 17,000 civilians from the Ottoman Armenian population of Trebizond are massacred by Ottoman Turks.
Armenian genocide
During this tenure, at about age 82

syriac:Ignatius_Elias_III.bio: St. Ignatius Elias III was the 119th Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1917 until his death in 1932. He is known for his visit to Malankara to resolve the dispute between the two factions of the Malankara church. He died before he could complete his mission and was buried in outside the St. Stephen's church in Majnikkara. He was canonised as a saint by Ignatius Zakka I in 1987.
ev: The first domestic radio sets come to stores in the United States; a Westinghouse radio costs $10.
Westinghouse Electric (1886)
During this tenure, at about age 53

syriac:Ignatius_Aphrem_I.bio: Mor Ignatius Aphrem I Barsoum was the 120th Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1933 until his death in 1957. He was consecrated as a Metropolitan and as a Patriarch at a very hard time for the Syriac Orthodox church and its people and parishes and he worked very hard to re-establish the church initiations to where his people moved. He researched, wrote, translated, scripted, and published many scholarly works that included books on the saints, tradition, liturgy, music, and history of Syriac Orthodox Church.
ev: The Manchester Baby in England becomes the first stored-program computer to successfully execute a program.
Manchester Baby
During this tenure, at about age 61

syriac:Ignatius_Jacob_III.bio: Mor Ignatius Jacob III was the 121st Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church 1957–1980. He was skilled in and knowledgeable in Syriac sacral music or Beth Gazo. He re-established the Maphrianate/Catholicate in the Jacobite Syrian Orthodox Church (the Indian Church).
ev: American researchers discover the Madrid Codices by Leonardo da Vinci in the National Library of Spain.
During this tenure, at about age 54

syriac:Ignatius_Zakka_I.bio: Mor Ignatius Zakka I Iwas was the 122nd reigning Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and All the East and, as such, Supreme Head of the Universal Syriac Orthodox Church. Also known by his traditional episcopal name, Severios, he was enthroned as patriarch on 14 September 1980 in St. George's Patriarchal Cathedral in Damascus. He succeeded Ignatius Ya`qub III. As is traditional for the head of the church, Mor Severios adopted the name Ignatius. Zakka was known for his involvement in ecumenical dialogue.
ev: State President of South Africa P. W. Botha meets the imprisoned 70-year-old Nelson Mandela face-to-face for the first time.
State President of South Africa
During this tenure, at about age 56

syriac:Ignatius_Aphrem_II.bio: Mor Ignatius Aphrem II is a Syrian–American Christian prelate who has served as the Patriarch of the Syriac Orthodox Church since 29 May 2014. Born and raised in Qamishili, Syria, Karim became a monk in 1985 and was later ordained as a deacon and then as a priest. He received a Bachelor of Arts in Divinity from the Coptic Theological Seminary in Cairo in 1988. In 1992, he received a Licentiate of Sacred Theology and in 1994, a Doctor of Divinity from St Patrick's College, Ireland.
ev: The Juno spacecraft performs its only flyby of Jupiter's moon Ganymede, the first flyby of the moon by any spacecraft in over 20 years.
Juno (spacecraft)
During this tenure, at about age 56

armenian:Jude_the_Apostle.bio: Jude the Apostle was one of the Apostles in the New Testament. He is generally identified as Thaddeus (Θαδδαῖος; Old Armenian: Թադէոս; Coptic: ⲑⲁⲇⲇⲉⲟⲥ) and is also variously called Judas Thaddaeus, Jude Thaddaeus, Judas son of James, Judas of James, Jude of James, or Lebbaeus. He is sometimes identified with Jude, the brother of Jesus, but is clearly distinguished from Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus prior to his crucifixion.
ev: Emperor Ming of Han introduces Buddhism to China inviting monks from the western Indus Valley.
Emperor Ming of Han
During this tenure, at about age 44

armenian:Bartholomew_the_Apostle.bio: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus according to the New Testament. Most scholars today identify Bartholomew as Nathanael, who appears in the Gospel of John (1:45–51; cf. 21:2).
ev: Pompeii, the city at the foot of Mount Vesuvius, builds a new monumental forum, after the town is heavily damaged by a strong earthquake.
Pompeii
During this tenure, at about age 163
Expedition by the Roman Septimius Flaccus to southern Egypt. He probably reaches Sudan.
Egypt
During this tenure
Vespasian fortifies Armazi (Georgia) for the Iberian king Mithridates I. The Alans raid the Roman frontier in Armenia.
Armazi
During this tenure
The Colosseum opens in Rome.
Colosseum
During this tenure
Emperor Hadrian averts a war with Parthia by a personal meeting with Osroes I (according to the Historia Augusta, disputed).
Hadrian
During this tenure
First year of Yonghe era of the Chinese Han Dynasty.
Han dynasty
During this tenure
Antonine Plague: A pandemic breaks out in Rome, after the Roman army returns from Parthia. The plague significantly depopulates the Roman Empire and China.
Antonine Plague
During this tenure
Nobles of Britain demand that Emperor Commodus rescind all power given to Tigidius Perennis, who is eventually executed.
Commodus
During this tenure

armenian:Merozanes.bio: Merozanes, Mehružan, or Meruzan was a Christian bishop present in Armenia around 240 to 270. The only mention of this individual, with an Iranian origin name, comes from Eusebius, who, in his Church History, states that around 250, Dionysius of Alexandria sent a letter of "repentance to the brethren in Armenia, of whom Merozanes was bishop." Given the onomastics of the person, it is possible that he was a Syriac bishop, perhaps in Taron.
ev: Battle of Augusta Traiana: The Romans lose the battle against the Goths.
Battle of Augusta Traiana
During this tenure

armenian:Gregory_the_Illuminator.bio: Gregory the Illuminator was the founder and first official head of the Armenian Apostolic Church. He converted Armenia from Zoroastrianism to Christianity in the early fourth century (traditionally dated to 301), making Armenia the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion. He is venerated as a saint in the Armenian Apostolic Church and in some other churches. Gregory is said to have been the son of a Parthian nobleman, Anak, who assassinated the Arsacid king of Armenia Khosrov.
ev: History of the Jews in Germany: Jews in modern-day Germany are documented for the first time, in Colonia Agrippinensium.
History of the Jews in Germany
During this tenure, at about age 82

armenian:St._Aristaces_I.bio: Aristaces or Aristakes I was the second Catholicos of the Armenian Church from 325 until his death in 333. He was the younger son and successor of Gregory the Illuminator, the founder and first head of the Armenian Church and his wife, Julitta (or Mariam) of Armenia. Most of the information about Aristaces's life comes from the fifth-century Armenian history attributed to Agathangelos. Aristaces was born in Caesarea of Cappadocia to Gregory the Illuminator and his wife Julitta (or Mariam) of Armenia.
ev: Emperor Constantine the Great pulls Roman troops out of Britain, and abandons work on Hadrian's Wall.
Constantine the Great
During this tenure, at about age 69

armenian:St._Vrtanes_I.bio: Vrtanes also known Saint Vrtanes (Armenian: Սբ. Վրթանէս Ա. Պարթև) was the 14th Catholicos-Patriarch of the Armenian Apostolic Church serving from 333 until his death in 341. He was the son of Julitta (or Mariam) of Armenia and Gregory the Illuminator. In 333, Vrtanes succeeded Aristaces as third in line in the then-hereditary Gregorid line of the Catholicos of the Armenian Catholic Church.
ev: Flavius Dalmatius puts down a revolt in Cyprus, led by Calocaerus. Calocaerus is brought to Tarsus (Cilicia), and executed.
Flavius Dalmatius
During this tenure, at about age 49
The Western Roman Emperor Constans I is in Britain, possibly in a military campaign against the Picts and Scots (the last visit to Britain by a legitimate emperor).
Constans
During this tenure

armenian:Daniel_I_of_Armenia.bio: Daniel I of Armenia was the 16th Catholicos-Patriarch of the Armenian Apostolic Church. He was a Syrian who reigned as the Catholicoi after the reign of four hereditary Parthian catholicoi (St. Gregory I the Enlightener, his son St. Aristaces I, St. Vrtanes I and St. Husik I. He only ruled less than one year in 347 AD and was succeeded by Pharen I of Armenia. Daniel was an ethnic Syriac and a disciple of Gregory the Illuminator. After King Tiran ordered the death of Catholicos Husik, he requested Daniel to replace him.
ev: Li Shi, ruler of Cheng Han, fails in his attempt to halt a Jin expedition under Huan Wen. He flees to the capital Chengdu and surrenders his forces. Emperor Jin Mudi spares his life and makes him a marquess.
Li Shi (emperor)
During this tenure
Nepotianus, Roman usurper, proclaims himself emperor and enters Rome with a group of gladiators.
During this tenure

armenian:St._Nerses_I.bio: There was also a Caucasian Albanian Catholicos Nerses I, who ruled in 689–706, and a Patriarch Nerses I of Constantinople, who ruled in 1704. Nerses I the Great (Armenian: Ներսէս Ա Մեծ, romanized: Nersēs A Mets; died c. 373), also known as Nerses the Parthian (Ներսէս Պարթև, Nersēs Part’ev), was an Armenian Catholicos (or Patriarch) who lived in the fourth century.
ev: Emperor Constantius II enters Rome for the first time to celebrate his victory over Magnentius. He address the Senate and the Roman people.
During this tenure, at about age 28

armenian:Sahak_I.bio: Sahak I (Armenian: Սահակ Ա. Մանազկերտցի) was a catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church and the first of several catholicoi during the Albaniosid Dynasty in fourth century. According to Faustus of Byzantium, a popular assembly selected Sahak I as the successor of Pharen I of Armenia after Pharen's death. Awags of the prince of Gardmanac'jor and ten other nakharars accompanied Sahak I to Caesarea in Cappadocia. There bishops ordained Sahak I as catholicos of Greater Armenia.
ev: Goths cross the Danube into the Roman Empire.
Gothic War (376–382)
During this tenure
Battle of Adrianople: Valens leads an elite Roman army to Thrace to confront revolts, but is defeated.
During this tenure

armenian:Aspuraces_I.bio: Aspuraces I (Armenian: Ասպուրակես Ա. Մանազկերտցի) was a catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church. He reigned from 381 to 386 AD and third of three catholicoi from the Albaniosid Dynasty.
ev: Niall of the Nine Hostages becomes the first High King of Ireland.
Niall of the Nine Hostages
During this tenure

armenian:Isaac_of_Armenia.bio: Isaac or Sahak of Armenia was the catholicos of the Armenian Church from c. 387 until c. 438. He is sometimes known as Isaac the Great or Sahak the Parthian (Armenian: Սահակ Պարթեւ; Sahak Part῾ew) in reference to his father's Parthian origin. He was the last Armenian patriarch who was directly descended from Gregory the Illuminator, who converted the Kingdom of Armenia to Christianity in the early fourth century and became the first head of the Armenian Church.
ev: Roman empress Galla Placidia departs with her children Grata Honoria and Valentinian to the court of Constantinople.
Galla Placidia
During this tenure, at about age 75

armenian:Brkisho_of_Armenia.bio: Brkisho or Brkisho "The Syrian" was a catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church of Assyrian origin, from 429 to 432.
ev: The Temple of Goddess Athena on the Acropolis of Athens is sacked. Athenian Pagans are persecuted.
Parthenon
During this tenure
Christmas is celebrated for the first time in Alexandria.
During this tenure

Period of civil war and famine in Britain, caused by rival kingdoms and Pictish invasions; the situation aggravates tensions between Pelagian and Roman factions. Pro-Roman citizens migrate towards Gaul.
civil war
During this tenure
The Vandals sack Rome.
Sack of Rome (455)
During this tenure
The Franks conquer the city of Trier. The Frankish Kingdom becomes a military power and gets involved in Roman politics.
Franks
During this tenure
Revolt of Euric: The Goths in Aquitania revolts. Their king Euric occupies the south of Gaul.
Gothic revolt of Euric
During this tenure
Emperor Zeno officially dissolves the east/west co-emperorship, ruling as the first sole emperor of Rome in 85 years. The position of emperor is never again divided.
Zeno (emperor)
During this tenure
King Gundobad issues a new legal code (Lex Burgundionum) at Lyon, that makes Gallo-Romans and Burgundians subject to the same laws.
During this tenure
Frankish tribesmen, under the command of King Chlothar I, plunder Burgundy.
Franks
During this tenure
Rudravarman is granted investiture by China, as the first king of the fourth dynasty of Champa.
List of Vietnamese monarchs
During this tenure
Battle of Camlann: King Arthur fights his last battle against the forces of his rebellious son (or nephew) Mordred, and is mortally wounded.
Battle of Camlann
During this tenure
Gothic War: Emperor Justinian I sends Belisarius back to the Ostrogothic Kingdom (Italy) with an inadequate Byzantine expeditionary force.
Gothic War (535–554)
During this tenure
Gothic War: King Totila establishes his military base at Tivoli (Central Italy), and prepares a campaign to reconquer the region of Latium.
Gothic War (535-554)
During this tenure
Gothic War: The Ostrogoths under king Totila recapture Rome after a long siege, by bribing the Isaurian garrison.
During this tenure
Elidyr of Strathclyde invades Gwynedd (Wales) and tries to expel his brother-in-law, King Rhun ap Maelgwn.
Kingdom of Strathclyde
During this tenure

armenian:Abraham_I_of_Armenia.bio: This is a list of the catholicoi of all Armenians, head bishops of the Armenian Apostolic Church. To this day 21 Catholicoi of a total of 132 have been glorified within the church.
ev: Goguryeo–Sui War: Emperor Yángdi invades Goguryeo (Korea) with an expeditionary force of over one million men, named the "24 Armies".
Goguryeo–Sui War
During this tenure

armenian:Komitas_Aghtsetsi.bio: Komitas I Aghtsetsi (Armenian: Կոմիտաս Ա Աղցեցի, lit. 'Komitas I of Aghtsk'), also known as Komitas the Builder (Armenian: Կոմիտաս Շինող, romanized: Komitas Shinogh), was the Catholicos of Armenia from 613 until his death in 628. He oversaw several building projects, among which were the complete renovation of Etchmiadzin Cathedral; the construction of Saint Hripsime Church; and the building of the Church of Saint Gregory in Dvin. He is also remembered for his hymn writing and his participation in the theological debates of the time.
armenian:Komitas_Aghtsetsi.next: armenian:name:Christopher II, died aft. 630 — Քրիստափոր Բ Ապահունի:628
armenian:Komitas_Aghtsetsi.nn: Christopher II, died aft. 630 — Քրիստափոր Բ Ապահունի
ev: The Tang dynasty is founded in China.
Tang dynasty
During this tenure

armenian:name:Christopher II, died aft..n: Christopher II, died aft. 630 — Քրիստափոր Բ Ապահունի
ev: Chorpan Tarkhan, general of the Khazars, invades and devastates Roman Armenia. He defeats a Persian cavalry force sent by Shahrbaraz to repel the invasion.
Chorpan Tarkhan
During this tenure

armenian:name:Ezra:630.prev: armenian:name:Christopher II, died aft. 630 — Քրիստափոր Բ Ապահունի:628
armenian:name:Ezra:630.pn: Christopher II, died aft. 630 — Քրիստափոր Բ Ապահունի
ev: Chang'an, capital of the Tang dynasty (China), becomes the largest city of the world, taking the lead from Ctesiphon, capital of Persia.
Chang'an
During this tenure

armenian:Nerses_III_the_Builder.bio: There was also a Caucasian Albanian Catholicos Nerses III, who ruled in 1235–1262. Nerses III the Builder (Armenian: Ներսես Գ Շինող Nerses 3 Shinogh) was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 641 and 661. He was originally from the village of Ishkhan in Tayk. He ruled at a troubled time during which Armenia had to choose between their neighbors Byzantines and Persians along with their new conquerors the Arabs. Catholicos Nerses III received the title of the Builder due to the grand construction works he undertook during his reign.
ev: King Yazdegerd III of Persia is murdered in a miller's hut near Merv by his followers, ending both Persian resistance to Arab conquest, and the Sassanid Empire.
Yazdegerd III
During this tenure
Battle of Baekgang: Korean Baekje forces and their Japanese allies are defeated in a naval battle, by a joint Silla–Tang coalition.
Battle of Baekgang
During this tenure
Arab forces under Yazid (son of caliph Muawiyah I) retire to Cyzicus (Turkey). For the next 4 years the Arab fleet installs a loose blockade around Constantinople.
Yazid I
During this tenure

armenian:Sahak_III.bio: Sahak III may also refer to Sahak III Bagratuni. Sahak III, was the Catholicos of Armenia from 677 through 703. According to the historian Hovhannes Draskhanakerttsi Sahak III was alive in Damascus, where he had gone to discuss peace instead of making war, while a Muslim warrior Okbay was moving with his army through the area of Vanand when the people there massacred them. Okbay returned to the Caliph to raise a large army against Armenia and destroy its churches and kill the population.
ev: Battle of Maskin: An Umayyad army under caliph Abd al-Malik defeats the rebel forces in Mesopotamia. He reconquers the Arabian Peninsula, taking the holy city of Medina.
Battle of Maskin
During this tenure
Emperor Rui Zong abdicates after a brief reign, in favor of his 27-year-old son Xuan Zong, who ascends the imperial throne of the Tang dynasty (China).
During this tenure
King Kʼinich Ahkal Moʼ Nahb III takes the throne of the Maya city-state of Palenque (southern Mexico).
During this tenure

armenian:David_I_of_Armenia.bio: David I was the 49th Catholicos-Patriarch of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 728 and 741. He was from Aramus (then called Aramonk) in the district of Kotayk. He moved the Armenian Apostolic Church's Holy See from Dvin to Aramonk due to Dvin's fall to Arab hands and problems which resulted from that. Catholicos David built a church and patriarchal residence there, near which he was buried upon his death.
ev: King Liutprand of the Lombards attempts to counter the growing independence of the Lombard duchies in southern Italy.
During this tenure

armenian:Dertad_I.bio: Catholicos Dertad I was the 50th Catholicos-Patriarch of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 741 and 764. According to the historian Kirakos Ganjaketsi, Dertad was from Otmus village and was a 'modest, blessed man, radiant in all virtue'. He reigned in a time of relative peace with a break in the Arab invasions.
ev: Arab–Byzantine War: Emperor Constantine V destroys the Arab fleet off Cyprus, with the aid of ships from the Italian city-states, breaking the naval power of the Umayyad Caliphate.{{citation.
Arab–Byzantine Wars
During this tenure
The Franks, under King Pepin III ("the Short"), destroy resistance in central Aquitaine. They conquer the capital of Bordeaux, and devastate the whole region.
Francia
During this tenure

The number 0 is introduced to the city of Baghdad, which will be developed in the Middle East by Arabian mathematicians, who will base their numbers on the Indian system (long after the Maya culture developed the concept, cf. Maya numerals).
0 (number)
During this tenure

armenian:Isaiah_I_of_Armenia.bio: This is a list of the catholicoi of all Armenians, head bishops of the Armenian Apostolic Church. To this day 21 Catholicoi of a total of 132 have been glorified within the church.
ev: The Frankish currency called the livre carolingienne is minted for the first time.
French livre
During this tenure
Charlemagne founds the town of Herford, in order to guard a ford crossing the narrow Werre River.
Herford
During this tenure
Charlemagne loses most of his riding and baggage horses during an equine epidemic; many Saxons take advantage of Charlemagne's Avar setback and rebel once more.
Wagon train
During this tenure
Offa arranges coastal defences to fend off Viking attacks. He forms an alliance with Essex, Kent and Sussex, in an attempt to unify England.
Vikings
During this tenure
Vikings raid Lindisfarne, opening the Viking Age in Britain.
Viking Age
During this tenure
The first known mention of Magdeburg (Saxony-Anhalt), founded by Charlemagne, is made.
Magdeburg
During this tenure

armenian:David_II_of_Armenia.bio: David II of Armenia was Catholicos of All Armenians from 806 to 833. He came from the village of Gagagh in the province of Maghaz.
ev: Emperor Saga of Japan is the first sovereign to drink tea (according to legend), imported from China by monks. The upper classes adopt this beverage for medicinal use.
Emperor Saga
During this tenure, at about age 35

armenian:John_IV_of_Armenia.bio: John IV was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church in 833–855 when the country was under Abbasid overlordship. In 841, he was deposed by the episcopal synod through the machinations of Bagrat II Bagratuni, but he was promptly re-installed in his see by Bagrat's brother Smbat with the assistance of the other princes. It was during John IV's tenure that the Tondrakians first emerged.
ev: Completion in Japan of the Nihon Kōki, third book of the Rikkokushi. This includes the earliest record of cherry blossom at the Imperial Court in Kyoto and of tea brought from China and served to the Emperor.
Nihon Kōki
During this tenure
The Diamond Sutra, the oldest dated printed book, is made in China.
Diamond Sutra
During this tenure

armenian:Gevorg_II_of_Armenia.bio: Catholicos Gevorg II of Garni was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 877 and 897. His contemporary Hovhannes Draskhanakerttsi described him as an honorable man who was selected from the Catholicos's household by Prince Ashot I of Armenia to succeed Patriarch Zakaria. Gevorg anointed and crowned Ashot I when he was declared King of Armenia in 884. Upon King Ashot's death, Gevorg went to Bagaran to preside over his funeral. Ashot's heir Smbat I, who had been away at war, missed his father's funeral and was very grieved.
ev: The Vikings invade Wales once more, and King Rhodri ap Merfyn ("the Great") of Gwynedd, Powys and Seisyllwg is forced to flee to Ireland.
Wales
During this tenure

armenian:Mashdotz_I.bio: Catholicos Mashdotz I was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 897 and 898. He was a monk of Sevanavank monastery and regarded as a very holy man. While a monk, he was asked by sparapet Abas to assist in overthrowing the current Catholicos, George II, and was promised the Catholicosate throne in return. Mashdotz wrote a long letter in response, rejecting the offer to rebel against the Catholicos, and chided Abas for his attempt. The plot failed and Mashdotz continued to be respected for his piety.
ev: King Alfred the Great makes his eldest son Edward the Elder co-ruler of Wessex in preparation for his accession to the English throne.
Alfred the Great
During this tenure, at about age 65

armenian:John_V_the_Historian.bio: Hovhannes Draskhanakerttsi, also called John V the Historian, was Catholicos of Armenia from 897 to 925, and a noted chronicler and historian. He is known for his History of Armenia. He is also the author of a list of Armenian Catholicoi titled Shar Hayrapetatsʻn Hayotsʻ. What little is known about Catholicos Hovhannes's life comes from his own written works.
ev: Emperor Zhao Zong is deposed and forced by a group of Tang eunuchs led by Liu Jishu to abdicate the throne to his son, Crown Prince Li Yu.
During this tenure, at about age 55
Sack of Mecca: The Qarmatians, led by Abu Tahir al-Jannabi, sack Mecca, desecrating the Zamzam Well and carrying off the Black Stone to their homeland in Eastern Arabia.
During this tenure
The Eldgjá volcanic eruption is the largest basalt flood in history (first documented).
Eldgjá
During this tenure

armenian:Yeghishe_I.bio: Yeghishe I also known as Yeghishe I Rshtunetsi was the Catholicos of All Armenians in 941–946. Yeghishe I succeeded his brother Catholicos Theodore I. Ruled the Church from Aghtamar, at the time – the Holy See of the Armenian Apostolic Church. Yeghishe Rshtunetsi was the Bishop of Rshtunik and after the death of Theodore I was elected Catholicos by the initiative of the King of Vaspurakan.
ev: Hywel Dda, king of Deheubarth, annexes Gwynedd and Powys, to become the sole ruler of most of Wales.
Hywel Dda
During this tenure

armenian:Ananias_I_of_Armenia.bio: Catholicos Ananias I, also known as Anania Mokatsi, was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 949 and 968. His predecessor Yeghishe had been deposed as Catholicos and by church regulations no one could be elected during his lifetime. The office was held by a deputy until Yeghishe died two years later and Ananias of Varagavank became pontiff. Catholicos Ananias moved the seat of the Catholicosate from Vaspurakan at Akhtamar to the town of Arghina. He crowned Ashot III in 961 at his new capital nearby of Ani.
ev: Fall – Otto the Great, Holy Roman Emperor, departs for a third expedition in Italy and fights in Lombardy against the partisans under Adalbert II of Ivrea. In November an imperial counter-coup in Rome takes control of Castel Sant'Angelo.
Otto the Great
During this tenure

Battle of Sulcoit in Ireland: The Irish of the Dál gCais led by Brian Boru defeats the Viking forces of Limerick. After the battle the Dál gCais seize and burn the Viking stronghold of Limerick. Ending of Norse expansion in Ireland.
Battle of Sulcoit
During this tenure
Eric the Victorious becomes the first (documented) king of Sweden in Uppland.
Eric the Victorious
During this tenure

armenian:Khachig_I_of_Armenia.bio: Catholicos Khachik I (Armenian: Խաչիկ Ա. Արշարունի) was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 973 and 992. After a one-year vacancy due to a confusing period where there were two rival Catholicoi, King Ashot III "the Merciful" called an assembly to pick a new Catholicos. Khachik, a relative of the Catholicos Ananias was selected and was able to settle the problems which had arisen from the dueling Catholicoi and the schism it caused.
armenian:Khachig_I_of_Armenia.next: armenian:name:Sarkis I, d. aft. 1019 — Սարգիս Ա Սևանցի:992
armenian:Khachig_I_of_Armenia.nn: Sarkis I, d. aft. 1019 — Սարգիս Ա Սևանցի
ev: Viking raids from Scandinavia threaten the southern English coast after a pause of 25 years. Hampshire and the Isle of Thanet are ravaged.
Vikings
During this tenure

armenian:name:Sarkis I, d. aft. 1019 — Ս.n: Sarkis I, d. aft. 1019 — Սարգիս Ա Սևանցի
ev: Emperor Sheng Zong of Liao launches a major offensive against the Song dynasty. He invades Shanyang and threatens the Song capital of Kaifeng.
Emperor Shengzong of Liao
During this tenure

armenian:Peter_I_of_Armenia.bio: Peter I, known as Petros Getadardz (Պետրոս Ա. Գետադարձ) in Armenian, was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1019 and 1058. He was the brother of a former Catholicos Khachik I. He was the author of several works of sermons, anthems, and elegies on early Christian martyrs. Peter I played an important political role in the last years of Bagratid Armenia.
armenian:Peter_I_of_Armenia.prev: armenian:name:Sarkis I, d. aft. 1019 — Սարգիս Ա Սևանցի:992
armenian:Peter_I_of_Armenia.pn: Sarkis I, d. aft. 1019 — Սարգիս Ա Սևանցի
ev: Murder of the daughter of the late Japanese Emperor Kazan, a lady-in-waiting to Shōshi who orders an investigation.
Emperor Kazan
During this tenure
King's College, Cambridge, is founded by King Henry VI of England.
During this tenure
The Empire of Trebizond, the last major Romano-Greek outpost, falls to the Ottoman Empire under Mehmed II, after a 21-day siege.
Empire of Trebizond
During this tenure
News reaches the Republic of Venice that the Ottoman Sultan is marching toward Italy with an army of 100,000 men.
During this tenure

armenian:Sarkis_II_the_Relic-Carrier.bio: Sarkis II the Relic-Carrier was the Catholicos of Armenian Apostolic Church in 1469–1474.
ev: The Chimor–Inca War ends with an Inca victory. The Chimor Empire is absorbed into the Inca Empire.
Chimor–Inca War
During this tenure

The Treaty of Constantinople is signed between the Ottoman Empire and Republic of Venice, ending 16 years of war between the two powers; Venice will cede Negroponte, Lemnos and Shkodër, and pay an annual sum of 10,000 gold ducats.
During this tenure
The fifth parliament of England's King Henry VII opens at Westminster.
During this tenure
Battle of Ridaniya: The Ottoman army of sultan Selim I defeats the Mamluk army in Egypt, commanded by king Tuman Bay II.
During this tenure
Manco Inca Yupanqui is crowned as Sapa Inca in Cusco, Peru by Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro, in succession to his brother Túpac Huallpa.
Manco Inca Yupanqui
During this tenure

The siege of the island of Corfu is started by the Ottoman Empire Navy, commanded by Suleiman the Magnificent. Suleiman abandons the siege in September after an outbreak of plague, and the Ottoman troops return home.
During this tenure

armenian:Stepanos_V_of_Salmast.bio: Step'anos V of Salmast, otherwise known as Stepanos V Salmastetsi (b. ? Salmas – d. 1567 Etchmiadzin), was Catholicos of All Armenians from 1547 to 1567.
ev: Catherine Parr, the former Queen consort of England and widow of King Henry VIII, publishes her book The Lamentation of a Sinner.
During this tenure
The Ottoman conquest of Cyprus is concluded, by the surrender of Famagusta. Cyprus is established as an eyalet of the Ottoman Empire, and the first Turkish colony moves into the island.
During this tenure
Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire for more than 14 years, is assassinated in Constantinople.
During this tenure
The Safavid Empire of Persia and the Spanish Empire conclude a defensive alliance and declare war on the Ottoman Empire.
Safavid Empire
During this tenure

armenian:Movses_III_of_Armenia.bio: Movses III was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1629 and 1632. He was a pioneer of the reform movement within the church and his work was carried on by his successors. He also obtained protection from the Shah of Persia against local Muslim chieftains.
ev: The Italian plague of 1629–31 reaches Venice.
During this tenure
Battle of Liaoluo Bay: A large Ming dynasty fleet under Zheng Zhilong defeats a Dutch East India Company fleet at the island of Quemoy.
During this tenure
The magnitude 8.0 North Anatolia earthquake causes 8,000 deaths in northern Anatolia, Ottoman Empire, and is the most powerful earthquake recorded in Turkey.
During this tenure
Morean War – Battle on Vrtijeljka: Advancing Ottoman forces prevail over defending Venetian irregulars, on a hill in the Montenegro Vilayet.
During this tenure
Damat Hasan Pasha, Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire, is removed from office by Ottoman Sultan Ahmed III, and replaced by Kalaylikoz Ahmed Pasha.
During this tenure

armenian:Alexander_I_of_Julfa.bio: Catholicos Alexander I of New Julfa, Persia was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1706 and 1714. Alexander was from New Julfa of the Armenian community in Persia. Prior to his election as Catholicos of All Armenians, he served as Archbishop of New Julfa from 1699 to 1706.
ev: The ancient Roman Pillar of the Boatmen is found during the construction of a crypt under the nave of Notre-Dame de Paris.
During this tenure, at about age 60

armenian:Asdvadzadur_of_Armenia.bio: Asdvadzadur of Armenia was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church from 8 May 1715 to 1725. He was anointed in Etchmiadzin. As Catholicos, he secured an alliance with Peter the Great of Russia for aid against the expansionist Muslim powers of the Ottoman Empire and Persia prior to the Russo-Persian War. He is buried at St. Hripsime Church, Echmiadzin.
ev: Antonio Vivaldi's opera Tieteberga is performed for the first time, premiering at the Teatro San Moisè in Venice.
During this tenure, at about age 67

armenian:Karapet_II_of_Armenia.bio: Catholicos Karapet II Oolnetzi was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1726 and 1729. Because of grave political and military situation in Armenia, it was not possible to elect a new Catholicos of All Armenians in Etchmiadzin following death of Catholicos Asdvadzadur I of Armenia (in Armenian Աստվածատուր Ա Համադանցի).
ev: George Frideric Handel's famous opera Lotario is given its first performance, premiering at the King's Theatre in London.
During this tenure

armenian:Abraham_II_of_Armenia.bio: Catholicos Abraham II Khoshabetzi was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1730 and 1734.
ev: General Nader Khan of Persia opens the first campaign of the Ottoman–Persian War, guiding the Persian Army from Shiraz and starting the Western Persia Campaign against the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure, at about age 53

armenian:Abraham_III_of_Armenia.bio: Abraham III was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1734 and 1737. Born in Heraklion, Crete, to a Greek mother, he was bishop of Rodosto, Thrace and then Armenian prelate of Thrace in 1708–1734. At this time he went on a pilgrimage to eastern Armenia, at that time under Persian rule, which now make up the area of modern-day Armenia and Nakhichevan. Abraham is said to have become Catholicos by chance, because while he was on his pilgrimage to Etchmiadzin Catholicos Abraham II died.
ev: Alcina, George Frideric Handel's Italian opera, premieres at the Royal Opera House in Covent Garden, London.
During this tenure, at about age 35

armenian:Lazar_I_of_Armenia.bio: Catholicos Lazar I of Armenia was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1737 and 1751. He is notable for the numerous troubles he personally got into during his reign. Lazar had been bishop of Smyrna, Turkey and was a native of Jahuk. He was said to be beloved by his nation and many wanted him to be the Catholicos when Abraham III died, though another party supported Gregory the Armenian Patriarch of Jerusalem.
ev: The third French and Indian War, known as King George's War, breaks out at Annapolis Royal, Nova Scotia.
King George's War
During this tenure
The first presentation of a Shakespearean play in America is performed when a company of players stages The Merchant of Venice in Williamsburg, Virginia.
During this tenure
French and Indian War: Battle of Jumonville Glen – The war begins when George Washington, 22, leads a company of militia from the Colony of Virginia, in an ambush on a force of 35 French Canadians.
During this tenure
A steam engine is used in the American colonies for the first time as New Jersey copper mine owner Arent Schuyler installs a Newcomen atmospheric engine to pump water out of a mineshaft.
During this tenure
Exhibition of 1761, the inaugural exhibition of the Society of Artists of Great Britain opens at Spring Gardens in London.
During this tenure

armenian:Simeon_I_of_Yerevan.bio: Simeon I of Yerevan, also known as Simeon Yerevantsi, served as the Catholicos of All Armenians between 1763 and 1780. Before his pontificate, he served as a representative of Etchmiadzin in Constantinople, New Julfa, and Madras. After becoming catholicos in 1763, he took measures to reassert Etchmiadzin's primacy over other sees of the Armenian church.
ev: Mozart's Serenade No. 7 (the "Haffner") is first performed in Salzburg, Austria.
During this tenure, at about age 66

armenian:Ghukas_Karnetsi.bio: Ghukas Karnetsi (Armenian: Ղուկաս Կարնեցի, lit. 'Luke of Karin/Erzurum'; 1722 – 28 December 1799) was Catholicos of All Armenians (head of the Armenian Church) in Etchmiadzin from 1780 to 1799. He succeeded his former teacher Simeon of Yerevan and continued many of his policies. He was catholicos during a time of economic hardship and conflict in Iranian Armenia and appealed to the Russian Empire to take Armenians under its protection. He was careful not to worsen the church's relations with Muslim rulers.
ev: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, in Vienna, completes his penultimate symphony, the Symphony No. 40 in G Minor.
During this tenure, at about age 66

armenian:Hovsep_Arghutian_(bishop).bio: Hovsep Arghutian, known in Russian as Iosif Argutinsky-Dolgorukov, was an eighteenth-century Armenian archbishop who served as the religious leader of Armenians in the Russian Empire. He played a key role in the establishment of Armenian settlements in Russia, most notably that of Nakhichevan-on-Don. He co-founded the first Armenian press in Russia and directed its activities. He had a close personal relationship with Catherine the Great and Grigory Potemkin and advised them on Russia's policies in the Caucasus region.
ev: Ludwig van Beethoven's Symphony No. 1 premieres at the Burgtheater, in Vienna.
Ludwig van Beethoven
During this tenure, at about age 57
Battle of Eylau: Napoleon fights a hard but inconclusive battle against the Russians under Bennigsen.
During this tenure
Beethoven's Symphony No. 3, Eroica, has its public premiere at the Theater an der Wien in Vienna under his baton.
During this tenure
Battle of Aspern-Essling: Austrian troops under Archduke Karl beat the French under Napoleon, in a hard-fought battle.
During this tenure
Queen Victoria moves from Kensington Palace into Buckingham Palace, the first reigning British monarch to make this, rather than St James's Palace, as her London home.
During this tenure

armenian:Nerses_V.bio: Nerses V of Ashtarak served as the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1843 and 1857. Previously, he served as the leader of the Diocese of Georgia from 1811 to 1830 and as the leader of the Diocese of Bessarabia and Nor Nakhichevan from 1830 to 1843. Nerses V is buried near Mother Cathedral of Holy Etchmiadzin.
ev: Giuseppe Verdi's opera Rigoletto is first performed at La Fenice in Venice.
During this tenure, at about age 81
Ottoman Penal Code decriminalized homosexual sex between consenting adults in the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure
The Lincoln County War begins in Lincoln County, New Mexico.
During this tenure
St Cuthbert's Society at the University of Durham in England is founded, after a general meeting chaired by the Reverend Hastings Rashdall.
During this tenure

armenian:Mkrtich_Khrimian.bio: Mkrtich Khrimian was an Armenian Apostolic Church leader, educator, and publisher who served as Catholicos of All Armenians from 1893 to 1907. During this period he was known as Mkrtich I of Van (Մկրտիչ Ա Վանեցի, Mkrtich A Vanetsi). A native of Van, one of the largest cities in Turkish (Western) Armenia, Khrimian became a celibate priest (vardapet) in 1854 after the death of his wife and daughter. In the 1850s and 1860s he served as the abbot of two important monasteries in Turkish Armenia: Varagavank near Van and Surb Karapet Monastery near Mush.
ev: The first modern Olympic Games are held in Athens.
1896 Summer Olympics
During this tenure, at about age 76

armenian:Matthew_II_Izmirlian.bio: Matthew II Izmirlian (Armenian: Մատթէոս Բ. Կոնստանդնուպոլսեցի (Իզմիրլեան), Matthew II of Constantinople; 22 February 1845 – 11 December 1910) was the Catholicos of All Armenians of the Armenian Apostolic Church at the Mother See of Holy Etchmiadzin in 1908–1910. He succeeded Mkrtich I Khrimian (better known as Khrimian Hayrik), who reigned as Catholicos from 1892 to 1907.
ev: French aviator Henri Farman makes the world's first flight with a passenger, Léon Delagrange.
During this tenure, at about age 63

armenian:Gevorg_V_of_Armenia.bio: Gevorg V of Armenia (in Armenian Գևորգ Ե. Սուրենյանց (Տփղիսեցի) (28 August 1847 – 8 May 1930) was the Catholicos of All Armenians of the Armenian Apostolic Church in the Mother See of Holy Etchmiadzin from 1911–1930. He succeeded Catholicos Matthew II (in Armenian Մատթեոս Բ Կոստանդնուպոլսեց), who had died on 11 December 1910 after less than three years as Catholicos.
ev: First Balkan War: Battle of Bizani – Forces of the Kingdom of Greece capture the forts of Bizani (covering the approaches to Ioannina) from the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure, at about age 66

armenian:Khoren_I_of_Armenia.bio: Khoren I Muradbekian was an Armenian Apostolic religious figure who served as Catholicos of All Armenians from 1932 until his murder in 1938. He previously served as locum tenens, between 1923 and 1932, in the latter years of and after the death of Catholicos Gevorg V, and bishop of Yerevan from 1910 to 1924. Khoren I died in mysterious circumstances at the Pontifical Residence in Etchmiadzin. The Armenian Church and most historians believe he was murdered by the NKVD, the Soviet secret police.
ev: The world's first regular television program (by Fernsehsender Paul Nipkow) is transmitted from the Funkturm in Berlin, Germany.
During this tenure, at about age 62

armenian:Gevorg_VI_of_Armenia.bio: Gevorg VI of Armenia (Armenian: Գևորգ Զ. Չորեքչյան (Նորնախիջևանցի), Kevork VI Cheorekjian; December 2, 1868 – May 9, 1954) was the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church from 1945 to 1954. The position had remained vacant from 1938 to 1945 following the Stalinist-era purges against organized religion, culminating in the murder of the then catholicos Khoren I in 1938. Etchmiadzin was ordered closed and the position of Catholicos of All Armenians remained vacant for seven years.
ev: The Miss America Pageant is broadcast on television for the first time.
During this tenure, at about age 86

armenian:Vazgen_I.bio: Vazgen I also Vazken I of Bucharest, born Levon Garabed Baljian was the Catholicos of All Armenians between 1955 and 1994. Serving for a total of 39 years, his tenure as Catholicos was the fourth longest in the history of the Armenian Apostolic Church. A native of Romania, Vazgen began his career as a philosopher, before becoming a Doctor of Theology and a member of the local Armenian clergy. The leader of the Armenian Apostolic Church hierarchy in Romania, he became Catholicos in 1955, moving to Soviet Armenia.
ev: Apollo program: Apollo 11 (Buzz Aldrin, Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins) lifts off from Cape Kennedy in Florida towards the first crewed landing on the Moon.
During this tenure, at about age 61

armenian:Karekin_I.bio: Karekin I served as the Catholicos of the Armenian Apostolic Church between 1994 and 1999. Previously, he served as the Catholicos of Cilicia from 1983 to 1994 as Karekin II (Armenian: Գարեգին Բ).
ev: IBM's Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov in the last game of the rematch, the first time a computer beats a chess World champion in a match.
During this tenure, at about age 65

armenian:Karekin_II.bio: Catholicos Garegin II is the Catholicos of All Armenians, the supreme head of the Armenian Apostolic Church, since 1999. In 2013 he was unanimously elected the Oriental Orthodox head of the World Council of Churches for the next eight years.
ev: A rare conjunction of seven celestial bodies (Sun, Moon, planets Mercury–Saturn) occurs during the new moon.
celestial bodies
During this tenure, at about age 49

ethiopian:Frumentius.bio: Frumentius was a Phoenician Christian missionary and the first bishop of Axum who brought Christianity to the Kingdom of Aksum. He is sometimes known by other names, such as Abuna ("Our Father") and Aba Selama ("Father of Peace"). He was a native of Phoenicia, born in Tyre, modern day Lebanon. As a boy, he was captured with his brother on a voyage, and they became slaves to the King of Axum. He freed them shortly before his death, and they were invited to educate his young heir. They also began to teach Christianity in the region.
ev: The Alamanni cross the Rhine and invade Gaul. Emperor Valentinian I moves to Paris to command the army and defend the Gallic cities.
During this tenure, at about age 55

ethiopian:Abuna_Yohannes.bio: Abuna Yohannes was an Abuna, or head of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church in the 14th century, during the reign of Emperor Amda Seyon. He was accused of simony by a group of Ethiopian clergy at the Royal Court. During this period the Abun was appointed by the Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of All Africa, who had diocesan authority over Ethiopia and the rest of Africa, at the request of the Emperor of Ethiopia, usually after paying a substantial fee to the Muslim government for the privilege.
ev: The Stone of Destiny, an oblong block of red sandstone, is placed at Scone Palace for the coronation of the first monarchs of Scotland.
Stone of Scone
During this tenure

ethiopian:Abuna_Sawiros.bio: Abuna Sawiros was an Abuna, or head of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church in the 11th century. During this period the Abun was appointed by the Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of All Africa, who had diocesan authority over Ethiopia, at the request of the Emperor of Ethiopia, usually after paying a substantial fee to the Muslim government for the privilege. Pope Cyril II intended to appoint one candidate, but Badr al-Jamali, the Vizier of Caliph Al-Mustansir, forced him to ordain Sawiros instead.
ev: The University of Bologna is founded.
University of Bologna
During this tenure
Muqali (or Mukhali), a Mongol general in service of Genghis Khan, is rewarded with the command of the left-wing of the newly reorganized Mongol army and takes control over the eastern Mingghans.
Muqali
During this tenure
Reconquista: The city of Alcácer do Sal, located along the Sado River, is conquered from the Moors by troops of King Afonso II of Portugal.
During this tenure
The Teutonic Knights are expelled from Transylvania by King Andrew II, because they wanted to separate from Hungary.
Teutonic Order
During this tenure
The Queen's College, a constituent college of the University of Oxford in England, is founded.
During this tenure
The Kingdom of France and the Crown of Castile defeat the Kingdom of England in the Battle of La Rochelle, and France gains control of the English Channel for the first time since 1340.
During this tenure

ethiopian:Bartalomewos_II_of_Ethiopia.bio: Bartalomewos of Ethiopia was an Abuna, or head of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church from 1398/99 to sometime after 1434; he succeeded Abuna Salama II. His tenure was a period marked by a series of doctrinal disputes in the Church, and at one point Bartalomewos was accused of denying the threefold nature of the Holy Trinity. Emperor Yeshaq appointed a committee to investigate this serious charge, whose members included graduates of the school at Istifanos Monastery in Lake Hayq.
ev: Following the Venetian Navy triumph over the Ottomans at Gallipoli, Dolfino Venier, the Republic of Venice's ambassador to the Ottoman Empire, reaches an agreement with the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed I to begin discussing a treaty.
During this tenure
Peace between Albania and Venice is established, bringing an end to the Albanian–Venetian War.
During this tenure
On his second voyage to the New World, Columbus and his crew become the first Europeans to sail into what is now Guantanamo Bay in Cuba.
During this tenure
King Henry VIII of England concludes an independent peace treaty with France in the War of the League of Cambrai, negotiated by Thomas Wolsey.
During this tenure
Suleiman the Magnificent, the Ottoman Sultan, begins the siege of the city of Esztergom in Hungary.
Suleiman the Magnificent
During this tenure
King Henry VIII opens the Parliament of England for the ninth time, in a session that lasts until December 24.
During this tenure

ethiopian:Andrés_de_Oviedo.bio: Andrés de Oviedo, also known as Andre da Oviedo, was a Spanish Jesuit missionary and Patriarch of Ethiopia. Oviedo was born in Illescas, Toledo. On 19 June 1541, while in Rome, he entered the Society of Jesus, nine months after it was approved by Pope Paul III. In autumn of that year he travelled to Paris, where he studied theology, although his studies were interrupted by the war between France and Spain, so he continued studying in Louvain, completing in 1544.
ev: Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville's play Gorboduc is performed for the first time, before Queen Elizabeth I of England. It is the first known English tragedy, and the first English language play to employ blank verse.
Thomas Norton
During this tenure, at about age 44
The Mariovo and Prilep rebellion occurs, the very first recorded rebellion by the Macedonian hajduks or voivode against the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure
A truce is signed between representatives of the Holy Roman Empire (ruled by Emperor Rudolf II) and the Ottoman Empire (ruled by Sultan Murad III).
During this tenure

ethiopian:Abuna_Petros_VII.bio: Abuna Petros VII was a cleric of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church who served as Abuna of Ethiopia from 1881 to 1889. He served during the reign of Emperor Yohannes IV (r. 1871–1889), a period during which the Ethiopian Church maintained traditional ecclesiastical ties with the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria and sought to strengthen episcopal leadership following years of instability.
ev: The first recorded performance of William Shakespeare's tragedy, Othello, takes place at the Palace of Whitehall in London.
During this tenure
August 15 (August 5 O.S.) – English astronomer Thomas Harriot becomes the first person to make a detailed drawing of the Moon, based on his observations through a telescope.
During this tenure

ethiopian:Afonso_Mendes.bio: Father Afonso Mendes was a Portuguese Jesuit theologian, and Patriarch of Ethiopia from 1622 to 1634. While E. A. Wallis Budge has expressed the commonly accepted opinion of this man, as being "rigid, uncompromising, narrow-minded, and intolerant", there are some who disagree with it. The writings of Mendes include Expeditionis Aethiopicae, which describes the customs and conditions of Ethiopia.
ev: In an invasion of Persia, Ottoman Empire Grand Vizier Gazi Hüsrev Pasha routs the Persians in a battle at Mahidasht near Kermanshah.
During this tenure, at about age 51
The Treaty of Polyanovka is signed between the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Tsardom of Russia, concluding the Smolensk War.
During this tenure
Charles II of England is defeated in the Battle of Worcester, the last major battle of the English Civil War, and forced to flee.
During this tenure
England's first chocolate house is opened in London and introduction of tea in England while coffee is introduced to France.
Tea in the United Kingdom
During this tenure
The Treaty of Bakhchisarai is signed, between the Ottoman vassal Crimean Khanate and the Russian Empire.
During this tenure
The Ottoman siege of Vienna is broken.
Battle of Vienna
During this tenure
The Holy Roman Empire wins the Battle of Niš, fought against the Ottoman Empire during the Great Turkish War in modern-day Serbia.
During this tenure
The first performance of Francesco Gasparini's most famous opera Tamerlano takes place at the Teatro San Cassiano in Venice.
During this tenure

November 15 (November 4 O.S.) – Russia's Emperor Peter the Great issues an order establishing the Caspian Flotilla during its war against Persia to gain complete control of the landlocked Caspian Sea.
During this tenure
Seven Years' War – Battle of Bernetz Brook: British troops defeat the French.
Seven Years' War
During this tenure

War of the First Coalition: Napoleon Bonaparte conquers Venice, ending the city and Republic of Venice's 1,100 years of independence. The last doge of Venice, Ludovico Manin, steps down. The Venetian Ghetto is thrown open.
During this tenure
Emperor Napoleon I joins the French army in Spain. He takes command to restore French authority after early disasters.
During this tenure
