ethiopian:Abuna_Qerellos_III.bio: Qerellos III was an Abuna, or head of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. In the words of Richard Pankhurst, "A controversial figure, he is reputed to have been fanatical and rapacious."
ev: Greek War of Independence – Chios massacre: 20,000 Greeks on the island of Chios are slaughtered by Ottoman troops, and 23,000 more are exiled.
During this tenure
Giuseppe Verdi's opera Il Trovatore premieres at Teatro Apollo in Rome.
During this tenure
New Constitution of the Ottoman Empire signed, ending Tanzimat in the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure

ethiopian:Abuna_Mattheos_X.bio: Abuna Mattheos X was a Coptic priest from Egypt, who came to Ethiopia in 1881, becoming a bishop of Shewa under King Sahle Mariam. When Sahle Mariam became the Emperor of Ethiopia under the regnal name Menelik II in 1889, Mattheos then became Archbishop of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church until his death. In 1916, on behalf of the Ethiopian church, Mattheos announced the dethronement and excommunication of the uncrowned Emperor of Ethiopia Lij Iyasu (Iyasu V), who reportedly converted to Islam.
ev: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed VI's representatives sign the Treaty of Sèvres with the Allied Powers, confirming arrangements for the partitioning of the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure, at about age 77

ethiopian:Abuna_Qerellos_IV.bio: Abuna Qerellos IV was a Coptic priest from Egypt, who came to Ethiopia in 1926, becoming the Archbishop of Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. Except for a break between 1936 and 1945 (including the Fascist Italian occupation between 1936 and 1941, following the Second Italo-Ethiopian War) which he spent in exile, Qerellos remained the head of the Ethiopian church until his death. Qerellos was the last Archbishop of Ethiopia of foreign descent.
ev: Japan renounces the Washington Naval Treaty of 1922 and the London Naval Treaty of 1930.
During this tenure, at about age 54

ethiopian:Abuna_Abraham.bio: Abuna Abraham was a cleric of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, who was installed as the archbishop of the Ethiopian church during the Fascist Italian occupation following the Second Italo-Ethiopian War, in place of the legitimate Archbishop Abuna Qerellos IV. On 27 November 1937, Marshal Rodolfo Graziani convened an assembly of Ethiopian clergymen to elect a new archbishop. Abuna Abraham, bishop of Gojjam, was elected.
ev: The Pan American Airways Boeing 314 flying boat Yankee Clipper inaugurates the world's first heavier-than-air North Atlantic air passenger service, between the United States (Port Washington, New York) and Britain.
During this tenure

ethiopian:Abuna_Yohannes_XV.bio: Abuna Yohannes XV was a cleric of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church who served as Abuna of Ethiopia from 1939 to 1945, during the final years of the Fascist Italian occupation of Ethiopia and the early restoration of imperial rule under Emperor Haile Selassie.
ev: The live blues radio program King Biscuit Time is broadcast for the first time on KFFA in Helena, Arkansas; it will attain its 17,000th broadcast in 2014 making it the longest-running daily American radio broadcast.
During this tenure

ethiopian:Abuna_Basilios.bio: Abuna Basilios was an Ethiopian Orthodox prelate who served as the first Archbishop of Ethiopia, and later the first patriarch of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.
ev: Atlantic College opens its doors for the first time in Wales, marking the birth of the pioneering United World College educational movement.
During this tenure, at about age 71

ethiopian:Abuna_Theophilos.bio: Abuna Theophilos, also known as Abune Tewophilos, was the second Patriarch of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. He officially succeeded Abuna Basilios in 1971 after he had assumed the role of acting patriarch upon Abuna Basilios's death in 1970. - and through dedicated service to his church he ultimately became a martyr for his faith.
ev: The Suez Canal opens for the first time since the Six-Day War.
During this tenure, at about age 65

ethiopian:Abuna_Takla_Haymanot.bio: Abuna Takla Haymanot was the third Patriarch of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church from 1976 to 1988. After political turmoil of the Ethiopian Revolution, the Derg arrested Abuna Theophilos in May 1976 to consecrate Melaku. The government proceeded to hold church assembly to elect the bahtawi (hermit) Melaku that has little education around the subject.
ev: Viking program: Viking 2 enters into orbit around Mars.
During this tenure, at about age 59

ethiopian:Abune_Merkorios.bio: Abune Merkorios was an Ethiopian bishop and the fourth Patriarch of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, elected after the death of Abuna Takla Haymanot in May 1988. Merkorios remained Patriarch for three years until 1991, when the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) overthrew the Communist military junta known as Derg in Addis Ababa. After spending almost three decades living in exile, he was allowed to return to Addis Ababa and be recognized as Patriarch alongside Abune Mathias.
ev: NASA's Kepler space telescope mission ends after the spacecraft runs out of fuel.
During this tenure, at about age 80

ethiopian:Abune_Paulos.bio: Abune Paulos was the fifth Patriarch of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church from 1992 to his death in 2012. His full title was "His Holiness Abuna Paulos, Fifth Patriarch of the Orthodox Tewahido Church of Ethiopia, Ichege of the see of Saint Tekle Haymanot, Archbishop of Axum and one of the seven serving Presidents of the World Council of Churches."
ev: A Russian air base opens in Kant, Kyrgyzstan, as Russia's first foreign air base since the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
Kant (air base)
During this tenure, at about age 68

ethiopian:Abune_Mathias.bio: Abune Mathias I is the sixth and current Patriarch of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church since 2013. His full title is "His Holiness Abune Mathias I, Sixth Patriarch and Catholicos of Ethiopia, Archbishop of Axum and Ichege of the See of Saint Taklehaimanot".
ev: Cinemas open in Saudi Arabia for the first time since 1983 with the American film Black Panther chosen as the first to be screened.
Saudi Arabia
During this tenure, at about age 77

moscow:Peter_of_Moscow.bio: Peter of Moscow was an Eastern Orthodox bishop of Kiev, who moved his see from Vladimir to Moscow in 1325. Later he was proclaimed a patron saint of Moscow. In spite of the move, the office remained officially entitled "Metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus'" until the autocephalous election of Jonah in 1448.
ev: Mongol Prince Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan becomes the ruler of the Ilkhanate, the Mongol-controlled area of the Middle East.
During this tenure, at about age 57
A severe Bubonic Plague epidemic begins in the Crimea, marking the first major epidemic of the Black Death.
Bubonic plague
During this tenure

moscow:Alexius,_Metropolitan_of_Kiev.bio: Alexius was Metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus' from 1354. He presided over the Muscovite government during Dmitrii Donskoi's minority.
ev: In the Battle of Pontvallain, fought in the Hundred Years' War, a French army under Bertrand du Guesclin heavily defeats an English force in surprise attacks in northwest France.
During this tenure, at about age 80
Battle of the Vozha River: Prince Dmitri Ivanovich of Moscow resists a small invasion by the Mongol Blue Horde under Mamai.
During this tenure

moscow:Cyprian,_Metropolitan_of_Kiev.o: Primate of the Russian Church · 2 terms
moscow:Cyprian,_Metropolitan_of_Kiev.bio: Cyprian was a prelate of Bulgarian origin, who served as the Metropolitan of Kiev, Rus' and Lithuania and the Metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus' in the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople. During both periods, he was opposed by rival hierarchs and by the grand prince of Moscow. He was known as a bright opinion writer, editor, translator, and book copyist. He is commemorated by the Russian Orthodox Church on May 27 and September 16 (O.S.).
ev: Turko-Mongol Emperor Timur sacks Damascus.
During this tenure, at about age 65

moscow:Pimen,_Metropolitan_of_Kiev.bio: Pimen was the Metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus' from June 1380 until he was deposed in 1384. At the same time, Cyprian, Metropolitan of Kiev was alive and claimed the same title.
ev: Construction of the Bastille fortress is completed in Paris, France.
Bastille
During this tenure, at about age 79

moscow:Dionysius,_Metropolitan_of_Kiev.bio: Saint Dionysius I was the metropolitan of the Russian Orthodox Church from 1384 to 1385.
ev: At the age of 10, Jadwiga is crowned "King" of Poland in Kraków following the 1382 death of her father, King Louis of Hungary.
During this tenure, at about age 84

moscow:Photius_(Metropolitan_of_Kiev_and.bio: Photius was Metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus'. He was of Greek descent.
moscow:Photius_(Metropolitan_of_Kiev_and.w: Photius (Metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus')
ev: The Ottoman Army defeats a rebellion, led by Miklós Csáki, Voivode of Transylvania. Two days later, the Ottoman troops loot and burn the city of Orăștie and take thousands of Transylvanian civilians as slaves.
During this tenure, at about age 70
The Ming Chinese expedition departs from Hormuz Island and begins its four-month voyage home to Beijing.
During this tenure

moscow:Isidore_of_Kiev.bio: Isidore or Isidor of Kiev, also known as Isidore of Thessalonica, was a prelate of Byzantine Greek origin. From 1437 to 1441, he served as the metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus', based in Moscow, after being chosen by Joseph II of Constantinople. As a supporter of the union with Rome, he left Moscow to attend the Council of Ferrara–Florence. On his return in 1441, he was imprisoned but allowed to escape later that year.
ev: Hundred Years War: Paris is recaptured from the English by French forces.
During this tenure, at about age 56

moscow:Jonah_of_Moscow.bio: Jonah of Moscow was Metropolitan of Kiev and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1448 until his death in 1461. After Isidore was condemned for supporting the Union of Florence, Jonah was appointed as metropolitan by a council of Russian bishops at the behest of Vasily II of Moscow. Like his immediate predecessors, he permanently resided in Moscow, and was the last Moscow-based metropolitan to keep the traditional title with reference to the metropolitan city of Kiev.
ev: At the Battle of Oranik, Albanian forces led by Skanderbeg defeat the armies of the Republic of Venice and the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure, at about age 58

moscow:Theodosius,_Metropolitan_of_Mosco.bio: Theodosius Byvaltsev was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1461 to 1464. He was the second metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: King Edward IV summons the English Parliament for the first time, directing the members of the House of Lords and House of Commons to assemble at Westminster on November 4.
During this tenure, at about age 111

moscow:Philip_I,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Philip I was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1464 to 1473. He was the third metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: The siege of Jajce in Bosnia, a strategic fortress under the control of Hungary, is started by the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II with 30,000 troops under his command.
During this tenure

moscow:Gerontius,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Gerontius was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1473 until 1489. He was the fourth metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: At the Battle of Otlukbeli, Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II defeats the White Sheep Turkmens, led by Uzun Hasan.
During this tenure, at about age 23
John Corvinus, son of the late King Matthias Corvinus of Hungary and a claimant to the throne, is defeated by the Kingdom of Hungary at the Battle of Bonefield.
During this tenure

moscow:Simon,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Simon was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1495 to 1511. He was the sixth metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: King Henry VII of England summons the English Parliament for the first time in more than three years, directing the members of the House of Commons and the House of Lords to assemble at Westminster on October 14.
During this tenure, at about age 45

moscow:Varlaam,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Varlaam was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1511 to 1521. He was the seventh metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: The Treaty of Westminster creates an alliance between Henry VIII of England and Ferdinand II of Aragon against France. Mallett and Shaw, The Italian Wars, 103; Hutchinson, Young Henry, 159.
During this tenure, at about age 70

moscow:Daniel,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Daniel was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1522 to 1539. He was the eighth metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm. He represented the belligerent ecclesiastic circle that was interested in alliance with the princely authority.
ev: Chinese Ming dynasty War Ministry official He Ru is the first to acquire the Portuguese breech-loading culverin, while copies of them are made by two Westernized Chinese at Beijing, Yang San (Pedro Yang) and Dai Ming.
Ming dynasty
During this tenure, at about age 30

moscow:Joasaphus,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Joasaphus Skripitsyn was the Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', serving as the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church from 1539 to 1542. He was the ninth metropolitan in Moscow appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, a break from the earlier tradition that had required such information. Joasaph is known to have authored a number of theological works.
ev: The first printing press in North America is set up in Mexico City.
North America
During this tenure, at about age 89

moscow:Macarius,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Macarius was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1542 to 1563. He was the tenth metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: Antoine Escalin des Eymars, the French ambassador, returns from Constantinople, with promises of Ottoman aid in a war against Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor.
During this tenure, at about age 60

moscow:Athanasius,_Metropolitan_of_Mosco.bio: Athanasius was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from March 1564 to May 1566. He was the eleventh metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: Livonian War – Battle of Ula: A Lithuanian surprise attack results in a decisive defeat of the numerically superior Russian forces.
During this tenure, at about age 14

moscow:Herman_of_Kazan_and_Svyazhsk.bio: Archbishop Herman, born Grigory Fyodorovich Sadyrev-Polev, was the archbishop of Kazan from 1564 to 1567. He was also a candidate for the position of metropolitan of Moscow. He died in Moscow and was buried in the Church of Saint Nicholas the Hospitable.
ev: The siege of Szigetvár is begun by Suleiman the Magnificent, Sultan of the Ottoman Empire. This is the Ottoman Empire at its greatest extent.
During this tenure, at about age 61

moscow:Philip_II,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Saint Philip II of Moscow was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1566 to 1568. He was the thirteenth metropolitan of Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm. He was one of a few metropolitans who dared to openly contradict Ivan the Terrible. It is widely believed that the tsar had him murdered on that account. He is venerated as a saint and martyr in the Eastern Orthodox Church.
ev: John Sigismund Zápolya, uncrowned claimant to the throne of the King of Hungary, leads an invasion of Upper Hungary on the orders of Ottoman Sultan Suleiman.
During this tenure, at about age 59

moscow:Cyril,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Cyril IV was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1568 to 1572. He was the fourteenth metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: Mary, Queen of Scots, flees across the Solway Firth from Scotland to England but on May 19 is placed in custody in Carlisle Castle on the orders of Queen Elizabeth I, her cousin.
During this tenure, at about age 76

moscow:Anthony,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Anthony was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1572 to 1581. He was the fifteenth metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: August 2 – Battle of Molodi: A large Crimean–Ottoman army which invaded Russia is routed.
During this tenure, at about age 71

moscow:Dionysius,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow.bio: Dionysius was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1581 to 1587. He was the sixteenth metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm.
ev: The army of King Stephen Báthory of Poland begins its siege of the Russian garrison of Pskov.
During this tenure, at about age 76

moscow:Patriarch_Job_of_Moscow.o: Primate of the Russian Church · 2 terms
moscow:Patriarch_Job_of_Moscow.bio: Job was Metropolitan of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church, from 1587 to 1589, and the first Patriarch of Moscow and all Rus' from 1589 to 1605. He was the seventeenth metropolitan in Moscow to be appointed without the approval of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as had been the norm. In 1589, Jeremias II, the patriarch of Constantinople, regularized Job's canonical status and raised him to the status of patriarch. 400 years later, the Russian Orthodox Church canonized him in 1989.
ev: A severe famine breaks out in Ming dynasty China.
Ming dynasty
During this tenure, at about age 62

moscow:Ignatius_of_Moscow.bio: Ignatius was a Russian Orthodox bishop of Greek descent who was the second Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia in 1605–1606, even though his status is now disputed and he is frequently omitted from the list of Patriarchs of Moscow by the Russian Orthodox Church. Ignatius was reported to be of Cretan descent. He came to Russia in 1595 as a member of an ecclesiastic mission, sent by the Patriarch of Constantinople. He took part in the coronation of Boris Godunov. In the early 17th century, Ignatius was appointed Archbishop of Ryazan.
ev: Tokugawa Ieyasu abdicates as shogun of Japan, becoming Ogosho (retired shogun). His son Tokugawa Hidetada succeeds him to the office.
Tokugawa Ieyasu
During this tenure, at about age 65

moscow:Patriarch_Hermogenes_of_Moscow.bio: Hermogenes, or Germogen was the Patriarch of Moscow and all Russia from 1606. It was he who inspired the popular uprising that put an end to the Time of Troubles. Hermogenes was glorified by the Russian Orthodox Church in 1913. At the Holy Synod of 1589, which established the patriarchy in Moscow, Hermogenes was appointed Metropolitan of the newly conquered city of Kazan. During the following two decades, he gained renown for a number of Muslim Volga Tatars converted to Eastern Orthodoxy.
ev: William Shakespeare's play King Lear is given its first recorded performance, staged at the Palace of Whitehall.
During this tenure, at about age 76

moscow:Patriarch_Filaret_of_Moscow.bio: Feodor Nikitich Romanov (Russian: Фео́дор Ники́тич Рома́нов, IPA: [ˈfʲɵdər nʲɪˈkʲitʲɪtɕ rɐˈmanəf]; 1553 – 1 October [O.S. 21 September] 1633) was a Russian boyar who after temporary disgrace rose to become patriarch of Moscow as Filaret (Russian: Филаре́т, IPA: [fʲɪɫɐˈrʲet]), and became de facto ruler of Russia during the reign of his son, Mikhail Feodorovich.
ev: In Jamestown, Virginia, the first English-speaking representative assembly in the Americas, the Virginia General Assembly (later named House of Burgesses), convenes for the first time.
During this tenure, at about age 66

moscow:Patriarch_Joasaphus_I_of_Moscow.bio: Joasaphus I (Russian: Иоасаф I, romanized: Ioasaf I; ? – 28 November 1640, Moscow) was the fifth Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia (1634–1640).
ev: Rebel Scots and Irish soldiers assassinate Bohemian military leader Albrecht von Wallenstein at Cheb.
During this tenure, at about age 44

moscow:Patriarch_Joseph_of_Moscow.bio: Joseph (Russian: Иосиф; secular name Ignaty Dyakov, Russian: Игнатий Дьяков; died 15 April [O.S. 5 April] 1652) was the sixth Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia, elected after an unusual one and a half year break.
ev: Irish Rebellion of 1641: The citizens of Galway seize an English naval ship and close the town gates in support of the rebellion.
During this tenure, at about age 37

moscow:Patriarch_Nikon_of_Moscow.bio: Nikon, born Nikita Minin (Никита Минин; 7 May [O.S. 27 April] 1605 – 17 August [O.S. 7 August] 1681) was the seventh Patriarch of Moscow and all Rus' of the Russian Orthodox Church, serving officially from 1652 to 1666. He was renowned for his eloquence, energy, piety and close ties to Tsar Alexis of Russia. Nikon introduced many reforms, including liturgical reforms that were unpopular among conservatives. These divisions eventually led to a lasting schism known as Raskol (schism) in the Russian Orthodox Church.
ev: The First Anglo-Dutch War begins formally as the English Commonwealth declares war against the Dutch Republic.
During this tenure, at about age 47
In the Battle of Rio Nuevo, part of the Anglo-Spanish War, a Spanish invasion force fails to recapture Jamaica from the English.
During this tenure

moscow:Patriarch_Joasaphus_II_of_Moscow.bio: Joasaph II was Patriarch of Moscow and all Rus' from 1667 until his death five years and one day later in 1672. Joasaph was archimandrite of the Rozhdestvenskii (Nativity) Monastery in Vladimir from 1654 to April 25, 1656, when he was named archimandrite of the Trinity-St. Sergius Lavra. In 1666, he was a member of the court that tried Patriarch Nikon and deposed him, although it also approved his reforms that had led to the Old Believer Schism. On February 10, 1667, Joasaph was elected patriarch.
ev: Louis XIV of France abolishes the livre parisis (Paris pound), in favor of the much more widely used livre tournois (Tours pound). He also designates Gabriel Nicolas de la Reynie as the first chief of "police" of Paris.
During this tenure, at about age 76

moscow:Patriarch_Pitirim_of_Moscow.bio: Pitirim of Krutitsy was the ninth Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia. When Nikon held the post of patriarch, Pitirim was a metropolitan of Krutitsy. When Nikon willfully left the altar, Pitirim became his deputy and acted on his own as a real patriarch without even dealing with Nikon. When an ecumenical council gathered for hearing of Nikon's case, Pitirim was one of his most bitter opponents and accusers, probably, hoping to fill his post after his official deposition. Pitirim didn't succeed, however, because the council chose Joasaphus II over him.
ev: The Royal Society of London for Improving Natural Knowledge, national science academy for England, elects Isaac Newton to its membership, and then demonstrates Newton's reflecting telescope to King Charles II.
During this tenure, at about age 22

moscow:Patriarch_Joachim_of_Moscow.bio: Patriarch Joachim was the eleventh Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia, an opponent of the Raskol, and a founder of the Slavic Greek Latin Academy. Born Ivan Petrovich Savelov (Иван Петрович Савелов) also in some other sources as Ivan Petrovich Savyolov, Joachim was of noble origin. When his family died in the 1654 epidemic, he became a monk and served in various monasteries, including the Mezhyhirya Monastery near Kyiv. He received the religious name Joachim upon his tonsure.
ev: The tragic opera Alceste, by Jean-Baptiste Lully, is performed for the first time, presented by the Paris Opera company at the Theatre du Palais-Royal in Paris.
During this tenure, at about age 53

moscow:Patriarch_Adrian_of_Moscow.bio: Patriarch Adrian was the last pre-revolutionary Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia. According to historian Alexander Avdeyev, the future Patriarch Adrian was born in the last days of September 1638. The years 1627, 1637 and 1639 given in the literature are incorrect. October 2, named as his birthday, is most likely the day of his baptism. Adrian's life path before being appointed Archimandrite of the Chudov Monastery remains unknown.
ev: The opera Orphée by Louis Lully receives its first performance at the Académie Royale de Musique (the Paris Opera).
During this tenure, at about age 52

moscow:Stefan_Yavorsky.o: Primate of the Russian Church · 2 terms
moscow:Stefan_Yavorsky.bio: Stefan Yavorsky, born Simeon Ivanovich Yavorsky (1658 – 8 December [O.S. 27 November] 1722), was an archbishop and statesman in the Russian Empire and the first president of the Most Holy Synod.
ev: Peter the Great proclaims the Russian Empire.
Russian Empire
During this tenure, at about age 63

moscow:Theophan_Prokopovich.bio: Theophan or Feofan Prokopovich (Russian: Феофан Прокопович; Ukrainian: Феофан Прокопович, romanized: Feofan Prokopovych; 18 June [O.S. 8 June] 1681 – 19 September [O.S. 8 September] 1736) was a Russian Orthodox bishop, theologian, pietist, writer, poet, mathematician, astronomer, pedagogue and philosopher of Ukrainian origin. He was the rector of the Academia Mohileana in Kiev (1711–1716), the bishop of Pskov (1718–1725), and the archbishop of Novgorod (1725–1736).
ev: July 26 (July 15 O.S.) – The Russo-Persian War begins with Peter the Great's Persian campaign.
During this tenure, at about age 41
George Frideric Handel's oratorio The Messiah is first performed, in Dublin, Ireland in aid of local charities.
During this tenure
War of Jenkins' Ear – Battle of Havana: a British Caribbean squadron engages a Spanish squadron based near Havana.
During this tenure
The Treaty of Westminster is signed between Great Britain and Prussia, guaranteeing the neutrality of the Electorate of Hanover, controlled by King George II of Great Britain.
During this tenure

France and Austria sign a second Treaty of Versailles, committing France to sending an additional 105,000 troops to the war against Prussia, and to pay expenses to Austria at the rate of 12 million florins annually.
During this tenure

moscow:Ambrose_of_Moscow.bio: Ambrose of Moscow also known as Ambrosius of Moscow was Archbishop of Moscow who met an untimely death in the hands of a berserk crowd of religious fanatics during the Moscow plague riot of 1771. Andrey Sertis-Kamensky was born at Nezhin in the government of Chernihiv and studied in the school of St. Alexander Nevsky, where he afterward became a tutor. At the age of thirty-one, he entered a monastery, where he took the name of Ambrose. Subsequently, he was appointed archimandrite of the convent of New Jerusalem at Voskresensk.
ev: The Sultan Mustafa III of the Ottoman Empire begins the Russo-Turkish War after the Russians refuse to withdraw troops from Poland.
During this tenure, at about age 60
June 20 (June 9 O.S.) – Russo-Turkish War: Battle of Kozludzha – The Imperial Russian Army, led by Alexander Suvorov, routs numerically superior Ottoman Empire forces.
During this tenure

moscow:Platon_Levshin.bio: Plato II or Platon II was the Metropolitan of Moscow from 1775 to 1812. He personifies the Age of Enlightenment in the Russian Orthodox Church. He was born at Chashnikovo near Moscow as Platon Levshin (Russian: Платон Левшин) in the family of a psalmodist, and was educated at the seminary and the Slavic Greek Latin Academy of Moscow. In 1757 he was appointed instructor in Greek and rhetoric at the latter institution, and became distinguished as a pulpit orator.
ev: American Revolution: George Washington takes command of the 17,000-man Continental Army at Cambridge.
During this tenure, at about age 38
Charles XIV of Sweden–Norway is crowned king of Sweden.
Charles XIV John
During this tenure
German astronomer Johann Georg Tralles discovers what will be called the Great Comet of 1819.
During this tenure

moscow:Philaret_Drozdov.bio: Metropolitan Philaret was Metropolitan of Moscow and Kolomna and the most influential figure in the Russian Orthodox Church for more than 40 years, from 1821 to 1867. He was canonized on 13 October 1994 and his feast day is celebrated on November 19.
ev: Greek War of Independence: At the Battle of Gravia Inn, a 120-man Greek force led by Odysseas Androutsos repulses an Ottoman army of 8,000.
During this tenure, at about age 39

moscow:Innocent_of_Alaska.bio: Innocent of Alaska (Russian: Иннокентий; August 26, 1797 – 12 April [O.S. March 31] 1879), also known as Innocent Metropolitan of Moscow, was a Russian Orthodox missionary priest, then the first Orthodox bishop and archbishop in the Americas, and finally the Metropolitan of Moscow and Kolomna. Remembered for his missionary work, scholarship, and leadership in Alaska and the Russian Far East during the 19th century, he is known for his abilities as a scholar, linguist, and administrator, as well as his great zeal for his work.
ev: The world's first traffic signal lights are installed at the junction of Great George Street and Bridge Street in the London Borough of Westminster.
During this tenure, at about age 71

moscow:Macarius_Bulgakov.bio: Metropolitan Macarius (Russian: Митрополи́т Мака́рий, born Mikhail Petrovich Bulgakov, Russian: Михаи́л Петро́вич Булга́ков; 1 October [O.S. 19 September] 1816–21 June [O.S. 9] 1882), was the Metropolitan of Moscow and Kolomna in 1879–82 and member of many learned societies, including the Russian Academy of Sciences. In 1841, he graduated from the Kiev Theological Academy, of which he served as a dean in 1851–57. His popular student manual, Orthodox Dogmatic Theology, steeped in the Latin methodology, was originally printed in 6 volumes in 1847–53.
ev: The first female students are admitted to study for degrees of the University of Oxford in England, at the new Lady Margaret Hall and Somerville Hall, and with the Society of Oxford Home-Students.
During this tenure, at about age 63
Holborn Viaduct power station in the City of London, the world's first coal-fired public electricity generating station, begins operation.
During this tenure
The London–Paris telephone system officially opens.
During this tenure

moscow:Patriarch_Sergius_of_Moscow.o: Primate of the Russian Church · 4 terms
moscow:Patriarch_Sergius_of_Moscow.bio: Patriarch Sergius I (Russian: Патриа́рх Се́ргий; born Ivan Nikolayevich Stragorodsky, Ива́н Никола́евич Страгоро́дский; January 23 [O.S. January 11] 1867 – May 15, 1944) was the 12th Patriarch of Moscow and all the Rus', from September 8, 1943 until his death on May 15, 1944. He was also the de facto head of the Russian Orthodox Church in 1925–1943, firstly as deputy Patriarchal locum tenens (1925–1937) subsequently as Patriarchal locum tenens (1937–1943).
ev: The first students enter St Hilda's College, Oxford, England, founded for women by Dorothea Beale.
St Hilda's College, Oxford
During this tenure, at about age 26

moscow:Vladimir_Bogoyavlensky.bio: Vladimir, baptismal name: Vasily Nikiforovich Bogoyavlensky (Russian: Василий Никифорович Богоявленский; 1 January 1848 – 7 February [O.S. January 25] 1918), was a bishop of the Russian Orthodox Church. He was appointed to the position of Metropolitan of Moscow and Kolomna between 1898 and 1912, Metropolitan of St. Petersburg and Ladoga between 1912 and 1915, and the Metropolitan of Kiev and Galicia between 1915 and 1918. Murdered by Bolshevik soldiers in 1918, Metropolitan Vladimir was glorified as a Hieromartyr by the Russian Orthodox Church in 1992.
ev: Chinese soldiers attack a party of British engineers at the Marco Polo Bridge on the Beijing to Hankou railway.
During this tenure, at about age 50

moscow:Macarius_(Nevsky).bio: Metropolitan Macarius was the Metropolitan of Moscow and Kolomna from 1912 to 1917, an outstanding missionary and enlightener of the masses in the Altai region.
ev: Italy and the Ottoman Empire sign a treaty in Ouchy near Lausanne, ending the Italo-Turkish War.
During this tenure, at about age 77

moscow:Patriarch_Tikhon_of_Moscow.bio: Tikhon of Moscow (Russian: Тихон Московский, 31 January [O.S. 19 January] 1865 – 7 April [O.S. 25 March] 1925), born Vasily Ivanovich Bellavin (Russian: Василий Иванович Беллавин), was a bishop of the Russian Orthodox Church (ROC). On 5 November 1917 (OS) he was selected the 11th Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia, after a period of about 200 years of the Synodal rule in the ROC. He was canonised as a confessor by the ROC in 1989.
ev: King Constantine I of Greece abdicates for the first time, being succeeded by his son Alexander.
During this tenure, at about age 52

moscow:Peter_of_Krutitsy.bio: Peter of Krutitsy (Священному́ченик Пётр Крути́цкий, born Pyotr Fyodorovich Polyansky, Пётр Фёдорович Поля́нский; July 10, 1862 – October 10, 1937, was a Russian Orthodox bishop and martyr. From April 12 till December 9, 1925 he was the head of the Russian Orthodox Church, serving as the patriarchal locum tenens. Despite his imprisonment, he remained technically locum tenens until his death in 1937. He is considered as a saint hieromartyr by the Russian Orthodox Church.
ev: In London, UK, John Logie Baird successfully transmits the first television pictures with a greyscale image.
During this tenure, at about age 63

moscow:Patriarch_Alexy_I_of_Moscow.bio: Patriarch Alexy I (Alexius I, Russian: Патриарх Алексий I, secular name Sergey Vladimirovich Simansky, Russian: Серге́й Влади́мирович Сима́нский; November 8 [O.S. October 27] 1877 – 17 April 1970) was the 13th Patriarch of Moscow and all Rus', Primate of the Russian Orthodox Church (ROC) between 1945 and 1970.
ev: Prague uprising: Prague rises up against occupying Nazi forces, encouraged by radio broadcasts (giving rise to the Battle for Czech Radio).
Prague uprising
During this tenure, at about age 68

moscow:Patriarch_Pimen_I_of_Moscow.bio: Patriarch Pimen I (Russian: Патриарх Пи́мен, born Sergey Mikhailovich Izvekov, Серге́й Миха́йлович Изве́ков; July 23 [O.S. July 10] 1910 – May 3, 1990), was the 14th Patriarch of Moscow and the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church from 1971 to 1990.
ev: Apollo 15 astronauts David Scott and James Irwin become the first to ride in the Lunar Roving Vehicle, a day after landing on the Moon.
During this tenure, at about age 61

moscow:Patriarch_Alexy_II_of_Moscow.bio: Patriarch Alexy II was the 15th Patriarch of Moscow and all Rus', the primate of the Russian Orthodox Church. Elected Patriarch of Moscow in 1990, eighteen months before the dissolution of the Soviet Union, he became the first Russian Patriarch of the post-Soviet period.
ev: British Satellite Broadcasting and Sky Television plc merge to form BSkyB as a result of massive losses.
During this tenure, at about age 61

moscow:Patriarch_Kirill_of_Moscow.bio: Kirill or Cyril is a Russian Orthodox bishop. He became Patriarch of Moscow and all Rus' and Primate of the Russian Orthodox Church on 1 February 2009. Prior to becoming Patriarch, Kirill was Archbishop (later Metropolitan) of Smolensk and Kaliningrad, and also Chairman of the Russian Orthodox Church's Department for External Church Relations. He has been a permanent member of the Holy Synod since 1989. A close ally of Russian leader Vladimir Putin, Kirill has described Putin's rule as "a miracle of God". According to Putin, Kirill's father baptized him.
ev: COVID-19 pandemic: China reports no new cases for the first time since the pandemic began, according to the National Health Commission.
During this tenure, at about age 74

antioch:Paul_the_Jew.bio: Paul the Jew was the Patriarch of Antioch from 519 to 521.
ev: Cerdic becomes the first king of the Kingdom of Wessex.
Cerdic of Wessex
During this tenure

antioch:Euphrasius_of_Antioch.bio: Euphrasius of Antioch was the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 521 to 526. He was elected after Paul the Jew abdicated and was milder than his predecessor in his persecution of the Oriental Orthodox of his diocese. According to Evagrius Scholasticus, Euphrasius was from Jerusalem. He died following the massive earthquake in May 526.
ev: Leptis Magna is sacked by Berber (Moor) raiders. Gelimer leads a successful expedition in North Africa.
Leptis Magna
During this tenure

antioch:Ephraim_of_Antioch.bio: Saint Ephraim of Antioch, also known as Saint Ephraim of Amida, was the Patriarch of Antioch, and head of the Greek Orthodox Church of Antioch, from 527 until his death in 545. He is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox and Catholic Churches. His feast day is 8 June.
ev: Battle of Anglon: A Byzantine invasion of Persarmenia is defeated by a much smaller force from the Sasanian Empire.
Battle of Anglon (543)
During this tenure, at about age 142
Taliesin, British poet, becomes court bard to King Brochwel of Powys.
Taliesin
During this tenure
First Tikal-Calakmul War: The Maya state of Caracol (Belize) defeats King Wak Chan K'awiil (Double Bird) of Tikal in battle, ending his dynasty.
First Tikal-Calakmul War
During this tenure

antioch:Gregory_of_Antioch.bio: Gregory of Antioch was the Eastern Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 571 to 593. Gregory began as a monk in the monastery of the Byzantines in Jerusalem, or so we learn from Evagrius Scholasticus. He was transferred by the emperor Justin II (565-578 ) to Sinai. He was abbot there when the monastery was attacked by Arabs. John Moschus mentions he was also abbot of Pharan in Palestine. In 569-70 he became Patriarch of Antioch after Justin II deposed the Patriarch Anastasius I of Antioch.
ev: The Lombard Kingdom (Italy) is converted to Roman Catholicism under the rule of King Authari.
Kingdom of the Lombards
During this tenure, at about age 38
Battle of Raith: An invading force of Angles lands on the Fife coast near Raith (Kirkcaldy) and defeats an alliance of Scots, Britons and Picts, under King Áedán mac Gabráin of Dál Riata (Scotland).
Battle of Raith
During this tenure
Moravians gain independence, by holding off the attacks from the Avars and the Franks who try to invade.
Moravia
During this tenure
Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty sends a Chinese mission to study Indian techniques of sugar manufacturing, at Bihar in the Ganges Valley.
Emperor Taizong of Tang
During this tenure
A Muslim Arab army led by Uqba ibn Nafi reaches Morocco, before being forced back into Cyrene by the Berbers.
Arab Muslims
During this tenure

antioch:George_II_of_Antioch.bio: George II of Antioch was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch in the 7th century. Little is known about him except that he attended the Quinisext Council in 691–692. It is speculated that he died of heat exhaustion caused by a long period of being outdoors. After his death the period of Arab tolerance that had allowed the continued existence of Christianity in regions under their domination ended. George II of Antioch's reign was one well known for peace, due to his love of many religions.
ev: The Gagakuryo (Bureau of Court Music) is formed at the Imperial Court in Kyoto. Numerous types of music and dance are performed.
Gagaku
During this tenure
Li Bai (also Li Po), Chinese poet and skilled calligrapher, meets Du Fu for the first time.
Li Bai
During this tenure
Emperor Xuan Zong abolishes the death penalty in China, during the Tang dynasty.
Emperor Xuanzong of Tang
During this tenure
Otomo no Yakamochi, Japanese general, compiles the first Japanese poetry anthology, Man'yōshū. It contains some 500 poems by Japanese poets who include the emperor, noblemen and commoners.
Otomo no Yakamochi
During this tenure
Shinsen Shōjiroku, a record of the genealogy of the ancient Japanese noble families, is completed during the reign of Emperor Saga.
Shinsen Shōjiroku
During this tenure
Viking raiders sack the cities of Paris, Cologne, Aachen, Worms and Toulouse.
Vikings
During this tenure
Viking raiders invade the Kingdom of Pamplona (Western Pyrenees), and capture King García Íñiguez I, somewhere in the Andalusian heartland. They extort a ransom, rising to around 70,000 gold dinars.
Kingdom of Pamplona
During this tenure

The Danes, led by Halfdan Ragnarsson and Bagsecg, invade Wessex and take the royal estate at Reading (Berkshire), which Halfdan makes his headquarters. A naval Viking contingent sails up the Thames River.
Halfdan Ragnarsson
During this tenure
Luoyang, eastern Chinese capital of the Tang dynasty, is captured by rebel leader Huang Chao, during the reign of emperor Xizong.
During this tenure

Prince Edward, the son of King Alfred the Great, defeats the Danish Viking raiders at Farnham, and forces them to take refuge on Thorney Island. At the same time, Danes from East Anglia sail around the Cornish coast, and besiege Exeter.
Edward the Elder
During this tenure

antioch:Elias_I_of_Antioch_(Chalcedonian.bio: Elias, fl. 907–934, was the Chalcedonian Patriarch of Antioch from 907 to 934. Prior to his elevation to the patriarchate, he served as a secretary at the Abbasid Caliph's court in Baghdad. He is noted for his diplomatic engagements with the Eastern Roman Empire, particularly concerning the Tetragamy controversy and the treatment of prisoners of war.
ev: The Hungarians cross Bavaria, and invade Swabia and Franconia. They plunder the territories from Minfeld to Aargau. After that, they cross the Rhine, and attack Burgundy for the first time.
Principality of Hungary
During this tenure
The Later Tang falls to the Later Jin (during the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period) founded by Emperor Shi Jingtang (posthumously known as "Gaozu of Jin").
Later Tang
During this tenure
King Hywel Dda ("the Good") convenes a conference at Whitland, which draws up a standardized code of laws in Wales.
Hywel Dda
During this tenure

antioch:Agapios_I_of_Antioch.bio: Agapios I, also known simply as Agapios, was the Melkite Patriarch of Antioch from approximately 953 to 959.
ev: A Byzantine fleet under Basil Hexamilites deals a crushing defeat to the Hamdanid fleet at Tarsus in Cilicia.
During this tenure

antioch:Christopher_of_Antioch.bio: Christopher was Chalcedonian Patriarch of Antioch from 960 to 967.
ev: Battle of Fitjar – A Viking force under the sons of Eric Bloodaxe lands on Hordaland. King Haakon the Good defeats the rebelling force, but is killed. Harald Greycloak becomes ruler of the western part of Norway.
Battle of Fitjar
During this tenure

antioch:Eustratios_of_Antioch.bio: Eustratios was briefly Patriarch of Antioch in late 969. Appointed by Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, Eustratios never formally assumed office or traveled to his see due to the emperor's assassination. He is a largely obscure figure in ecclesiastical history, omitted from most traditional patriarchal lists, and is known primarily through the late 12th-century text De translationibus episcoporum.
ev: Fatimid conquest of Egypt: Caliph Al-Mu'izz's army under General Jawhar invades Egypt. Jawhar occupies the lands around the Nile from the Ikhshidids after a siege at Giza and the capitulation of Fustat.
During this tenure

antioch:Theodore_II_of_Antioch.bio: Theodore II was the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 23 January 970 until his death in 976. Appointed by Emperor John I Tzimiskes, Theodore's patriarchate was marked by the restoration of patriarchal rights in Antioch following the Roman reconquest, as well as his involvement in the political turmoil of the early reign of Basil II.
ev: Skagul Toste leads a Viking expedition to England and demands Danegeld.
Skagul Toste
During this tenure

antioch:Agapios_II_of_Antioch.bio: Agapios II was the Patriarch of Antioch from 20 January 978 until his abdication in September 996. Initially serving as the Bishop of Aleppo, he secured the patriarchal throne through a political agreement with the Byzantine Emperor Basil II, helping to bring the city of Antioch back under imperial control during the rebellion of Bardas Skleros. His tenure was marked by ecclesiastical disputes, the turmoil of Bardas Phokas's revolt, and a lengthy period of exile in Constantinople.
ev: Viking Age: Danish Viking raiders, (probably) under King Sweyn Forkbeard, plunder the city of Stade (Lower Saxony). Count Lothair Udo I is captured and killed, during the battle with the pirates.
During this tenure

antioch:John_III_of_Antioch_(Chalcedonia.bio: John of Antioch, also known by the epithet Polites, was the Chalcedonian Patriarch of Antioch from 4 October 996 until his death in July 1021. Before his elevation to the patriarchate, he served as the chartophylax of the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.
ev: Máel Mórda mac Murchada starts a rebellion against High King Brian Boru in Ireland, which ends in 1014 at the Battle of Clontarf.
Máel Mórda mac Murchada
During this tenure

antioch:Nicholas_II_of_Antioch.bio: Nikolaos II was the Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 17 January 1025 to 8 October 1030. Prior to his elevation to the patriarchate, he was a monk, a priest, and the hegumenos (abbot) of the Stoudios Monastery in Constantinople.
ev: Zoë Porphyrogenita takes the throne as empress consort. Her husband, Romanos III (age 60) becomes emperor of the Byzantine Empire.
During this tenure

antioch:Elias_II_of_Antioch.bio: Elias II Sophronites was the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from April 1, 1032 until his death.
ev: Treaty of Merseburg: Conrad II attends a Hoftag at Merseburg and signs an agreement with King Mieszko II. He divides Poland in three parts with Mieszko designated as supreme ruler, in exchange for Conrad's support.
Treaty of Merseburg
During this tenure
The Chinese rime dictionary of the Jiyun is published during the Song Dynasty.
rime dictionary
During this tenure

antioch:Peter_III_of_Antioch.bio: Peter III was a Patriarch of Antioch. He originally came from Antioch, but had been educated in Constantinople, where he rose to high office in the church of the Hagia Sophia. He was appointed as Patriarch of Antioch by Emperor Constantine Monomachos in 1052, and served in this role until his death in 1057. Peter corresponded with Christian leaders of the time, including Pope Leo IX and Patriarch Michael Keroularious.
ev: Astronomers record a supernova that leaves the Crab Nebula.
During this tenure
The Pagoda of Fogong Temple at Shanxi in northern China is built during the Liao dynasty. Work begins on the Pizhi Pagoda of Lingyan Temple at Shandong under the opposing Song dynasty.
Pagoda of Fogong Temple
During this tenure

antioch:Theodosius_III_of_Antioch.o: Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch · 2 terms
antioch:Theodosius_III_of_Antioch.bio: Theodosios III Chrysoberges served as the Patriarch of Antioch during the mid-11th century. He was in office prior to August 30, 1057, and still occupied the patriarchal seat on April 4, 1059. The exact dates of the start the end of his patriarchate remain unknown.
ev: King Béla III of Hungary and Croatia goes to war with Venice in an effort to recover Dalmatia. The city of Zadar (located on the Adriatic Sea) accepts Béla's suzerainty.
Béla III of Hungary
During this tenure
Norman conquest of southern Italy: Italo-Norman forces under Robert Guiscard de Hauteville and Richard I of Capua, conquer the fortress city of Salerno after a short siege.
During this tenure
King William the Conqueror establishes the New Forest in Southern England. He proclaims it as a royal forest, using it for hunting, mainly of deer.
William the Conqueror
During this tenure

antioch:John_the_Oxite.bio: John the Oxite or John Oxeites was the Greek Orthodox patriarch of Antioch from c. 1089 until 1100, when he was exiled by Prince Bohemond I of Antioch. He fled to the Byzantine Empire and continued to govern those parts of the patriarchate that were under Byzantine rule. He was a prominent writer of religious texts, and reformer of religious and charitable foundations. Prior to his patriarchate, John was a monk.
ev: Siege of Jerusalem: The Crusaders reach the outskirts of Jerusalem, and begin the siege of the Holy City. Iftikhar al-Dawla offers a peace agreement but this is refused.
During this tenure, at about age 98

Jin–Song Wars: Jurchen forces sack the Chinese capital of Kaifeng of the Northern Song dynasty during the Jingkang incident. They capture Emperor Qinzong, along with his father, Huizong, and members of the House of Zhao.
During this tenure
Géza II is crowned King of Hungary and Croatia at age 11, succeeding his father.
During this tenure
The Hōgen rebellion, a dispute between Emperor Go-Shirakawa and his half-brother retired-Emperor Sutoku, erupts in Japan.
During this tenure

antioch:Athanasius_I_Manasses.bio: Athanasius I Manasses, also known as Athanasius III, was the Greek Orthodox patriarch of Antioch from 1157 to 1170. His early life is poorly documented, but it is known that he was a monk at the Monastery of Saint John the Theologian and composed a eulogy of Christodoulos of Patmos. He was elected patriarch in 1157 but resided in Constantinople, as the patriarchal see of Antioch had been held by Catholic prelates since the establishment of the Principality of Antioch during the First Crusade.
ev: Emperor Sutoku of Japan dies in Sanuki Province (on the island of Shikoku), having lived in exile from the capital at Kyoto since 1156.
During this tenure
Battle of Montgisard: Baldwin IV of Jerusalem and Raynald of Chatillon defeat Saladin.
During this tenure

antioch:Theodore_IV_of_Antioch.bio: Theodore Balsamon, also called Balsamo, was a canonist of the Eastern Orthodox Church and 12th-century Eastern Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch.
ev: Minamoto no Yoritomo becomes shogun of Japan.
Kamakura shogunate
During this tenure

antioch:Theodosius_of_Villehardouin.bio: Theodosius of Villehardouin or Theodosios Prinkips was the Greek Orthodox patriarch of Antioch as Theodosius V from 1278 to 1283. He amassed a considerable library of manuscripts, several of which are known today dispersed among different collections.
ev: Battle of Hova: King Valdemar Birgersson of Sweden is defeated by his brother Magnus in the forest of Tiveden.
During this tenure
The Mongol Golden Horde led by Nogai Khan and Talabuga attacks Hungary for the second time. They successfully subdue Slovakia and sack territory north of the Carpathian Mountains.
Golden Horde
During this tenure
Ottoman-Turkish forces led by Sultan Osman I conquer the ancient city of Ephesus from the Byzantine Empire, massacring and deporting its native population.
During this tenure
Byzantine civil war of 1352–1357 – Battle of Demotika: Fighting as allies of John VI Kantakouzenos, the Ottoman beylik scores its first victory on European soil, against the Serbs.
During this tenure
The Bibliothèque nationale de France (National Library of France) is founded as the Royal Library at the Louvre Palace in Paris, by Charles V of France.
Bibliothèque nationale de France
During this tenure
Hundred Years' War: The French burn Portsmouth, England; the English raid Picardy and Normandy.
During this tenure
The Treaty of Bruges, signed on June 27, 1375 between England and France to end hostilities in the Hundred Years' War for a year, is extended by agreement to June 24, 1377.
During this tenure
King Richard II opens the Irish Parliament for the first time since the death of his father, King Edward III, a year earlier.
During this tenure
King Richard II of England summons the members of the English Parliament to assemble at Westminster on November 3.
During this tenure
The city of Afyonkarahisar (in modern-day western Turkey) is conquered by Sultan Beyazid I, of the Ottoman Empire.
Afyonkarahisar
During this tenure
The first 200 Chinese treasure ships are ordered by the new Ming dynasty Emperor Cheng Zu from the Capital Guards at Nanjing.
During this tenure
China's Emperor Cheng Zu orders the fourth of the Ming treasure voyages, to be led by Admiral Zheng He.
During this tenure
The Xuande Era begins in Ming dynasty China as the first Lunar New Year of the reign of the Emperor Xuanzong.
During this tenure
Venice sends Andrea Venier to negotiate with the Ottoman Empire in an attempt to have the Ottomans invade Albania. Afterwards, Venier is sent to meet with Skanderbeg to ask him to cease hostilities.
During this tenure
At the Battle of Leskovac, Nikola Skobaljić, voivode of Dubočica, defeats Ottoman Turks invading Serbia.
During this tenure
At the Battle of Albulena, the Albanian general Skanderbeg's defeats Ottoman Empire army, in the open field.
During this tenure
Magdalen College was founded in the University of Oxford, England.
Magdalen College, Oxford
During this tenure
William Hastings, 1st Baron Hastings, is executed, in the first recorded execution at the Tower of London.
During this tenure
Manco Inca Yupanqui, nominally Sapa Inca, is imprisoned by the Spanish Conquistadors of Peru.
During this tenure
King Henry VIII of England allies with Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, against France.
During this tenure
King Henry VIII of England signs an agreement with Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor to invade France by June 20, 1544 with at least 35,000 infantry and 7,000 cavalry.
During this tenure

antioch:Michael_VI_of_Antioch.bio: Patriarch Michael VI was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 1576 to 1581, and antipatriarch of Antioch from 1581 to 1583.
ev: Mehmed II Giray becomes the new Khan of Crimea for the Ottoman Empire, after the death of his father, Devlet I Giray, from a plague.
During this tenure

antioch:Joachim_V_of_Antioch.bio: Patriarch Joachim V was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 1581 to 1592.
ev: The Kingdom of England establishes its first diplomatic relations with the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure

antioch:Joachim_VI.bio: Patriarch Joachim VI was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 1593 to 1604.
ev: William Shakespeare's tragedy Hamlet, recently premiered by the Lord Chamberlain's Men, is licensed for publishing in London but not in fact printed at this time.
During this tenure

antioch:Dorotheus_IV_Ibn_Al-Ahmar.bio: Patriarch Dorotheus IV Ibn Al-Ahmar, sometime known also as Dorotheus V, was Melkite Patriarch of Antioch from 1604 to 1611.
ev: Galileo Galilei's treatise on astronomy, Sidereus Nuncius, the first printed scientific record of observations through a telescope, is first published.
During this tenure

antioch:Athanasius_II_Dabbas.bio: Patriarch Athanasius II Dabbas, sometime known also as Athanasius III, was Eastern Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 1611 to 1619.
ev: Johannes Kepler publishes Dissertatio cum Nuncio Sidereo, in response to Galileo's discovery of Jupiter's moons.
Johannes Kepler
During this tenure

antioch:Cyril_IV_Dabbas.bio: Cyril IV Dabbas was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch. He succeeded his brother Athanasius II Dabbas as Patriarch after his death in 1619.
ev: Polish-Swedish War: Battle of Wallhof in Latvia – Gustavus Adolphus, King of Sweden, defeats a Polish army.
During this tenure, at about age 66

antioch:Euthymius_II_Karmah.bio: Patriarch Abdel-Karim Meletios Euthymius II Karmah was Melkite Patriarch of Antioch from 1634 to 1635. He had been a leading figure in the Melkite Church and metropolitan bishop of Aleppo. He died a few months after his election as Patriarch, probably poisoned because his will to proceed with a union with the Catholic Church.
ev: Thirty Years' War – The Peace of Prague is signed, which ends the German civil war aspect of the conflict.
During this tenure, at about age 63

antioch:Euthymius_III_of_Chios.bio: Patriarch Meletios Euthymius III of Chios, sometimes known also as Euthymius IV, was Melkite Greek Patriarch of Antioch from 1635 to 1647.
ev: The Battle of Songjin begins in the modern-day North Korean city of Kimch'aek, at the time part of the Chinese Empire controlled by the Ming dynasty. The Ming, led by General Wu Sangui, defeat the Qing rebels.
During this tenure, at about age 61
Portuguese Restoration War: In the Battle of Vilanova, a Spanish army, having crossed the Minho, defeats the Portuguese.
During this tenure

antioch:Cyril_V_Zaim.bio: Patriarch Constantine Cyril V Zaim, sometimes known also as Cyril III, was Patriarch of Antioch.
ev: The first performance of George Frideric Handel's opera Il pastor fido takes place at the Queen's Theatre in the Haymarket, London.
During this tenure, at about age 57

antioch:Neophytos_of_Chios.bio: Patriarch Neophytos of Chios was Patriarch of Antioch from 1673 to 1682. Though the family of Neophytos was originally from Chios, he was educated in Damascus under the Jesuits. He was the nephew of previous Patriarch Euthymius III of Chios and he was appointed vicar in Aleppo under the reign of Patriarch Macarios III Zaim. In 1672 he was appointed bishop of Hama.

antioch:Sylvester_of_Antioch.bio: Sylvester was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch, the first patriarch after the Catholic schism. He was the nephew of Patriarch Athanasius III Dabbas. He was a figure of importance in the history of Arabic printing.
ev: King George's War: The British capture Cape Breton Island in North America from the French.
During this tenure, at about age 65

antioch:Philemon_of_Antioch.bio: Philemon was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch.

During this tenure

antioch:Daniel_of_Antioch.bio: Daniel was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch.
ev: Austrian composer Joseph Haydn, on his visit to England, is awarded an honorary doctorate of music at the University of Oxford.
During this tenure, at about age 41

antioch:Euthymius_V_of_Antioch.bio: Euthymius or Anthemius was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 1792 to 1813.
ev: The famous composer Joseph Haydn dies in Vienna at age 77 following Napoleon's second siege of Vienna.
Joseph Haydn
During this tenure, at about age 59

antioch:Seraphim_of_Antioch.bio: Seraphim was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch.
ev: War of the Sixth Coalition – Battle of Mormant: A French army led by Napoleon effectively destroys a Russian division.
During this tenure, at about age 64

antioch:Methodius_of_Antioch.bio: Methodius was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch. Little is known of Patriarch Methodius' life. In May 1848, Methodius was a signatory, with the patriarchs of Constantinople, Alexandria, and Jerusalem, of an encyclical to the Church responding to the "Epistle to the Easterns" by Pope Pius IX. The encyclical denounced the Filioque added by Rome to the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed as a heresy, censured the papacy for missionizing among Orthodox Christians, and repudiated Ultramontanism (papal supremacy).
ev: Greek War of Independence: the London Protocol entails the creation of an autonomous Greek state under Ottoman suzerainty encompassing the Morea and the Cyclades.
During this tenure, at about age 57

antioch:Hierotheos_of_Antioch.bio: Hierotheos was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch.
ev: The Royal Titles Act 1876 in the UK Parliament confers the title 'Empress of India' upon Queen Victoria from 1877.
Royal Titles Act 1876
During this tenure, at about age 76

antioch:Gerasimus_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Gerasimus I was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem from March 11, 1891, to February 21, 1897. It was during his administration as Patriarch of Jerusalem that the full significance of the mosaic map found on the church floor in Madaba was understood. In 1885, Gerasimus was the Bishop of Scythopolis, a city just south of the Sea of Galilee.
ev: The Finnish epic Kalevala is published for the first time in the English language, by American linguist John Martin Crawford.
Kalevala
During this tenure, at about age 49

antioch:Spyridon_of_Antioch.bio: Patriarch Spyridon was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch.
ev: The Stars and Stripes Forever, an American patriotic march by John Philip Sousa, is performed for the first time.
The Stars and Stripes Forever
During this tenure, at about age 59

antioch:Meletius_II_of_Antioch.bio: Patriarch Meletius II Doumani (Arabic: البطريرك ملاتيوس الثاني دوماني al-Baṭriyark Milātiyūs aṯ-Ṯānī Dūmānī, was Patriarch of Antioch from 1899 to 1906.
ev: The first Nobel Prize ceremony is held in Stockholm, on the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.
During this tenure, at about age 62
The British viceroy of India and Mohandas Gandhi sign the Gandhi–Irwin Pact.
During this tenure

antioch:Theodosius_VI_of_Antioch.bio: Patriarch Theodosius VI was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch from 1958 to 1970.
ev: The Shinkansen high-speed rail system, the world's first such system, is inaugurated in Japan, for the first sector between Tokyo and Osaka.
Shinkansen
During this tenure, at about age 75

antioch:Elias_IV_of_Antioch.bio: Patriarch Elias IV was the Patriarch of the Greek Orthodox Church of Antioch and All the East from 1970 to 1979.
ev: Viking program: NASA launches the Viking 1 planetary probe toward Mars.
During this tenure, at about age 61

antioch:Ignatius_IV_of_Antioch.bio: Patriarch Ignatius IV was the Patriarch of the Greek Orthodox Church of Antioch and All The East from 1979 to 2012.
ev: The King of Bhutan allows television transmissions to commence in the Kingdom for the first time, coinciding with the King's Silver Jubilee.
During this tenure, at about age 79

antioch:John_X_of_Antioch.bio: Patriarch John X is primate of the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch and All The East.
ev: A fast radio burst is detected from the Magnetar SGR 1935+2154, the first ever detected inside the Milky Way, and the first to be linked to a known source.
fast radio burst
During this tenure, at about age 65

georgia:John_I_of_Mtskheta.bio: John I of Mtskheta was the first archbishop of the Georgian Orthodox Church in period of 335–363.
ev: King Shapur II of Persia begins a war against the Roman Empire. He sends his troops across the Tigris to recover Armenia and Mesopotamia.
Shapur II
During this tenure

georgia:Jacob_of_Mtskheta.bio: Jacob of Mtskheta was the second archbishop of the Georgian Orthodox Church in period of 363–375.
ev: Roman poet Ausonius writes of a voyage on the Rhine and the Moselle in his work 'Mosella'.
Ausonius
During this tenure

Emperor Theodosius I signs a peace treaty with King Shapur III; they divide Armenia into two kingdoms (vassal states). The treaty establishes friendly relations between the Roman Empire and Persia for the next 36 years.
Theodosius I
During this tenure
Alaric, Visigothic leader of the foederati, renounces Roman fealty and is declared king, waging war against both parts of the Roman Empire, and ending a 16-year period of peace.
Alaric I
During this tenure
The remaining Roman legions in Britain decide to mutiny. The usurper Marcus is proclaimed emperor.
Roman legion
During this tenure
The Franks conquer new territories in their kingdom and sack the old Roman capital Augusta Treverorum.
Franks
During this tenure
The University of Constantinople is founded by emperor Theodosius II at the urging of his wife Aelia Eudocia.
During this tenure
The Huns are united by King Rugila (also called Rua) on the Hungarian Plain. He exacts annual peace payments from the Eastern Roman Empire.
Rugila
During this tenure
Emperor Theodosius II bribes the Huns (after the death of Rugila) to keep the peace in the Eastern Roman Empire.
Theodosius II
During this tenure
King Genseric concludes a peace treaty with the Romans, under which the Vandals retain Mauretania and a part of Numidia as foederati (allies under a special treaty) of Rome.
Genseric
During this tenure
K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' dies after an 11-year reign. He is the founder and first ruler of the pre-Columbian Maya civilization centered at Copán.
K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo'
During this tenure
Nalanda University (India) is founded.
Nalanda mahavihara
During this tenure
King Dhatusena of Anuradhapura of the Moriyan dynasty rules over Sri Lanka. During his reign the Avukana Buddha statue is built.
Dhatusena of Anuradhapura
During this tenure
Mount Vesuvius erupts. During the volcanic eruption the whole of southern Europe is blanketed by ash.
Mount Vesuvius
During this tenure
Julius Nepos, former emperor of the Western Roman Empire, dies in exile in Dalmatia (he is murdered by his own soldiers, in his villa, near Salona).
Julius Nepos
During this tenure
War with Sassanid Persia: Emperor Anastasius I gains the upper hand in Armenia, with the renewed investment of Amida.
Anastasian War
During this tenure
King Theodoric the Great grants citizens on Mount Vesuvius exemption from taxes, after a severe eruption in southeastern Italy.
Theodoric the Great
During this tenure
An earthquake destroys the city of Scupi, in what once was the Roman province of Moesia Superior.
earthquake
During this tenure
Justinian issues the first edition of his law code.
Corpus Juris Civilis
During this tenure
Battle of Faventia: King Totila scatters the Byzantine forces near Faventia with 5,000 men, beginning the resurgence of Gothic resistance to the reconquest of Italy.
Battle of Faventia
During this tenure
Lazic War: King Gubazes II revolts against the Persians, and requests aid from Justinian I. He sends a Byzantine expeditionary force to Lazica.
Lazic War
During this tenure
King Gubazes II is invited to observe the siege of a Persian-held fortress, and is murdered by the Byzantine military staff after accusing them of incompetence.
Gubazes II of Lazica
During this tenure
Calakmul defeats Tikal, bringing an end to the First Tikal-Calakmul War.
Calakmul
During this tenure
Byzantine–Sassanid War: A Byzantine expeditionary force under command of Justinian (magister militum) invades Caucasian Albania, launching raids across the Caspian Sea against the Persians.
Byzantine–Sassanid War of 572–591
During this tenure
The Franks and Burgundians under King Guntram and his nephew Childebert II invade Northern Italy, but suffer a disastrous defeat against the Lombards.
Franks
During this tenure
The Lombards sack the town of Terracina (Central Italy). After they conquer more cities, Terracina remains an important military stronghold of the Byzantine Empire.
Lombards
During this tenure
Smallpox arrives in Western Europe for the first time.
Smallpox
During this tenure
King Edwin of Northumbria invades and annexes the minor British kingdom of Elmet.
Edwin of Northumbria
During this tenure
The town of Cholula is founded in central Mexico (later said to be the oldest continuously occupied town in all of North America).
Cholula, Puebla
During this tenure
Battle of Buzakha: An Islamic column under Khalid ibn al-Walid defeats the Apostate rebels under Tulayha, near Ha'il (Saudi Arabia).
During this tenure
The Xumi Pagoda of Zhengding (China) is built, during the reign of Emperor Taizong of Tang.
Xumi Pagoda
During this tenure
Arabs begin construction of the Mosque of Amr at Cairo, the first mosque built in Egypt and in all of Africa.
Mosque of Amr ibn al-As
During this tenure
Baekje in southwestern Korea is conquered by an alliance of the Tang dynasty and Silla, led by general Su Dingfang and King Munmu of Silla. The Japanese envoys detained in Chang'an are paroled.
Korea
During this tenure
Conflict erupts between King Sighere of Essex and his brother Sæbbi, as they struggle for overlordship between Mercia and Wessex.
Sighere of Essex
During this tenure
Battle of Dafei River: Chinese forces, under general Xue Rengui of the Tang dynasty, are annihilated by the Tibetans, who take over control of the Tarim Basin.
Battle of Dafei River
During this tenure
Emperor Tenmu assumes the Chrysanthemum Throne of Japan at the Palace of Kiyomihara, in Asuka.
During this tenure
Tang China declares the deposed Bojang of Goguryeo "King of Joseon", placing him in charge of the Liaodong area under the Protectorate General to Pacify the East.
Tang dynasty
During this tenure
In Japan the Asuka Kiyomihara Code is commenced under Emperor Tenmu.
Japan
During this tenure
684 Hakuho earthquake. A great earthquake strikes Japan. The people, houses, temples, shrines and domestic animals are greatly damaged.
During this tenure
Wu Zetian exiles her son Zhong Zong, former emperor of the Tang dynasty, and his family to the island of Fang Zhou.
exile
During this tenure

Arab–Byzantine War: An Umayyad army under Maslamah ibn Abd al-Malik invades Asia Minor, and lays siege to Tyana (Cappadocia). The fortress city resists, dragging the siege through the winter and into 708.
Arab–Byzantine wars
During this tenure
Battle of Hehil: The West Saxons are defeated by a combined Viking and Cornish army, at Cornovii in Cornwall.
Battle of Hehil
During this tenure
King Æthelbald of Mercia is described in the Ismere Diploma as ruler (bretwalda) of the Mercians, and all the provinces in southern England. He is also named "Rex Britanniae" (king of Britain).
Æthelbald of Mercia
During this tenure
Empress Kōmyō founds the Shin-Yakushi-ji Buddhist temple in Nara (Japan).
Empress Kōmyō
During this tenure
The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur founds Baghdad.
Baghdad
During this tenure
King Alhred of Northumbria makes overtures of friendship toward Charlemagne.
Alhred of Northumbria
During this tenure
In Japan, the Kiyomizu-dera Buddhist temple is founded in Kyoto. Its main hall (Hondo) is built in 1633 without a single nail.
Japan
During this tenure
The Frankish Kingdom conquers Girona and Urgell from the Moors. The Franks divide Catalonia into 14 countships. Charlemagne suppresses a rebellion by count Hardrad of Thuringia.
Francia
During this tenure
King Charles the Younger, a son of Charlemagne, conquers Corsica and Sardinia.
Charles the Younger
During this tenure
The Gymnasium Carolinum in Osnabrück is founded by Charlemagne (the oldest school in Germany).
Gymnasium Carolinum (Osnabrück)
During this tenure
Charlemagne dies at Aachen.
Charlemagne
During this tenure
The Viking ship of Oseberg near Tønsberg is buried in a mound, during the Viking Age.
Viking ships
During this tenure
Máel Sechnaill mac Máele Ruanaid becomes the first High King of Ireland. [Factually disputed. Source needed].
Máel Sechnaill mac Máele Ruanaid
During this tenure

The Viking chieftains Hastein and Björn Ironside ravage upstream and move to Italy, sacking Luna (believing it to be Rome). They sail up the River Arno to sack the cities of Pisa and Fiesole (Tuscany).
Hastein
During this tenure
Viking leader Halfdan Ragnarsson formally establishes the Danish kingdom of York, after the removal of the puppet king Ricsige of Northumbria, and becomes the first monarch.
Halfdan Ragnarsson
During this tenure
Viking raiders (80 ships) under Hastein arrive in the Thames Estuary, and set up camp at Middleton. King Alfred the Great decides to position his army in the Wealden Forest.
Hastein
During this tenure
The Danish Vikings invade Anglesey after being driven out of Dublin. They fail to gain a foothold in Wales, and sail on to Chester.
Denmark
During this tenure
The Fatimid Caliphate of Ifriqiya launch the second Fatimid invasion of Egypt in an attempt to seize Egypt from its Abbasid rulers. The expedition fails and the Fatimids will be forced to retreat.
During this tenure
Ngô Quyền, who the previous year defeated the Chinese at the Battle of Bạch Đằng thereby regaining Vietnamese independence after 1000 years, becomes king of Vietnam.
Ngô Quyền
During this tenure
The Mount Edziza volcanic complex in British Columbia, Canada, produces an explosive eruption that deposits the Sheep Track Member.
Mount Edziza volcanic complex
During this tenure
Tai Zong invades the Northern Han and besieges the capital of Taiyuan. A relief force sent by the Liao Dynasty is defeated. The Kingdom is absorbed into the Song Dynasty.
Northern Han
During this tenure
Norse Viking settlers establish a mint in Dublin (Ireland), to produce silver pennies.
Vikings
During this tenure
The First Battle of Alton: Danish invaders defeat the English.
First Battle of Alton
During this tenure

georgia:Melchizedek_I_of_Georgia.bio: Melchizedek I was the first Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia, serving from c. 1010 to 1033, and was based in Ani. He is venerated as a saint by the Eastern Orthodox Church. Prior to his tenure, the heads of the Georgian Church bore the title of Catholicos of Kartli. The unification of Georgia into a single kingdom under Bagrat III (r. 975–1014) contributed to the adoption of the combined title of Catholicos-Patriarch.
ev: Viking explorer Thorfinn Karlsefni attempts to found a settlement in North America.
Viking
During this tenure
Li Yuanhao proclaims himself Emperor of the Western Xia, declaring independence from the Song dynasty in China.
During this tenure
King Harthacnut collapses and dies while attending a party. His half-brother Edward the Confessor becomes king of England.
Harthacnut
During this tenure
King Edward the Confessor goes to war against Flanders, blockading the English Channel with a fleet based at Sandwich, Kent.
Edward the Confessor
During this tenure
Hedeby in Jutland is sacked by King Harald Hardrada of Norway, during the course of a conflict with Sweyn II of Denmark.
Hedeby
During this tenure
Battle of Cerami: Duke Roger I leads a small Norman force, and defeats a much larger Saracen army at Cerami (near Troina) in Sicily.
Battle of Cerami
During this tenure
The Normans conquer England.
Norman Conquest
During this tenure
The output of copper currency for the Chinese Song dynasty reaches 6 billion coins a year, prompting the Chinese government to adopt the world's first paper-printed money later in the 1120s.
copper
During this tenure
Battle of Anglesey Sound: A Norwegian fleet led by King Magnus Barefoot reverses an Anglo-Norman invasion of North Wales. Magnus conquers the Orkney Islands, the Hebrides and the Isle of Man.
Battle of Anglesey Sound
During this tenure
The coronation of Japan's Emperor Sutoku takes place.
During this tenure
Treaty of Shaoxing: The northern Jin Dynasty and Southern Song Dynasty sign a peace treaty, this ending the Jurchen campaigns against the Song Dynasty in China.
During this tenure
Angkor Wat is completed in the Khmer Empire.
Angkor Wat
During this tenure
Closeted Emperor Go-Shirakawa holds an opening ceremony for the Sanjūsangen-dō, a temple built by Taira no Kiyomori in Japan.
During this tenure

georgia:Michael_IV_of_Georgia.bio: Michael IV or Mikel Mirianisdze was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia, from 1178 to 1184, Mtsignobartukhutses-Chkondideli since 1184. Michael held his high offices to the end of his life. Archbishop of Samtvisi Michael was loyal to King George III. After the resignation of Nikoloz I Gulaberisdze he was appointed as Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia.
ev: Andronikos makes a treaty with Venice, in which he promises a yearly indemnity as compensation for Venetian losses, during the Massacre of the Latins.
During this tenure

georgia:Theodore_II_of_Georgia.bio: Theodore II was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia, from 1187 to 1204. During a revolt of treasurer Qutlu Arslan and Tamar's disgraced husband, Yuri, around 1191, Theodore remained loyal to the Queen. He, along with Anton Kutateli, the Archbishop of Kutaisi was sent to make peace with the rebels, but was unsuccessful.
ev: King Richard I of England (the Lionheart) has Château Gaillard (Normandy) built on the Seine River as he fights to restore Angevin power in northern France.
Richard I of England
During this tenure

georgia:Basil_IV_of_Georgia.bio: Basil IV was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia, from 1206 to 1208, during the reign of Queen Tamar. His name is mentioned in manuscripts of Shio-Mgvime monastery dated to 1270.
ev: Genghis Khan is proclaimed ruler of the Mongols.
Genghis Khan
During this tenure

georgia:John_VII_of_Georgia.bio: John VII was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia, from 1208 to 1210. He belonged to the group of reactionary monks that supported Georgian-Dyophysitism and condemned Armenian Miaphysitism. His activities resulted by baptizing Ivane Mkhargrdzeli, the ruler of Dvin and Vaspurakan, and a great number of Armenians with him.
ev: William Marshal is recalled and humiliated by King John at court in London, while John gives his justiciar in Ireland, Meiler Fitzhenry the order to invade Marshal's lands there, burning the town of New Ross.
William Marshal, 1st Earl of Pembroke
During this tenure
King John seals Magna Carta.
Magna Carta
During this tenure
The Ghurid dynasty capital of Firozkoh (in modern-day Afghanistan) is destroyed, by Mongol Emperor Ögedei Khan.
Ghurid dynasty
During this tenure
After a failed attempt on December 28, the Mongol General Muqali leads a second attack on the Chinese fortress of Fengxiang and fails.
During this tenure

Siege of Galway in Ireland: Norman forces under Richard Mór de Burgh invade Connacht and desolate a large portion of the country. He besieges Galway, but is forced to retreat after a week-long inconclusive battle.
Sieges of Galway
During this tenure
Siege of Caizhou: The Mongols under Ögedei Khan besiege Caizhou and ally themselves with the Chinese Song dynasty to eliminate the Jin Dynasty.
During this tenure
The city of Kraków is granted Magdeburg rights by High Duke Bolesław V the Chaste, having been rebuilt after being nearly destroyed during the First Mongol invasion of Poland.
During this tenure

Second Mongol invasion of Burma: Five weeks after beginning the siege of Myinsaing with no success, the Mongol invaders launch a major assault, but the Burmese defenders continue their defense for 12 days, leading to a truce.
During this tenure
In Asia, Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan is proclaimed as the Mongol Emperor Renzong of Yuan Dynasty China, 10 weeks after the death of his brother, Külüg Khan.
Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan
During this tenure
Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton: England recognises Scotland as an independent nation, after the Wars of Scottish Independence.
During this tenure
Second War of Scottish Independence: English forces relieve Stirling Castle, ending Edward III of England's last campaign in Scotland.
During this tenure

Within a month after the devastating earthquake the Ottomans besieged and captured the town of Gallipoli, making it the first Ottoman stronghold in Europe and the staging area for Ottoman expansion across the Balkans.
During this tenure
Ottoman Turks seize Filibe (Philippopolis) in Thrace in the Byzantine–Ottoman wars.
Ottoman Turks
During this tenure
Hundred Years' War: Charles V of France recaptures most of Aquitaine from the English.
During this tenure
Isabeau of Bavaria, who married King Charles V of France on July 17, 1385, is crowned as Queen consort of France..
During this tenure
The world's first quarantine station, the Lazzaretto Vecchio, is built in Venice, to protect against the Black Death.
quarantine
During this tenure
Ming dynasty Chinese Admiral Zheng He returns to Nanjing after his third voyage, and presents the ruler Vira Alakesvara, captured during the Ming–Kotte War, to China's Emperor Cheng Zu.
During this tenure
