The Aztec Empire is formed by the triple alliance of the Aztec city-states Tenochtitlán, Texcoco and Tlacopán and defeats Azcapotzalco to win control of the Valley of Mexico. Itzcóatl becomes 1st emperor.
Aztec Empire
During this tenure

georgia:Theodore_III_of_Georgia.bio: Theodore III was a 15th-century Georgian prelate mentioned as the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia in the documents dating from 1427 to 1434. Theodore was a close associate of King Alexander I of Georgia, with whom cooperated to restore the kingdom from the effects of the disastrous invasions by Timur earlier that century.
ev: Henry VI of England is crowned King of France at Notre-Dame de Paris.
During this tenure

georgia:David_III,_Catholicos-Patriarch_.bio: David III or IV was a 15th-century Catholicos-Patriarch of Georgia known from the group of documents dated from 1435 to 1439. They testify to David's efforts to restore the patriarchal see of Mtskheta from the devastation of Timur's invasions earlier that century. David's tenure coincided with the Council of Ferrara held from 1438 to 1439, at which the Georgian delegates rejected the union with the Roman Catholic Church.
ev: In Ming dynasty China, the inauguration of the Zhengtong-era Emperor Yingzong of Ming takes place.
Ming dynasty
During this tenure

georgia:Shio_II_of_Georgia.bio: Shio II was a 15th-century Georgian prelate mentioned as the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia in the documents dating from 1440 to 1443/47. Shio was a close associate of King Alexander I of Georgia, with whom he cooperated to restore the kingdom from the effects of the disastrous invasions by Timur earlier that century.
ev: King Henry VI of England summons the English Parliament, directing all members to assemble at Westminster on November 12.
During this tenure

georgia:David_IV,_Catholicos-Patriarch_o.bio: David IV or V was a 15th-century Catholicos-Patriarch of Georgia known from the group of documents dated from 1447 to 1457. They testify to David's efforts to restore the patriarchal see of Mtskheta from the devastation of Timur's invasions earlier that century. The scholarly opinion is divided as to whether David III is the same catholicos as David II (III) and David III (IV), mentioned in the years 1426–1428 and 1435–1439, respectively, or not.
ev: Hundred Years' War: The French invade Normandy.
During this tenure
At the University of Cambridge in England, Henry Abyngdon becomes the first person in the world to receive a degree of Bachelor of Music.
During this tenure
At the Battle of Valea Albă, fought at what is now Războieni in Romania, the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II defeats Stephen III of Moldavia.
During this tenure
Christopher Columbus sails from La Gomera in the Canary Islands, his final port of call before crossing the Atlantic Ocean for the first time.
During this tenure
The day before sighting land for the first time in a month, Columbus quells an attempt at mutiny by sailors who demand that he turn the Niña around to sail back to Spain.
During this tenure
King Louis XII of France and his troops seize Milan, driving out Duke Ludovico Sforza, and Leonardo da Vinci flees to Venice.
During this tenure
Ottoman–Venetian War: The Turkish fleet of Kemal Reis defeats the Venetians in the Second Battle of Lepanto.
During this tenure
In Venice, the envoy of the French king Louis XII delivers the declaration of war to the Venetian doge Leonardo Loredan, thus marking the official beginning of the War of the League of Cambrai.
During this tenure
Catherine of Aragon gives birth to her first child, and the first known child of King Henry VIII, a stillborn daughter.
During this tenure
Battle of Dubica (part of the Hundred Years' Croatian–Ottoman War): Croatian troops under Petar Berislavić, Ban (Viceroy) of Croatia, defeat an Ottoman army under Sanjak-bey Junuz-aga.
Battle of Dubica
During this tenure
Hernán Cortés enters Tenochtitlan, capital of the Aztec Empire, and appears at the court of Aztec ruler Moctezuma II.
During this tenure
The third Ottoman–Venetian War begins as the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent leads an invasion of the Republic of Venice. The war will continue until October 2, 1540.
During this tenure

georgia:Melchizedek_II_of_Georgia.bio: Melchizedek II was the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia in the years of c. 1538–1541 or in the periods of 1528-1529, 1540-1545, and 1548-1552. He was a son of King Constantine II of Kartli by his wife Tamar.
ev: The Parliament of Ireland is opened by King Henry VIII for a session that will last for two years.
During this tenure
King Henry VIII of England declares war on King Francis I of France, one month after sending an ultimatum.
During this tenure
The English Parliament, the first convened since the death of King Henry VIII, is opened by King Edward VI.
List of acts of the Parliament of England from 1547
During this tenure
Princess Elizabeth is imprisoned in the Tower of London on charges of working with the organizers of Wyatt's rebellion for the overthrow of Queen Mary of England.
During this tenure

georgia:Domentius_I_of_Georgia.bio: Domentius I was a Georgian churchman and the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia who presided over the Georgian Orthodox Church in the latter half of the 16th century. Surviving documents testify to Domentius' efforts to aggrandize the church's land properties and restore those holdings that had earlier been lost to secular noble landlords. According to the early-18th-century royal historian Prince Vakhushti, Domentius "was installed" as catholicos by King Simon I immediately after his accession to the throne of Kartli in eastern Georgia in 1556.
ev: The Treaty of Hampton Court, between Queen Elizabeth I of England and Huguenot leader Louis I, Prince of Condé, is signed.
During this tenure
The Holy League defeats the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto.
Battle of Lepanto
During this tenure

georgia:Nicholas_V_of_Georgia.bio: St. Nicholas V, also known as Nicholas VIII was the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia from 28 February 1584 to 1591. He was born into the Bagrationi dynasty of Kakheti, a son of King Levan (r. 1520–1574). He was canonized by the Georgian Orthodox Church as the Holy Father Nicholas the Catholicos of Georgia, his feast day marked on 18 February (N.S.: 2 March).
ev: Hundred Years' Croatian–Ottoman War: The Ottoman Empire successfully captures the Croatian rebel fort of Ripač.
During this tenure, at about age 62
William Shakespeare's play Titus Andronicus, is given its first performance, presented by the Admiral's Men company of players at The Rose in London.
During this tenure

georgia:Domentius_II_of_Georgia.bio: Domentius II was a Georgian churchman and the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia who presided over the Georgian Orthodox Church from c. 1595 to 1610. Like his predecessors, Domentius pushed for the efforts to aggrandize the church's land properties and restore the holdings that had earlier been lost to secular noble landlords. Some historians such as Kalistrate Salia consider this Domentius to have been the same person as the earlier Catholicos Domentius I, who might have occupied his office twice, with a significant gap of nearly four decades.
ev: Ottoman–Safavid War: The Safavid Army of Iran, led by Emperor Abbas the Great, recaptures Tabriz from the Ottoman Empire after 15 years of Ottoman occupation.
During this tenure
William Shakespeare's play, The Tragedie of Macbeth, is given its first performance, staged at the Globe Theatre in London.
During this tenure
The first known performance of William Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale, probably new this year, is given at the Globe Theatre in London.
During this tenure
The Treaty of Stolbovo ends the Ingrian War between Sweden and Russia. Sweden gains Ingria and Kexholm.
During this tenure

georgia:Zachary_of_Georgia.bio: Zachary, born Zakaria Jorjadze, was the Catholicos–Patriarch of the Georgian Orthodox Church in the period 1623–1632. Before that Zachary was the bishop of Nekresi in 1613–1623 and was the bishop of the Georgian royal Bagrationi dynasty.
ev: Francesca Caccini's opera La liberazione di Ruggiero has its premiere, stated in Florence in Italy. The opera will continue to be staged almost 400 years later, as late as the year 2018.
During this tenure, at about age 24

georgia:Eudemus_I_of_Georgia.bio: Eudemus I Diasamidze was a Georgian churchman serving as Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia from 1632 until his death in 1642. His demise was occasioned by his involvement in a plot against the Muslim king of Kartli, Rostom-Khan, who had him arrested and put to death in prison. He was buried in the Anchiskhati church in Tbilisi. Eudemus was canonized by the Georgian Orthodox Church as a "holy hieromartyr", his feast day marked on 17 October [O.S. 4 October].
ev: Galileo's Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems is published in Florence.
During this tenure, at about age 32
King Charles I of England, Scotland and Ireland is found guilty of high treason in a public session.
During this tenure

georgia:Domentius_III_of_Georgia.bio: Domentius III was a Georgian churchman and the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia from 1660 to 1676. He was a member of the princely Mukhrani branch of the Bagrationi dynasty, born as a younger son of Kaikhosro, Prince of Mukhrani. His regnal name is sometimes given as Domentius II. Domentius was a son of Kaikhosro, Prince of Mukhrani, born sometime before 1629. In 1649, he was ordained as an archbishop of Samtavro.
ev: Molière's L'Amour médecin is first presented, before Louis XIV, at the Palace of Versailles, with music by Jean-Baptiste Lully.
During this tenure
Franco-Dutch War – Battle of Turckheim: The French defeat Austria and Brandenburg.
During this tenure
Morean War: The Republic of Venice captures the fortress town of Igoumenitsa from the Ottoman Empire, and razes it to the ground.
During this tenure
Morean War: The navy of the Republic of Venice raids the Dalmatian coast, and attacks Ottoman Turkish strongholds in Greece.
During this tenure
Russo-Turkish War: Russia begins the Azov campaigns against the Ottoman Empire, with 31,000 troops departing to the Ottoman fortress at Azov on the Don River.
During this tenure
The Spanish conquest of Petén, and of Yucatán, is completed with the fall of Nojpetén, capital of the Itza Maya Kingdom, the last independent Maya state.
During this tenure
Richard Bentley at Cambridge in England introduces the first written (as opposed to oral) competitive examinations in a Western university.
Richard Bentley
During this tenure

georgia:Domentius_IV_of_Georgia.bio: Domentius IV was the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia from 1705 to 1724 and again from 1739 to 1741. He was a member of the royal Mukhrani branch of the Bagrationi dynasty, born as a younger son of Prince Levan of Kartli and his first wife Tuta Gurieli. Domentius was energetically involved in the politics of Kartli and, according to some contemporary accounts, he even had regal ambitions.
ev: George I, the new King of Great Britain and Ireland, arrives in Britain for the first time in his life, after having departed Hannover and sailing from the Netherlands.
During this tenure, at about age 37
The first (wooden) Putney Bridge is completed, as the only fixed crossing of the River Thames between London Bridge and Kingston, England.
Putney Bridge
During this tenure
Serse, an Italian opera by George Frideric Handel, premieres in London.
During this tenure
The War of the Hats: The Swedish army surrendered to the Russians in Helsinki, ending the war and starting Lesser Wrath.
During this tenure

georgia:Anton_I_of_Georgia.bio: Anton I (Georgian: ანტონ I; 28 October [O.S. 17 October] 1720 – 12 March [O.S. 1 March] 1788), born as Teimuraz Bagrationi, was the Catholicos–Patriarch of the Georgian Orthodox Church in the period 1744–1755 and again in 1764–1788.
ev: American Revolutionary War: Battle of Fort Washington – Hessian forces under Lieutenant General Wilhelm von Knyphausen capture Fort Washington (Manhattan) from the American Continental Army.
American Revolutionary War
During this tenure, at about age 56
Seven Years' War: French and Indian War – Battle of Restigouche: The British defeat French forces, in the last naval battle in New France.
During this tenure

georgia:Anton_II_of_Georgia.bio: Anton II the Great Martyr, born Prince Royal Teimuraz, was a member of the Georgian royal family and churchman. A son of Heraclius II, the penultimate King of Kartli and Kakheti, he was the Catholicos Patriarch of Georgia from 1788 to 1811. After the Russian Empire annexed Georgia in 1801, Anton resisted the encroachments from the Imperial officials in the Georgian church affairs. Eventually, Anton was forced to leave Georgia for St. Petersburg in 1810 and stripped of his office in 1811.
ev: The Russo-Ottoman Siege of Corfu ends with the surrender of the French garrison, bringing an end to the first period of French rule in the Ionian Islands.
During this tenure, at about age 37
War of the Sixth Coalition – Battle of La Rothière: Blücher's Allied army defeats the French under Napoleon.
War of the Sixth Coalition
During this tenure
Ottoman Empire Defeats the First Saudi State and captures Abdullah bin Saud Al Saud.
During this tenure
The world's first modern railway, the Stockton and Darlington Railway, opens in England.
During this tenure
Charles Darwin and the crew of arrive at South America for the first time.
During this tenure
Giacomo Meyerbeer's opera, Les Huguenots is performed for the first time in Paris, France.
During this tenure
The Great Exhibition of the Works of Industry of All Nations in the Crystal Palace, Hyde Park, London is opened by Queen Victoria.
During this tenure
Franco-Prussian War: Battle of Sedan – Prussian forces defeat the French armies and take Emperor Napoleon III and 100,000 of his soldiers prisoner at Sedan, France.
During this tenure
The Gokstad ship is found in Norway, the first Viking ship burial to be excavated.
Gokstad ship
During this tenure
April 10 (Easter Sunday) – The Catholic University of America is founded in Washington, D.C.
During this tenure
The Washington Monument officially opens to the general public in Washington, D.C.thumb|145px|right|[[October 9: Washington Monument opens.]].
During this tenure
Queen Victoria surpasses her grandfather King George III as the longest-reigning monarch in British history up to this time.
During this tenure
The second Olympic Games, Paris 1900, open (as part of the Paris World Exhibition).
During this tenure
The Ottoman Empire and the German Empire sign an agreement to build the Constantinople–Baghdad Railway.
During this tenure
The Lick Observatory announces the discovery on 3 December 1904 of a sixth moon of Jupiter, made by their astronomer Charles D. Perrine.
During this tenure
The London Electrobus Company starts running the first ever service of battery-electric buses between London's Victoria Station and Liverpool Street.
During this tenure
The Encyclopædia Britannica Eleventh Edition is published under American management in England, by Cambridge University Press.
Encyclopædia Britannica Eleventh Edition
During this tenure
A secret treaty between the Ottoman Empire and German Empires secures Ottoman neutrality.
Ottoman Empire
During this tenure
Armenian genocide: The Ottoman Empire transfers Armenians from its armed forces to unarmed Ottoman labour battalions.
During this tenure
Armenian genocide: 15,000 civilians from the Ottoman Armenian population of Bitlis are massacred by Ottoman Turks and Kurds.
Armenian genocide
During this tenure

georgia:Kyrion_II_of_Georgia.bio: St. Kyrion II was a Georgian religious figure and historian who served as the first Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia after the restoration of independence of the Georgian Orthodox Church from the Russian Orthodox Church in 1917 until his assassination in 1918. He was canonized by the Georgian Holy Synod in 2002.
ev: 13 – WWI: First Battle of Ramadi – British troops fail to take Ramadi from the Ottoman Empire; a majority of British casualties are due to extreme heat.
During this tenure, at about age 62

georgia:Leonid_of_Georgia.bio: Leonid was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia from 1918 to 1921, leading the Georgian Orthodox Church during the Georgian Democratic Republic.
ev: The Third Transjordan attack ends with ANZAC Mounted Division victory at the Second Battle of Amman, with the subsequent capture at Ziza of the Ottoman II Corps, and more than 10,000 Ottoman and German prisoners.
Third Transjordan attack
During this tenure, at about age 57

georgia:Ambrosius_of_Georgia.bio: St. Ambrosius was a Georgian religious figure and scholar who served as the Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia from 1921 to 1927. Best known for his opposition to the Soviet regime, he was canonized in 1995 by the Georgian Orthodox Church as Saint Ambrosius the Confessor (ამბროსი აღმსარებელი, Ambrosi Aghmsarebeli).
ev: Luxury goods brand Gucci is founded in Florence, Italy.
Luxury goods
During this tenure, at about age 60

georgia:Christophorus_III.bio: Christophorus III was a Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia from 1927 until his death in 1932. His tenure coincided with the increasingly repressive Soviet rule in Georgia.
ev: The first transatlantic telephone call is made via radio from New York City, United States, to London, United Kingdom.
During this tenure, at about age 54

georgia:Callistratus_of_Georgia.bio: St. Callistratus was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia from June 21, 1932, until his death. His full title was His Holiness and Beatitude, Archbishop of Mtskheta-Tbilisi and Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia.
ev: Buck Rogers in the 25th Century debuts on American radio. It is the first science fiction program on radio.
During this tenure, at about age 66

georgia:Melchizedek_III_of_Georgia.bio: Melchizedek III was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia from 1952 until his death. His full title was His Holiness and Beatitude, Archbishop of Mtskheta-Tbilisi and Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia. Born Mikheil Pkhaladze (მიხეილ ფხალაძე) in the Tiflis Governorate, Russian Empire, the future prelate received his education at the theological colleges of Tiflis, and Kazan in Russia. He then taught at various seminaries in Russia and Georgia. In 1915, Melchizedek was ordained to the priesthood.
ev: The Treaty of Taipei between Japan and the Republic of China goes into effect, officially ending the Second Sino-Japanese War.
During this tenure, at about age 80

georgia:Ephraim_II_of_Georgia.bio: Ephraim II was Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia from 1960 until his death. His full title was His Holiness and Beatitude, Archbishop of Mtskheta-Tbilisi and Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia. Born as Grigol Sidamonidze, the future prelate graduated from the Tiflis Theological Seminary in 1918 and from the Tbilisi State University with a degree in philosophy in 1925. He became a monk in 1922. At various times, from 1927 to 1960, he served as bishop of Nikortsminda, bishop of Gelati and Kutaisi, and metropolitan of Batumi-Shemokmedi and Chkondidi.
ev: The world's first standard gauge passenger preserved railway, the Bluebell Railway, opens to the public in southern England.
standard gauge
During this tenure, at about age 64

georgia:David_V,_Catholicos-Patriarch_of.bio: David V, born as Khariton Devdariani was a Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia from July 2, 1972, until his death. His full title was His Holiness and Beatitude, Archbishop of Mtskheta-Tbilisi and Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia. Born in the village of Mirotsminda (now Kharagauli Municipality, Imereti), David became a priest in 1927 and a bishop in 1956. From 1959 to 1972 he served as a chorbishop to Catholicos-Patriarch Ephraim II, upon whose death he succeeded to the position of primate of the Georgian Orthodox Church.
ev: Apollo program: Eugene Cernan becomes the last person to walk on the Moon until 2028 at the earliest, after he and Harrison Schmitt complete the third and final extra-vehicular activity (EVA) of Apollo 17.
During this tenure, at about age 69

georgia:Ilia_II_of_Georgia.bio: Ilia II was the Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia from 1977 until his death in 2026. He was the longest serving patriarch in the history of the Georgian Orthodox Church, which spans more than a millennium. Born in Ordzhonikidze (modern-day Vladikavkaz, Russia), to a Georgian Orthodox family, he studied at the Moscow Theological Academy from 1956 to 1960. During that time he became a monk and was also ordained to the priesthood. Ilia served as bishop of Batumi and Shemokmedi from 1963 to 1967 and as bishop of Sukhumi and Abkhazia from 1967 to 1977.
ev: Optical fiber is first used to carry live telephone traffic, as an Italian company in Turin, Centro Studi e Laboratori Telecomunicazioni (CSELT) begins operation of two telephone exchanges.
During this tenure, at about age 44

georgia:Shio_III_of_Georgia.bio: Shio III is the Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia. He was previously the bishop of Senaki and Chkhorotsku from 2003 to 2026 and locum tenens of the Patriarchal Throne from 2017 to 2026. Born in Tbilisi, Soviet Georgia, he studied at the Moscow Theological Academy and Saint Tikhon's Orthodox University. He became a monk in 1993 and was also ordained to the priesthood in 1996. In 2003, Mujiri was made the bishop of the new eparchy of Senaki and Chkhorotsku, and was also placed in charge of parishes in Australia and New Zealand in 2009.
ev: NASA launches the Artemis II lunar flyby mission, marking the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972.
During this tenure, at about age 57
Qian Fei Di, then Ming Di, becomes ruler of the Liu Song dynasty after his nephew is assassinated.
Emperor Qianfei of Liu Song
During this tenure

jerusalem:Martyrius_of_Jerusalem.tag: Former monastery in the West Bank.
jerusalem:Martyrius_of_Jerusalem.bio: Monastery of Martyrius, whose ruins, known as Khirbet el-Murassas in Arabic, have been excavated in the centre of the West Bank settlement and city of Ma'ale Adumim, was one of the most important centres of monastic life in the Judean Desert during the Byzantine period. It was active between the second half of the 5th and the mid-7th century.
ev: The first Shinto shrines are built in Japan.
Shinto
During this tenure
The Burgundians, under King Gundobad, cross the Alps and plunder Liguria. Many Romans are taken into captivity.
Burgundians
During this tenure

jerusalem:Elias_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Elias of Jerusalem was a bishop and Patriarch of Jerusalem from 494 until he was deposed by Byzantine Emperor Anastasius I in 516 for supporting the decrees of the Council of Chalcedon. Elias was an Arab, by birth, who had been educated in a monastery in Egypt. At the Synod of Sidon (512) he successfully defended, together with Flavian II of Antioch, the dyophysite Christological doctrine proclaimed by the Council of Chalcedon.
ev: King Kavadh I hands over the fortress-city of Amida, and agrees to an armistice with the Byzantine Empire.
Kavadh I
During this tenure, at about age 54

jerusalem:John_III_of_Jerusalem.bio: John III, was a 6th Century bishop of Jerusalem. John of Jerusalem was the son of a certain Marcian, who was bishop of Sebaste in Samaria. He was bishop in 516–524 AD. John III anathematized all the opponents of the Council of Chalcedon. He died on April 20, 524, according to Cyril of Scythopolis. The feast of John III, together with that of the Emperor Marcian (450–457) was in the Church of the Apostles on July 9, according to the Palestinian-Georgian calendar.
ev: Ma`adikarib Ya`fur becomes king, supported by the Aksumites; he begins a military campaign against the Arabian tribes.
Kingdom of Aksum
During this tenure, at about age 71

jerusalem:Peter_of_Jerusalem.bio: Peter of Jerusalem was the Patriarch of Jerusalem from 524 to 544. He held to the Chalcedonian belief.
ev: The Plague of Justinian strikes the Mediterranean world.
Plague of Justinian
During this tenure

jerusalem:Macarius_II_of_Jerusalem.bio: Macarius II of Jerusalem was the Patriarch of Jerusalem for two periods from 544 to 552 and from 564 to 574. He was patriarch during the era of the Christological disputes in the latter part of the reign of emperor Justinian. The early life of Macarius is unknown. Upon the death of Patr. Peter in 544, the Origenist monks of Jerusalem installed Macarius as patriarch of Jerusalem. However, emperor Justinian, who was staunchly Orthodox, favored Eustochius, the Oeconomus of the Church of Alexandria.
ev: Siege of Rome: The Ostrogoths under Totila besiege Rome for the third time, after Belisarius has returned to Constantinople. He offers a peace agreement, but this is rejected by Emperor Justinian I.
Siege of Rome (549-550)
During this tenure

jerusalem:Eustochius_of_Jerusalem.bio: Eustochius of Jerusalem was the patriarch of Jerusalem from 552 to 564. He was patriarch during the time of the Christological disputes during the reign of emperor Justinian I. After the death of Patr. Peter of Jerusalem in 544, a group of Origenist monks in Jerusalem elected Marcarius II, an Origenist, the Patriarch of Jerusalem. However, emperor Justinian I, who was staunchly Orthodox, favored Eustochius, who was Oeconomus of the Church of Alexandria although he lived in Constantinople.
ev: Chlothar I is crowned King of the Franks.
During this tenure
Battle of Solachon: A Byzantine army under command of Philippicus defeats the Sassanid Persians, near Dara.
Battle of Solachon
During this tenure

jerusalem:Amos_of_Jerusalem.bio: Amos of Jerusalem was the patriarch of the Church of Jerusalem from 594 to 601, having succeeded as patriarch after John IV. Little is known of the life of Amos. He apparently found it difficult to exercise his authority as patriarch, particularly in his relations with the abbot of the New Lavra, as Pope Gregory found it necessary to write to Amos and Anastasius (Athanasius?) requesting that they suppress the secular life of the monks at the monastery that was next to the Nea Church.
ev: Loma Caldera (El Salvador) erupts, burying the Maya village of Joya de Cerén.
Loma Caldera
During this tenure, at about age 50

Byzantine–Persian War: King Khosrau II captures the Byzantine positions east of the Euphrates; the Persians destroy many cities in the Levant region, after prolonged sieges such as the Byzantine fortress of Dara.
Byzantine-Sassanid War of 602–628
During this tenure

jerusalem:Zacharias_of_Jerusalem.bio: Zacharias of Jerusalem was the Patriarch of Jerusalem of the Church of Jerusalem from 609 to 632. Zacharias spent most of his patriarchate as a prisoner of the Sasanian Emperor Khosrow II following the Sasanian conquest of Jerusalem. He is commemorated by the Orthodox Church on February 21. He is also venerated in the Catholic Church, where he is known mostly for the sacramental called the "Plague Cross of Saint Zacharias of Jerusalem". The early life of Zacharias is unknown. He was elected patriarch in 609.
ev: Battle of Qianshuiyuan: The Tang dynasty scores a decisive victory over their rival Xue Rengao.
During this tenure, at about age 68

jerusalem:Modestus_of_Jerusalem.bio: Saint Modestus of Jerusalem was Patriarch of Jerusalem from 632–634. He is commemorated as a saint by the Catholic Church on December 17, and by the Eastern Orthodox Church, on May 17, March 29 or December 16. The Palestinian-Georgian calendar venerates him on December 16 and October 19 in the Acta Sanctorum.
ev: The Tuyuhun Kingdom is invaded by Chinese forces under Li Jing (Tang dynasty) during Emperor Taizong's campaign against Tuyuhun, resulting in the murder of their leader (khan) Murong Fuyun in 635.
Tuyuhun Kingdom
During this tenure, at about age 97

jerusalem:Anastasius_II_of_Jerusalem.bio: Anastasius II of Jerusalem was patriarch of the Church of Jerusalem from an unknown date until 706 as the see of Jerusalem came under control of the nascent Muslim caliphate, and church life was disrupted by the Monothelite controversy. The records for the Patriarchate of Jerusalem after the reign of Patriarch Sophronius are sparse and tempered by Muslim interventions. After the death of Sophronius in 638, Bishop Stephen of Dora served as a Patriarchal Vicar, assisted by John of Philadelphia (Amman).
ev: King Ergica of the Visigoths accuses the Jews of aiding the Muslims, and sentences all Jews to slavery.
During this tenure

jerusalem:John_V_of_Jerusalem.bio: John V was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem. John V of Jerusalem was the patriarch of Jerusalem during the iconoclastic struggles under the Byzantine emperor Leo III the Isaurian as well as the time of persecution in Palestine and Syria under Muslim rulers. John, who was a monk, succeeded Patriarch Anastasius II as patriarch of Jerusalem in 706. He was a friend of John of Damascus and ordained him to the priesthood shortly after John of Damascus entered the monastery to become a monk.
ev: Arab–Byzantine War: Muslim forces under Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik resume their expedition against Anatolia. In a large-scale raid they plunder the fortress city of Caesarea.
Arab–Byzantine wars
During this tenure, at about age 76

jerusalem:Theodore_of_Jerusalem.bio: Theodorus of Jerusalem, also Theodore was the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem. The dates of his patriarchate vary, from 745-770 to 760-782. Theodorus saw, during his episcopate, a severe persecution of the Christians and Jews in Palestine by the Muslim ruler Abdallah ibn Ali, who demanded extremely high taxes from Christians and placed harsh restrictions on them: forbidding nocturnal vigils, confiscating sacred vessels, and demanding removal of crosses from all the churches. Abdallah required Christians and Jews to bear distinctive markings.
ev: The Franks under Pepin III invade Italy, and defeat the Lombards under King Aistulf, in the Susa Valley (Piedmont). He enforces the terms, including cession of the Exarchate of Ravenna to Rome.
Franks
During this tenure, at about age 53

jerusalem:Elias_II_of_Jerusalem.bio: Elias II was the Patriarch of Jerusalem in 770–797. He was patriarch during the reign of Caliph Harun al-Rashid and during the Arab tribal wars in Palestine between the late 780s and 796. His patriarchate saw the plundering of the St. Chariton Monastery and the assault on the Mar Saba Monastery, in which some twenty monks were killed by tribal marauders.
ev: Charlemagne issues the Admonitio generalis, which covers educational and ecclesiastical reforms within the Frankish Kingdom.
Admonitio generalis
During this tenure, at about age 39

jerusalem:George_of_Jerusalem.bio: George of Jerusalem was the Patriarch of Jerusalem from 797 until his death. Little is known about his activities while he was patriarch. At the time, the Church of Jerusalem was under the Abbasid Caliphate. George was the syncellus of Patriarch Elias II before he became patriarch about 797. During the final years before the death of Patriarch Elias, Syncellus George sent a delegation to western Europe to Charlemagne to gain the help and protection of the Franks against the Muslims in the Holy Lands.
ev: Pagan Danes invade Obodrite-ruled Schleswig, to take over territory almost emptied by the forcible deportations of the Saxons by emperor Charlemagne.
Danes
During this tenure

jerusalem:Thomas_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Thomas I of Jerusalem, also known in Persian as Tamriq, was the Patriarch of Jerusalem of the Church of Jerusalem from 807 to 821. Patriarch Thomas held a firm Orthodox theological position and opposed both the iconoclasts and the filioque. He is considered a saint, commemorated in May 16.
ev: Danish Viking raiders, led by King Horik I, attack Vestfold, due to its insubordination.
Vikings
During this tenure, at about age 63
Prince Li Zhan, 14 years old, is enthroned as the Emperor Jingzong of China, four days after the death of his father, Emperor Muzong.
During this tenure
Third Civil War: King Louis the German, grandson of Charlemagne, invades Swabia. His nephew, Pepin II of Aquitaine, and his Gascon subjects, conquer territory all the way to the Loire.
Louis the Pious
During this tenure

jerusalem:Theodosius_of_Jerusalem_(died_.bio: Theodosius of Jerusalem was Patriarch of the Church of Jerusalem from 864 to 879. Theodosius was a monk at a monastery near Jerusalem before he was elected the successor to Patriarch Solomon in 864. Theodosius was represented at the council held in Constantinople between 869-870 by his legate, syncellus Elijah. Elijah signed the decisions of the council that deposed Patriarch Photius of Constantinople and decreed that Patriarch Ignatius was improperly deposed.
ev: Louis II, Holy Roman Emperor, defeats the Saracen invaders who are ravaging southern Italy.
Louis II, Holy Roman Emperor
During this tenure

jerusalem:Elias_III_of_Jerusalem.bio: Elias III was the Patriarch of Jerusalem from about 879 to 907. According to the annals of Eutychius of Alexandria, he was a descendant of the family of Mansur ibn Sarjun, the grandfather of John of Damascus. There is evidence that he sent a circular letter to European rulers asking for financial help in restoring the churches in his diocese. One of them was received by the Carolingian Emperor Charles the Fat in 881, and another was probably sent to king Alfred the Great.
ev: Battle of the Conwy: King Anarawd of Gwynedd (Wales) initiates a revenge attack on the Mercian armies, and defeats them on the River Conwy.
Battle of the Conwy
During this tenure, at about age 31
Emperor Taizu (Zhu Wen) of Later Liang has the 15-year-old Li Zhu, the last Tang Dynasty emperor, poisoned. Li Zhu receives the posthumous name of Ai ("lamentable").
During this tenure

jerusalem:Leontius_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Leontius I of Jerusalem, also Leo, was Patriarch of Jerusalem of the Church of Jerusalem from 911 to 928. Little is known about his activities while he was patriarch.
ev: Battle of Tempsford: The English army led by Edward the Elder defeats the Danish Vikings at Tempsford. They storm the fortified burh and kill King Guthrum II of East Anglia, along with the Danish Jarls Toglos and Manna.
Battle of Tempsford
During this tenure
Shi Jingtang is enthroned as the first emperor of the Later Jin by Tai Zong, ruler of the Khitan-led Liao Dynasty, following a revolt against his rival, emperor Fei of Later Tang.
During this tenure

jerusalem:Christodulus_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Christodulus I of Jerusalem, also Christopher, was Melkite Patriarch of Jerusalem of the Church of Jerusalem from 937 to 951. Early in his patriarchate he was confronted with Muslim rioting and church destruction. Originally named Habib; he was from Caesarea. He took the name Christodulus when he became the patriarch of Jerusalem. He succeeded Nicholas who was patriarch for a very short time in 937, and had been killed before the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.
ev: Narita-san ("New victory temple"), a Shingon Buddhist temple, is founded in Chiba (Japan).
Narita-san
During this tenure
The Tiger Hill Pagoda (or Huqui Tower) is built in the city of Suzhou, located in Jiangsu Province (Eastern China).
Tiger Hill Pagoda
During this tenure

jerusalem:John_VII_of_Jerusalem.bio: John VII was Patriarch of Jerusalem from 964 to 966. He was among the bishops of Jerusalem who is believed to have suffered a martyr's death at the hands of Muslim mobs. He was elected patriarch after the death of his predecessor Agathon in 964. Two versions of his martyrdom have come down to us. The first involved revenge by the ruling governor. John became patriarch during the rule of the Ikhshidid governor Muhammad Ismail ibn al-Sanaji in Jerusalem.
ev: The Hungarians invade the Bulgarian Empire and force Peter I, emperor (tsar) of the Bulgarians, to conclude a peace treaty with them. He lets them cross to attack the Byzantine Empire.
Principality of Hungary
During this tenure

jerusalem:Christodolus_II_of_Jerusalem.bio: Christodulus II of Jerusalem was the Melkite patriarch of Church of Jerusalem from 966 to 969. He previously was known as Habib of Caesarea. Patriarch Christodulus began to restore the Church of the Holy Sepulchre that had been damaged by fire during the riots in 966, but was unable to finish the restoration because of his sudden death while visiting Cairo.
ev: The Fatimids found Cairo.
Cairo
During this tenure

jerusalem:Joseph_II_of_Jerusalem.bio: Joseph II of Jerusalem was the patriarch of the Church of Jerusalem from 981 to 983. Little is known of his life. It was during his episcopate that Sadaqah Ibn Bishr, the Patriarchal syncellus, was able to complete the renovation of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre that had been damaged by fire during riots in 966. Joseph was a philosopher and a physician as well as a generous almsgiver. In 985, he, like Christodulus II earlier, died in Cairo.
ev: King Harald Bluetooth orders the construction of the Viking ring fortress of Trelleborg.
Harald Bluetooth
During this tenure

jerusalem:Theophilus_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Theophilus I of Jerusalem was the patriarch of the Church of Jerusalem from 1012 to 1020. Theophilus was Bishop of Hibal before his appointment as Patriarch of Jerusalem by Mufarrij ibn Daghfal ibn al-Jarrah, the autonomous ruler of Palestine. The appointment occurred under the rule of Fatimid Caliph al-Hakim. Mufarrij suggested that the Christian community should re-build the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.
ev: King Cnut the Great of Denmark launches an invasion of Mercia and Northumbria in England.
Cnut the Great
During this tenure

jerusalem:Nicephorus_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Nicephorus I of Jerusalem was the patriarch of the Church of Jerusalem from 1020 to 1048. He was appointed by the Fatimid Caliph al-Hakim. After his appointment, Patriarch Nicephorus visited Al-Hakim at his capital in Egypt. He pleaded with him about the persecutions of the Christians in the Holy Land and asked Al-Hakim's protection for both himself and the Christians. The Caliph agreed to provide protection. After the death of Al-Hakim in 1021, Emperor Romanus III Argyrus and Ali az-Zahir, the son of Al-Hakim, made peace in 1030.
ev: August 27 – The Cairo Canal is opened in Fatimid Egypt in a ceremony that includes the Caliph al-Zahir.
During this tenure, at about age 74
The city of Oslo is founded by King Harald Hardrada of Norway.
Oslo
During this tenure
Sack of Rome: Duke Robert Guiscard leads a Norman army north and enters Rome; the city is sacked, and Henry IV is forced to retreat.
During this tenure

jerusalem:Simeon_II_of_Jerusalem.bio: Simeon II or Symeon II was a Greek Orthodox patriarch of Jerusalem in the 11th century. Simeon was appointed patriarch in the 1080s. Pope Urban II addressed a letter to him, urging him to acknowledge papal primacy to achieve the union of the Roman Catholic and Greek Orthodox churches. Patriarch Nicholas III of Constantinople warned Simeon against accepting the pope's offer, reminding him about the Orthodox views about the Eucharist, papal primacy and the Filioque.
ev: King William the Conqueror calls for a meeting at Old Sarum, where he invites his major vassals and tenants-in-chief to swear allegiance to him. This is known as the Oath of Salisbury.
During this tenure, at about age 36
A comet is seen and reported by several civilisations around the world. Lasting for 40 days, the comet grows steadily in brightness until finally fading away.
During this tenure
The construction of Liuhe Pagoda ("Six Harmonies Pagoda") in Hangzhou is completed in Song dynasty China.
Liuhe Pagoda
During this tenure

A Zangid expedition under General Shirkuh accompanied by his nephew Saladin invades Egypt. King Amalric I of Jerusalem orders his fleet to return to Acre and retreats with the Crusaders back to Palestine.
Shirkuh
During this tenure
Portuguese forces under King Afonso I (the Conqueror) capture the city of Beja from the Almohads.
Afonso I of Portugal
During this tenure
The Mongol General Subutai withdraws eastward after the victory at the Battle of the Kalka River, after General Jebe has died.
During this tenure

jerusalem:Athanasius_II_of_Jerusalem.bio: Athanasius II was the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem from c. 1231 to 1244. The Church of the Holy Sepulchre seems to have been largely in Athanasius' hands during the Latin control of Jerusalem. The Serbian Archbishop Sava (1174–1237) was the guest of Athanasius twice in the Holy Land, and according to Serbian chronicles they were good friends. After the Latin retreat from Jerusalem in 1244, the Melkites (who were the majority of the south of the Latin kingdom) turned to Athanasius.
ev: The original set of woodblocks of the Tripitaka Koreana is destroyed by fire during the Second Mongol invasion of Korea.
Tripitaka Koreana
During this tenure, at about age 131
Mongol conquest of the Song dynasty: The Mongols under Ögedei Khan penetrate deep into the Southern Song. The important city of Xiangyang, gateway to the Yangtze plain, capitulates to them.
Mongol conquest of the Song dynasty
During this tenure
The 8th Parliament of King Henry IV of England is opened, with Thomas Chaucer as Speaker of the House of Commons.
During this tenure
The Ottoman sultan Murad II besieges Constantinople; the siege is broken off as a result of the rebellion of Küçük Mustafa.
During this tenure
The Republic of Venice signs a treaty with the Ottoman Empire to end the eight-year war between the two nations after the Ottoman capture of Thessalonica, replacing the previous agreement of 1419.
During this tenure
King Matyas of Hungary issues a declaration of war against King Jiri of Bohemia, starting a war that will last 10 years.
During this tenure
Cuauhtémoc becomes the last Aztec Emperor after the death from smallpox of the Emperor Cuitláhuac, who reigned for only 80 days.
During this tenure
After heavy losses by the Ottoman Empire, the Siege of Eger in Hungary is broken off by the Ottomans.
During this tenure
February 2 (Candlemas night) – In London, the first known production of William Shakespeare's comedy Twelfth Night takes place.
During this tenure

jerusalem:Theophanes_III_of_Jerusalem.bio: Theophanes III of Jerusalem was the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem from 1608 to 1644. As the successor to Sophronius IV, Theophanes continued Sophronius' defense of Orthodox rights to the Christian shrines in the Holy Lands. In 1611, with a decree from the Ottoman sultan, Theophanes stopped the Armenian Patriarchate of Jerusalem from taking over the celebration of the Holy Light.
ev: In Japan, a treaty is signed between Spanish nobleman Rodrigo de Vivero, former Governor-General of the Philippines and the former shogun Tokugawa Ieyasu, for the establishment of a Spanish factory in eastern Japan.
During this tenure, at about age 39
First Anglo-Dutch War: The English navy defeats the Dutch fleet in the Battle of the Gabbard after a two-day fight.
During this tenure

jerusalem:Patriarch_Nectarius_of_Jerusal.bio: Nectarius of Jerusalem, born Nikolaos Pelopidis, was the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem from 1661 to 1669.
ev: King Charles II of England leaves London with his entourage, fleeing the Great Plague. He moves his court to Salisbury, then Oxford.
During this tenure, at about age 63

jerusalem:Patriarch_Dositheos_II_of_Jeru.bio: Dositheus II Notaras of Jerusalem was the Patriarch of Jerusalem between 1669 and 1707 and a theologian of the Eastern Orthodox Church. He was known for standing against influences of the Roman Catholic and Protestant churches. He convened the Synod of Jerusalem in 1672 to counter the Calvinist confessions alleged to be from Cyril Lucaris.
ev: Morean War: Siege of Santa Maura – The Republic of Venice captures the Ottoman island fortress of Santa Maura.
During this tenure, at about age 43

jerusalem:Chrysanthus_of_Jerusalem.bio: Chrysanthus Notaras, also known as Chrysanthus of Jerusalem, was Patriarch of Jerusalem and a scholar in Eastern Orthodoxy. He was a mathematician, astronomer, geographer, and author. He is known for creating modern maps in the Greek language. He was one of Giovanni Domenico Cassini's students. He also built astronomical equipment.
ev: Old Dock, Liverpool, England, the world's first enclosed commercial wet dock (Thomas Steers, engineer), opens.
During this tenure, at about age 60

jerusalem:Meletius_of_Jerusalem.bio: Meletius was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem. He was born in Turkey.
ev: George Frideric Handel's opera Ariodante is premièred at the Royal Opera House in Covent Garden, London.
During this tenure, at about age 85

jerusalem:Parthenius_of_Jerusalem.bio: Parthenius was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem. He was born in Athens. He attended the Council of Constantinople in 1755.
ev: The Qianlong Emperor of China visits the southern capital of Nanjing for the first time, bringing with him 3,000 staff and 6,690 horses and stays for four days.
During this tenure, at about age 61

jerusalem:Ephram_II.bio: Ephram II was a Greek writer. He was born in Athens. He was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem (1766 – April 26, 1770).
ev: Battle of Aspindza: Georgian king Erekle II defeats the Ottoman forces, despite being abandoned by an ally, Russian General Totleben.
During this tenure, at about age 20

jerusalem:Sophronius_V_of_Jerusalem.bio: Sophronius II of Constantinople served as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople during the period 1775–1780 and, as Sophronius V, Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem in 1771–1774. Before his elevation to the patriarchates of Jerusalem and Constantinople, he was a major Arabic-speaking Orthodox intellectual and churchman in the circle of Patriarch Sylvester of Antioch. He was born in Aleppo, Syria.
ev: The popular (and enduring) comedy She Stoops to Conquer, by Irish playwright Oliver Goldsmith, is performed for the first time, premiering at London's Covent Garden Theatre.
During this tenure, at about age 63

jerusalem:Abraham_II_of_Jerusalem.bio: Abraham II was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem.
ev: American Revolutionary War – Battle of Germantown: Troops under George Washington are repelled by British troops under Sir William Howe.
During this tenure, at about age 127

jerusalem:Procopius_I.bio: Procopius I was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem.
ev: Treaty of Versailles signed, forming an alliance between the Kingdom of France and the Lord Nguyễn Phúc Ánh, future Emperor of Vietnam.
During this tenure

jerusalem:Patriarch_Anthemus_of_Jerusale.bio: Anthimus was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem. Manuscripts belonging to him were taken to England by Joseph Dacre Carlyle.
ev: 22 – Revolt of Cairo: Napoleon Bonaparte suppresses a revolt in Cairo. French occupation survives but becomes more dependent on force and administration.
During this tenure, at about age 81

jerusalem:Polycarpus_of_Jerusalem.bio: Polycarpus was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem.
ev: War of the Sixth Coalition – Battle of Montereau: A French army led by Napoleon is victorious against Austrian forces.
During this tenure, at about age 64

jerusalem:Athanasius_V_of_Jerusalem.bio: Athanasius V was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem. He was born in Edirne.
ev: Britain abolishes slavery across most of its empire.
Slavery Abolition Act 1833
During this tenure, at about age 79

jerusalem:Patriarch_Cyril_II_of_Jerusale.bio: Cyril II of Jerusalem; was a 19th-century Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem.
ev: Giuseppe Verdi's opera La traviata premieres at La Fenice in Venice, but is poorly received at this time.
During this tenure, at about age 61

jerusalem:Procopius_II.bio: Procopius II was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem.
ev: American Indian Wars: Modoc War: First Battle of the Stronghold – Modoc Indians defeat the United States Army.
During this tenure, at about age 83

jerusalem:Hierotheus_of_Jerusalem.bio: Hierotheus was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem.
ev: Russo-Turkish War: Battle of Shipka Pass IV – Russian and Bulgarian forces defeat the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure, at about age 60

jerusalem:Nicodemus_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Nicodemus I was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem. He was born in Constantinople. In 1890 he built a summer house near the San Simon monastery in Katamon.
ev: The Royal Holloway College for women is opened by Queen Victoria, near London, England.
During this tenure, at about age 58

jerusalem:Gerasimus_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Gerasimus I was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem from March 11, 1891, to February 21, 1897. It was during his administration as Patriarch of Jerusalem that the full significance of the mosaic map found on the church floor in Madaba was understood. In 1885, Gerasimus was the Bishop of Scythopolis, a city just south of the Sea of Galilee.
ev: Booker T. Washington High School (Houston) is founded as "Colored High", the first African-American high school in Houston, Texas.
Booker T. Washington High School (Houston)
During this tenure, at about age 54

jerusalem:Damian_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Damian I was Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem from 1897 to 1931. During the patriarchate of Damian I of Jerusalem, the Greek Orthodox Church expanded its rural land acquisitions in Palestine, including the 1909 purchase of 600 dunams south of Caesarea’s Roman road from Ottoman governor Sadeq Pasha. This acquisition formed part of a wider strategy of establishing agricultural estates in areas of religious and strategic significance, supported by Russian imperial patronage in the late Ottoman period.
ev: Italian Dorando Pietri wins the Olympic marathon (run from Windsor Castle to London) in one of the most dramatic arrivals in Olympic history, only to be disqualified soon afterwards for receiving assistance; victory is awarded to Irish-American Johnny Hayes.
During this tenure, at about age 60

jerusalem:Benedict_I_of_Jerusalem.bio: Patriarch Benedict of Jerusalem, also Benediktos I of Jerusalem, born Vasileios Papadopoulos was the Patriarch of Jerusalem of the Greek Orthodox Church of Jerusalem from 1957 to 1980.
ev: Apollo program: Apollo 10 returns to Earth, after a successful 8-day test of all the components needed for the upcoming first crewed Moon landing.
Apollo 10
During this tenure, at about age 77

jerusalem:Patriarch_Diodoros_of_Jerusale.bio: Diodoros or Diodorus Greek: Διόδωρος; born Damianos G. Karivalis Greek: Δαμιανός Γ. Καρίβαλης (14 August 1923 – 20 December 2000) was the Patriarch of Jerusalem in the Eastern Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem from 1980 to 2000. He was born on the Greek island of Chios on 14 August 1923. He became a monk in 1943 and was renamed Diodoros. Three years later he became a priest, then the titular archbishop of the archdiocese of Hierapolis in Phrygia in 1965.
ev: TAT-8, the first transatlantic telephone cable to use optical fibers, is completed. This led to more robust connections between the American and European Internet.
TAT-8
During this tenure, at about age 65

jerusalem:Irenaios_of_Jerusalem.bio: Emmanouil Skopelitis was, under the name Irenaios, the 140th patriarch of the Greek Orthodox Church of Jerusalem, from his election in 2000 when he succeeded Patriarch Diodoros, until his dismissal in 2005, when he was succeeded by Patriarch Theophilos III.
ev: SMART-1, an ESA spaceprobe and ESA's first mission to the moon, is launched from Kourou, French Guiana.
During this tenure, at about age 64

jerusalem:Patriarch_Theophilos_III_of_Je.bio: Theophilos III is the current Greek Orthodox patriarch of Jerusalem since 2005. He is styled Patriarch of the Holy City of Jerusalem and all Palestine, Syria, Arabia, beyond the Jordan River, Cana of Galilee, and Holy Zion. Theophilos (also spelled Theofilos or Theophilus) was elected unanimously on 22 August 2005 by the Holy Synod of Jerusalem as the 141st primate of the Orthodox Church of Jerusalem, succeeding the deposed Irenaios.
ev: NASA, ESA, the Canadian Space Agency and the Space Telescope Science Institute launch the James Webb Space Telescope, the successor of the Hubble Space Telescope.
During this tenure, at about age 69

alexandria:Gainas_of_Alexandria.bio: Gaianus was the Patriarch of Alexandria for three months in 535. Following the death of Patriarch Timothy IV on 7 February 535, there was a double election to fill the vacant patriarchate. The two main parties in Alexandria at the time were the Severans, followers of Severus of Antioch, and the Julianists, followers of Julian of Halicarnassus. The former elected the deacon Theodosius while the latter elected Gaianus, who had been archdeacon under Timothy IV.
ev: Gothic War: Belisarius crosses the Strait of Messina and invades Italy. He conquers the city of Rhegium and advances to Naples.
Gothic War (535–554)
During this tenure
Siege of Rome: King Vitiges of the Ostrogoths ends his siege and abandons Rome. He retreats with his Gothic army northeast along the Via Flaminia.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Zoilus_of_Alexandri.bio: Zoilus served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 541 and 551. Zacharias Rhetor reports on how Patriarch Paul of Alexandria was involved in a murder. He was consequently deposed and replaced by Zoilus (in 539/540). Acacius was the military officer tasked to protect Zoilus from the hostile population of Alexandria. Zacharia details: "Ephraim of Antioch was sent to Alexandria, and Abraham Bar Khili [accompanied him]; and, as they passed through Palestine, they took with them a monk named Zoilus.
ev: King Khosrau I signs a five year truce with the Byzantine Empire, but war continues to ravage the Caucasus region, especially in Armenia.
Khosrau I
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Apollinarius_of_Ale.bio: Apollinarius served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 551 and 569. Before his appointment by Justinian I, he was a reader of the monastery of Salama.
ev: King Chlothar I reunites the Frankish Kingdom after his brother Childebert I dies, becoming sole ruler of the Franks.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_John_IV_of_Alexandr.bio: John IV served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 569 and 579.
ev: The Visigoths under King Liuvigild invade the Suebian Kingdom (Northern Spain). Intermarriage between Goths and non-Goths is allowed in the Visigothic Kingdom.
Visigoths
During this tenure

alexandria:Eulogius_I_of_Alexandria.bio: Eulogius of Alexandria was Greek Patriarch of that see from about 580 to 608. He is regarded as a saint, with a feast day of June 13.
ev: Aj Ne' Yohl Mat becomes ruler (ajaw) of the Maya city of Palenque (Mexico). During his reign his kingdom is invaded by people from Calakmul.
Aj Ne' Yohl Mat
During this tenure, at about age 104

alexandria:Patriarch_Theodore_I_of_Alexa.bio: Theodore I, also known as Theodore Scribo, served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 607 and 609. Having been appointed by Phocas, he opposed the Heraclian revolt and was killed in the conflict.
ev: Byzantine–Persian War: King Khosrau II invades Armenia, and raids deep into Anatolia through the Byzantine provinces of Cappadocia, Phrygia, Galatia, and Bithynia.
Byzantine–Sassanid War of 602–628
During this tenure, at about age 58

alexandria:John_the_Merciful.bio: John V Eleemon, also known as John the Almsgiver, John the Almoner, John the Compassionate, or John the Merciful, was the Chalcedonian Patriarch of Alexandria from 606 to 616. He was born in Amathus around 560. Originally appointed by Emperor Heraclius, at the end of his life he was obliged to flee back to Cyprus, where he died around 620. He was unusual for his time in a number of ways. He was a married man with children, was elected bishop as a layman, and became a saint without being a martyr.
ev: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks: A khagan of the Western Turkic Khaganate is assassinated in a Chinese palace by Eastern Turkic rivals, with the approval of Emperor Gaozu of Tang.
During this tenure, at about age 69

alexandria:Patriarch_George_I_of_Alexand.bio: George I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 621 and 631, succeeding St. John the Almsgiver. A biography of St. John Chrysostom, reviewed by St. Photios in his Myriobiblos, has been attributed to him, as well as fragments on Psalm 2.
ev: Muhammad, Islamic unifies all nomadic tribes of the Arabian Peninsula, converts them to Islam and prepares an expedition against the Jews.
Muhammad
During this tenure

alexandria:Cyrus_of_Alexandria.bio: Cyrus of Alexandria was a prominent figure in the 7th century Byzantine Empire. He served as a Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria, as well as the de facto governor of Egypt. As governor, he heavily persecuted the Copts, and during the Arab conquest of Egypt, continually pushed for surrender and sabotaged the Byzantine military's defence of the country. Notably, he also played a significant role in the development of monothelitism. Cyrus died in Alexandria on March 21, 642.
ev: Gaza is conquered by the Muslim Arabs under 'Amr ibn al-'As. It becomes the first city in Palestine developed into a centre of Islamic law.
Gaza City
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Peter_IV_of_Alexand.bio: Peter IV served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria from 642 to 651. Following the Muslim conquest of Egypt, he sought refuge in Constantinople. In Constantinople he attended the Sixth Ecumenical Council for which he signed the council's records. Peter's departure from Alexandria initiated a period in Alexandria referred to as the Coadjutoration of the Patriarchal Throne, generally during which those bishops, as coadjutors, of the Church of Alexandria remained resident in Constantinople. This period lasted until Patriarch Cosmas I was enthroned in 727.
ev: Peroz III, son of Yazdegerd III, the last Sassanid king of Persia, flees to territory under the control of the Tang dynasty in China.
Peroz III
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Cosmas_I_of_Alexand.bio: Cosmas I or Kosmas I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between c. 727 and his death in 768. Cosmas was the first residential Chalcedonian (Melkite) patriarch to be established in Alexandria following the Muslim conquest of Egypt in the 640s. The see had remained vacant since, but Cosmas was appointed with the consent of both the Umayyad Caliph and the Byzantine Emperor.
ev: The oldest surviving printed document, a Buddhist scripture, is printed in Korea.
Buddhism
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Politianus_of_Alexa.bio: Politianus served partas Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 768 and 813. According to Eutychius, Politianus was a physician by training, visited Baghdad and healed Hārūn al-Rašīd's concubine. He reportedly participated in the translation of Vindonius Anatolius of Berytus' "Collection of Agricultural Practices" from Greek into Arabic for Yahya ibn Khalid in 795 CE.
ev: Emperor Charlemagne formally cedes Nordalbian territory to the pagan Obotrites (allies of the Carolingian Empire).
Charlemagne
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Eustatius_of_Alexan.bio: Eustatius served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 813 and 817.
ev: Louis the Pious, king of Aquitaine (and only surviving legitimate son), is crowned co-emperor of the Franks, with his father Charlemagne.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Christopher_I_of_Al.bio: Christopher I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 817 and 841.
ev: The House of Wisdom flourishes in Baghdad.
House of Wisdom
During this tenure, at about age 129

alexandria:Patriarch_Sophronius_I_of_Ale.bio: Sophronius I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 841 and 860.
ev: Viking chieftain Ubba winters in Milford Haven (Wales) with 23 ships.
Ubba
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Michael_I_of_Alexan.bio: Michael I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 860 and 870.
ev: Battle of Brissarthe: Frankish forces, led by Robert the Strong, are defeated by a joint Breton-Viking army.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Michael_II_of_Alexa.bio: Michael II served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 870 and 903.
ev: Treaty of Ribemont: Louis the Younger and the kings of the West Frankish Kingdom sign a treaty. The young Frankish monarch, Louis III, is reduced to merely Neustria.
During this tenure

alexandria:Christodoulos_(Greek_Orthodox.bio: Christodoulos served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 907 and 932.
ev: Orso II Participazio becomes the doge of Venice. He sends his son Pietro to Constantinople in order to re-establish the relationship with Alexander III.
Orso II Participazio
During this tenure, at about age 62

alexandria:Patriarch_Eutychius_of_Alexan.bio: Eutychius of Alexandria was the Melkite Patriarch of Alexandria. He is known for being one of the first Christian Egyptian writers to use the Arabic language. His writings include the chronicle Nazm al-Jawhar ("Row of Jewels"), also known by its Latin title Eutychii Annales ("The Annals of Eutychius").
ev: Battle of Bach Dang: Tĩnh Hải Quân forces under the rule of Ngô Quyền defeated an invading force of the Southern Han state at the Bach Dang River. This put an end to Chinese imperial domination in Vietnam after nearly 1,000 years.
Battle of Bach Dang (938)
During this tenure, at about age 61

alexandria:Patriarch_Sophronius_II_of_Al.bio: Sophronius II briefly served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria in 941.
ev: The famed Green Dome of the Palace of the Golden Gate at Baghdad collapses, amidst heavy rainfall.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Isaac_of_Alexandria.bio: Isaac served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 941 and 954.
ev: King Hugh of Provence lays siege to Vignola to put an end to Berengar's advance. But to no avail, as Berengar of Ivrea is hailed throughout northern Italy as a liberator, and Hugh flees to Provence.
Hugh of Italy
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Job_of_Alexandria.bio: Job served as Melkite Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 954 and 960.
ev: The Kingdom of Aksum is destroyed by Beta Israel invaders, under the leadership of Queen Gudit.
Kingdom of Aksum
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Elias_I_of_Alexandr.bio: Elias I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 963 and 1000 AD.
ev: Leif Erikson reaches North America.
Leif Erikson
During this tenure
Danish Viking raiders under Sweyn Forkbeard continue to ravage the cities (mostly poorly defended) in southern England. A famine strikes Sweyn's army, which has to live off the land.
Vikings
During this tenure

alexandria:Theophilus_II_(Greek_patriarc.bio: Theophilus served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1010 and 1020, during the persecution of the Christians under the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim.
ev: The fortified city of Fiesole in Italy is captured and destroyed by the people of nearby Florence.
Fiesole
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_George_II_of_Alexan.bio: George II served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1021 and 1052.
ev: Battle of Lemnos: Kievan Viking raiders sail through the straits at Abydos to the Aegean Sea. From there they make for the island of Lemnos, but are defeated by a Byzantine fleet of the Cibyrrhaeot Theme.
Battle of Lemnos (1024)
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Leontius_of_Alexand.bio: Leontius served as the Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1052 and 1059. He was succeeded by Alexander II (1059–1062) as the patriarch of Alexandria.
ev: The Seljuk Turks led by Sultan Tughril capture Baghdad and enter the city in a Roman-styled triumph. Al-Malik al-Rahim, the last Buyid emir in Iraq, is taken prisoner.
Seljuk Turks
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Alexander_II_of_Ale.bio: Alexander II served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1059 and 1062.
alexandria:Patriarch_Alexander_II_of_Ale.next: alexandria:name:John VI Kodonatos Eulogius II Coadjutor?:1062
alexandria:Patriarch_Alexander_II_of_Ale.nn: John VI Kodonatos Eulogius II Coadjutor?
ev: The compilation of the New Book of Tang is completed, under a team of scholars led by Ouyang Xiu.
New Book of Tang
During this tenure

alexandria:name:John VI Kodonatos Eulogi.n: John VI Kodonatos Eulogius II Coadjutor?
ev: Siege of Exeter: Norman forces under King William I (the Conqueror) take the city of Exeter after a siege of 18-days.
Siege of Exeter (1068)
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Cyril_II_of_Alexand.bio: Cyril II served as Greek Orthodox Patriarchs of Alexandria in the 12th century.
alexandria:Patriarch_Cyril_II_of_Alexand.prev: alexandria:name:John VI Kodonatos Eulogius II Coadjutor?:1062
alexandria:Patriarch_Cyril_II_of_Alexand.pn: John VI Kodonatos Eulogius II Coadjutor?
ev: A Genoese fleet leaves Italy to support the Crusaders' efforts to conquer the coastal cities; the ships reach Latakia on September 25.
During this tenure
The magnetic compass is first used for maritime navigation purposes during the Song dynasty in China.
History of the compass
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Sophronius_III_of_A.bio: Sophronius III served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1137 and 1171. In 1161, he was in Constantinople to attend the wedding of Emperor Manuel I Komnenos and Maria of Antioch. He may also be the patriarch who Theodore Balsamon says was pressured to replace the Liturgy of Saint Mark, native to Egypt, with the Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom, favoured by Constantinople. A copy of the chrism liturgy from Sophronius' pontificate is preserved on a scroll from Saint Catherine's Monastery (Sinai Greek NF/E 55).
ev: In Japan, the Heiji Rebellion began with the siege of the Sanjō Palace.
Heiji Rebellion
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Elias_II_of_Alexand.bio: Elias II served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1171 and 1175.
ev: The establishment of the Sultanate of Egypt, Saladin proclaimed the Sultan.
Sultan of Egypt
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Eleutherius_of_Alex.bio: Eleutherius served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1175 and 1180.
ev: The union of Egypt and Syria under Sultan Saladin Yusuf ibn Ayyub, the foundation of the Ayyubid Sultanate.
Saladin
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Mark_III_of_Alexand.bio: Mark III served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1180 and 1209.
ev: The Yōwa era, marked by famine, ends during the reign of Emperor Antoku in Japan.
Yōwa
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Nicholas_I_of_Alexa.bio: Patriarch Nicholas I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1210 and 1243.
ev: Battle of Grobnik Field: Croatian forces under Béla IV stop the Mongol invasion in Hungary and Croatia. Béla rebuilds the country and orders the building of fortifications through his kingdom.
Battle of Grobnik Field
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Gregory_I_of_Alexan.bio: Gregory I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1243 and 1263.
ev: The first usage is made of the English word "cuckold", according to the Oxford English Dictionary.
cuckold
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Nicholas_II_of_Alex.bio: Nicholas II was Greek Patriarch of Alexandria. Before his ordination, he had been the Ambassador of the Sultan of Egypt in Constantinople.
ev: Treaty of Montgomery: King Henry III of England acknowledges Llywelyn ap Gruffudd's title of Prince of Wales.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Athanasius_III_of_A.bio: Athanasius III served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1276 and 1308.
ev: King Edward I summons the English Parliament for the first time in more than two years.
During this tenure, at about age 54

alexandria:Patriarch_Gregory_II_of_Alexa.bio: Gregory II served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1316 and 1354.
ev: Italian author Dante Alighieri, known for The Inferno, dies of malaria at Ravenna after having undertaken a diplomatic mission in the Republic of Venice.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Gregory_III_of_Alex.bio: Gregory III served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1354 and 1366.
ev: The Chancellor of England for the first time opens Parliament with a speech in English. Under Edward III, the Pleading in English Act makes English rather than Law French the official language in English law courts.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Niphon_of_Alexandri.bio: Niphon served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1366 and 1385.
ev: Hundred Years' War: The English, weakened by the plague, lose so much ground to the French that they agree to sign the Treaty of Bruges, leaving them with only the coastal towns of Calais, Bordeaux and Bayonne.
During this tenure, at about age 25

alexandria:Patriarch_Mark_IV_of_Alexandr.bio: Mark IV served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1385 and 1389.
ev: Mircea I of Wallachia and Polish king Władysław II Jagiełło sign their first treaty, to protect their countries against Ottoman expansion.
Mircea I of Wallachia
During this tenure
Penistone Grammar School, later to be one of the first community comprehensive schools in England, is founded near Barnsley, England.
Penistone Grammar School
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Gregory_IV_of_Alexa.bio: Gregory IV served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1398 and 1412.
ev: (13th day of 5th month Ōei 8) The shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu dispatches a mission to Ming Dynasty China as the first step of opening trade between the two nations.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Nicholas_IV_of_Alex.bio: Nicholas IV served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1412 and 1417.
ev: The English defeat the French at Agincourt.
Battle of Agincourt
During this tenure, at about age 15

alexandria:Patriarch_Athanasius_IV_of_Al.bio: Athanasius IV served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1417 and 1425.
ev: The interment of Ming dynasty China's Yongle Emperor, who died on August 12, takes place at the Chang Mausoleum in Beijing's Ming tombs.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Mark_V_of_Alexandri.bio: Mark V served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1425 and 1435.
ev: The Ottoman Empire, led by the Sultan Murad II, captures Thessalonica in Greece after an eight-year siege.
During this tenure

alexandria:Philotheos_(Greek_patriarch_o.bio: Philotheus served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1435 and 1459.
ev: The treaty between the Republic of Venice and the Byzantine Empire is renewed for five years in a signing at Constantinople.
During this tenure
The Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II conquers the Greek island of Lesbos after a 14-day attack by sea and by land with over 20,000 troops, capturing the last fortress in the siege of Mytilene.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Gregory_V_of_Alexan.bio: Gregory V served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria for two years, between 1484 and 1486.
ev: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola returns to Florence, and writes Oration on the Dignity of Man.
Giovanni Pico della Mirandola
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Joachim_of_Alexandr.bio: Joachim served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1486 and 1567.
ev: King Henry VII of England signs the commercial treaty Intercursus Magnus with Venice, Florence, and the cities of the Hanseatic League and the Netherlands.
During this tenure, at about age 48

alexandria:Patriarch_Silvester_of_Alexan.bio: Silvester served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1569 and 1590.
ev: The 3rd Parliament of Elizabeth I, with 438 members, assembles in England at Westminster after being summoned on February 17.
3rd Parliament of Elizabeth I
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Meletius_I_of_Alexa.bio: Meletius I of Constantinople served as patriarch of Alexandria between 1590 and 1601. Simultaneously from 1597 to 1598 he served also as locum tenens of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He is honoured as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church, with his feast day held on 13 September.
ev: Siege of Pyongyang: A Japanese invasion is defeated in Pyongyang by a combined force of Korean and Ming troops.
During this tenure, at about age 44

alexandria:Cyril_Lucaris.bio: Cyril I of Constantinople (Cyril Lucaris or Kyrillos Loukaris was a Greek prelate and theologian, and a native of Heraklion, Crete. He later became the Greek Patriarch of Alexandria as Cyril III and Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as Cyril I. He has been said to have attempted a reform of the Eastern Orthodox Church along Calvinist Protestant lines. Attempts to bring Calvinism into the Orthodox Church were rejected, and Cyril I's actions, motivations, and specific viewpoints remain a matter of debate among scholars.
ev: August (approx.) – Possible first performance of William Shakespeare's tragedy Macbeth in London.
During this tenure, at about age 34

alexandria:Patriarch_Gerasimus_I_of_Alex.bio: Gerasimus I served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1620 and 1636.
ev: Fire engines are used for the first time in England in order to control and extinguish a fire that breaks out at London Bridge, but not before 43 houses are destroyed.
England
During this tenure, at about age 73

alexandria:Patriarch_Metrophanes_of_Alex.bio: Metrophanes Kritopoulos, sometimes Critopoulos, Critopoulus, Kritopulus was a Greek monk and theologian who served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1636 and 1639.
ev: The first printing press in British North America is started in Cambridge, Massachusetts, by Stephen Daye.
During this tenure, at about age 50

alexandria:Patriarch_Nicephorus_of_Alexa.bio: Nicephorus served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1639 and 1645.
ev: The first professional book publisher to use printing press in Norway is established in Oslo.
printing press
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Joannicius_of_Alexa.bio: Joannicius served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1645 and 1657.
ev: The Dutch artist Rembrandt produces the works Rembrandt drawing at a window and Beggars at the Door.
Rembrandt
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Paisius_of_Alexandr.bio: Paisius Ligarides, born Pantaleon Ligarides was a Greek Orthodox scholar, Metropolitan of Gaza. Born in Chios, he taught literature and theology in the Greek college in Rome established in 1577 by Pope Gregory XIII. He was at first supportive of reconciliation of Orthodox with Catholic theology, but later returned to Greek Orthodoxy and wrote against both Catholicism and Calvinism. Leaving Rome, he went to Constantinople, and later (1646) to Târgoviște in Wallachia where he established (or revived) a Greek school.
ev: The Ottoman Empire declares war on Poland.
During this tenure, at about age 61

alexandria:Patriarch_Parthenius_I_of_Ale.bio: Parthenius I served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1678 and 1688. Prior to being the Patriarch, he served as Metropolitan of Nazareth. He suffered a serious injury in an earthquake in 1688 and died later that year in Smyrna, in Asia Minor.
ev: Morean War: The Republic of Venice captures the fortress town of Preveza from the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure, at about age 34

alexandria:Patriarch_Gerasimus_II_of_Ale.bio: Gerasimos II Palladas served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1688 and 1710. He is honoured as a saint of the Eastern Orthodox Church and is commemorated annually on 16 January.
ev: Hearing that William of Orange has landed in England, Louis XIV declares war on the Netherlands.
During this tenure, at about age 55

alexandria:Patriarch_Samuel_of_Alexandri.bio: Samuel served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria in 1710–1712 and in 1714–1723. Pope Clement XI sent the Franciscan Lorenzo Cozza (later Cardinal) to Samuel in 1703 with the hope that the Patriarch might conclude union with Rome. He in fact signed a declaration of his renunciation of Orthodoxy, and his embrace of Catholicism ten years later was conveyed to the Pope in consistory on 28 April 1713.
ev: Rinaldo by George Frideric Handel, the first Italian opera written for the London stage, premieres at the Queen's Theatre, Haymarket.
Rinaldo (opera)
During this tenure, at about age 50
Newcomen builds the first practical steam engine.
Newcomen atmospheric engine
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Cosmas_III_of_Alexa.bio: Cosmas III served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1737 and 1746.
ev: Austria enters the Russo-Turkish War as an ally of Russia against the Ottoman Empire.
During this tenure

alexandria:Patriarch_Matthew_of_Alexandr.bio: Matthew Psaltis served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1746 and 1766. He was born in the Greek island of Andros.
ev: French and Indian War – Battle of Fort Necessity: George Washington surrenders Fort Necessity to French Capt. Louis Coulon de Villiers, the only surrender in Washington's military career.
During this tenure, at about age 54

alexandria:Patriarch_Cyprian_of_Alexandr.bio: Cyprian, formerly a Cypriot deacon, served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1766 and 1783.
ev: American Revolutionary War: The last British troops leave New York City and George Washington triumphantly returns, three months after the signing of the Treaty of Paris.
During this tenure, at about age 60

alexandria:Patriarch_Gerasimus_III_of_Al.bio: Gerasimus III served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1783 and 1788.
ev: Mozart's Great Mass is first performed, in Salzburg, Austria.
During this tenure, at about age 33

alexandria:Patriarch_Parthenius_II_of_Al.bio: Parthenius II Pankostas served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1788 and 1805.
ev: The Treaty of Tripoli, a peace treaty between the United States and Ottoman Tripolitania, is signed at Algiers.
During this tenure, at about age 62

alexandria:Patriarch_Theophilus_III_of_A.bio: Theophilus III or Pope Theophilus Pankostas, was Pope and Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria and All Africa between 1805 and 1825. He was a native of Patmos and the grandson of Patriarch Parthenios II, whom he succeeded on the throne of Alexandria. He supported the immigration of Greeks to Egypt, with the approval of the reformer Mohammed Ali. In 1818 he fell ill and retired to the island of Patmos to recover; there he was initiated into the Filikí Eteria.
ev: War of the Sixth Coalition – Battle of Berry-au-Bac: French cavalrymen led by Napoleon defeat Cossacks under Ferdinand von Wintzingerode.
During this tenure, at about age 50

alexandria:Patriarch_Hierotheus_I_of_Ale.bio: Hierotheus I of Alexandria served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1825 and 1845. Hierotheus I was an Aromanian. He was from Klinovos (now Kleino; Aromanian: Clinova).
ev: The London Protocol establishes the full independence and sovereignty of Greece from the Ottoman Empire, as the result of the Greek War of Independence.
During this tenure, at about age 80

alexandria:Patriarch_Artemius_of_Alexand.bio: Artemius served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1845 and 1847.
ev: The Milan–Venice railway's bridge, over the Venetian Lagoon between Mestre and Venice in Italy, opens, the world's longest since 1151.
During this tenure, at about age 71

alexandria:Patriarch_Hierotheus_II_of_Al.bio: Hierotheus II served as Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria between 1847 and 1858. He was born in Sifnos.
ev: Queen Victoria institutes the Victoria Cross as a British military decoration.
Queen Victoria
During this tenure, at about age 106

alexandria:Patriarch_Callinicus_of_Alexa.bio: Callinicus served as the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria from 14 March 1858 until his resignation on 24 May 1861. He was born in Skotina, Pieria in 1800. Callinicus died in Mytilene on 12 July 1889.
ev: Napoleon III, Emperor of the French, and Empress Eugénie visit Algiers and stay at the Casbah of Algiers.
Napoleon III
During this tenure, at about age 60

alexandria:Patriarch_Jacob_of_Alexandria.bio: Jacob served as Greek Patriarch of Alexandria between 1861 and 1865.
